 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Katamari_on_the_Rocks_-_Katamari_Damacy_REROLL;;;The rip is an homage to the rips "Katamari on the Rocks - Katamari Damacy" and "Lost Woods (Complete Version) - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time". Similar to the aforementioned rips, it is a dense mashup medley using various sources, with this rip being comprised almost entirely of channel memes that became popular after the latter rip. This rip also incorporates various arranged instrumentals.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/The_Number_314_-_Gamedec;;;At 0:08, "e (Euler's Number)" fades in over the advertised track, with every letter in the advertised game's logo except the first "E" slowly disappearing as this happens. At 0:25, "e (Euler's Number)" is simultaneously pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track as James Grimes' head fades in over the character's head in the thumbnail. At 0:50, the visuals zoom closer to Jay Grimes' head, with the "E" moving to the left. At the same time, "Smooth" and the instrumental of "Mega Man" play, referencing "Main Theme - e" and "Main Theme (Alternate) - e", with them getting bass-boosted at 0:53. At 0:54, the visuals flash and transition into the thumbnail for the original "e (Euler's Number)" video. The overall joke is likely based on The numberphile's return after the rip "News of Jay's Death - The Ignition Factor" and him being absent from the thumbnail of e in "The Problem - e" and "The Solution - e". Additionally, this rip was uploaded on March 14 (3/14), as a play on the advertised track's title.      A frame from the rip.        Another frame from the rip.        Yet another frame from the rip.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/News_of_Jay's_Death_-_The_Ignition_Factor;;;This rip continues the "e∩Ω" story arc, taking place after "It's time for a feast...". The rip's title references Jay Eazy, and in turn the events of "Golden Ratio - e". At the start, the screen moves from the game's thumbnail to the inside of Hell. An "e" portal opens and both Gegagedigedagedago and the roasted chicken from "Gegagedigedagedago 5" by Gchmch step out of it. From 0:08 to 0:37, the advertised track's melody is mashed up with the vocals of @raizoff's "Cotton Eye Joe" cover while Gegagedigedagedago and the Roasted Chicken character traverse the depths of Hell. Additionally, several characters and references to other rips make cameo appearances during this trip:  Jerry from Undertale can be seen at 0:10-0:11 From 0:12 to 0:18, both CraftyCorn from Poppy Playtime and a Young Sheldon / Walter White edit, which references the "Young Sheldon Ending" meme, appear in the backgroud. Between 0:19 and 0:24, the Josh Hutcherson / Omega Nugget edit, circular chain, Last Bible III logo and "AI Rick Laughing" videos from "Senatus - Last Bible III" can be seen at the top of the screen. Jack-in-the-Box Zombie from Plants vs. Zombies appears in the background between 0:25 and 0:31. Gegagedigedagedago eventually reaches a large hole at 0:38 as the background music stops. Gegagedigedagedago pulls out an "e" tile, which first appeared in "Gameplay - 2048", and punctures a hole in it with his knife featuring a ROBLOX Man-Face, which first appeared in "Tsurupettan (Beta Mix) - Umineko no Naku Koro ni". This leads to the simple continued fraction form of "e" bursting out of the tile, creating a staircase that Gegagedigedagedago and the Roasted Chicken character use to slide down the hole. At the bottom of the hole, the rip "The Infinite Hole - The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe" plays, as they come across The numberphile's ghost, who greets them with the "Hey" lyric from "Mega Man". Gegagegedigedagedago nods to The numberphile and exchanges a handshake, with the latter walking up to the fraction staircase. The numberphile touches the staircase, which causes it to move towards The numberphile. The infinite staircase collides with him, which causing him to glow white before being fully revived. The numberphile thanks the duo for reviving him, and drops another "e" tile for them, before jumping away. The Roasted Turkey grabs the "e" tile and throws it to open a portal as the fart sound associated with Brainless Kitty plays. The rip ends with Gegagedigedagedago and the Roasted Chicken entering the portal as the screen becomes black.

At 5:56, the thumbnail fades out, followed by the logoswap at 6:06. The "bigfoot creature" and "circus feature" in the spoof lyrics refer to two characters in Sam & Max Hit the Road – Bruno the Bigfoot and Trixie the Giraffe-Necked Girl from Scranton – whom Bumpus has kidnapped and forced to play in his backing band.     https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_(A_Lil'_Bigger_Mix)_-_Five_Nights_at_Freddy's;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Like all other "Main Theme" rips from the Five Nights at Freddy's series, this rip uses "Five Nights at Freddy's 1 Song" instead of the actual "Main Theme" track. This is an arrangement of "Step Yo Game Up" by Snoop Dogg ft. Trina & Lil Jon using the instruments of "Five Nights at Freddy's 1 Song", with the original vocals of "Step Yo Game Up" included, specifically Trina's verse of the song. At 0:47, Snoop Dogg and Lil Jon's chorus of the song plays, with Lil Jon's "step yo game up" lyrics replicated using sentence mixed vocals from "Five Nights at Freddy's 1 Song". At 1:23, Lil Jon's verse of "Step Yo Game Up" starts, with the visuals changing to the music video for "Step Yo Game Up" and various Five Nights at Freddy's animations shown over the security camera screen from the advertised game. At 2:01, the visual switch back to the thumbnail, with the mashup returning to the 0:47 portion.

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Dudley_Stage_-YOU_BLOW_MY_MIND-_(Arcade_Distribution)_-_Street_Fighter_III:_Third_Strike;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This rip is part of a series of fakeout rips that start out the same as existing BotanicSage mashups before veering off into different directions, and which list BotanicSage as a composer. However in this case, the rip is based on a BotanicSage mashup that uses a different version of the advertised track. The advertised track is mashed up with "Burning Desires" from Zenless Zone Zero and "Gangnam Style", referencing "Theme of Dudley -SSFIV Arrange- - Ultra Street Fighter IV", which itself references "Oppa Dudley Style (PSY vs Capcom)" by BotanicSage, a mashup of "Theme of Dudley -SSFIV Arrange-" and "Gangnam Style", and various mashups made of "Burning Desires" and "Gangnam Style" due to how similar they are. At 0:14 and throughout, an unknown sound effect plays. At 0:15, the rip switches to only "Burning Desires" being mashed up with the advertised track. At 0:46 and 1:45, a different unknown sound effect plays in place of the "3, 2, 1, fire!" lyric of "Burning Desires".

At 0:40, "The Mine Song" vocals return at the start of the second loop. At 1:16, the remix stops, as it plays Eric saying "P-E-N-I-S, I'm on the RedBull Network", followed by Stingy saying "That's what I said" from "The Mine Song", and then back to Eric saying "I'm on the RedBull Network".

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/The_First_Date_-_A_Date_with_Boykisser!;;;There doesn't exist a track named "The First Date" in A Date with Boykisser!. Instead, this rip is fake gameplay of a fake visual novel-style "Choose Your Own Adventure" game focus on Boykisser. The rip starts with the player arriving at the fancy restaurant, and attends to the waitress - being the cat Ethel, associated with the "oo ee a e a" meme - for a front desk reservation. The waitress then guides the player to the table, while "U ii a io ui ii a io #keşfetolmaduası🤲📿🧕" by @krexarpect plays when "walk-spin", and lets the player sit there patiently while wait for their date to arrive. Not too long after, Boykisser arrives for the date, saying that he was late due to "got too caught up at home", in which the player calms him down to not worry about it, and just had arrived at the right time. Boykisser says to be his first time on a date, and feeling a bit nervous, specially for "being around with a cute boy like the player". The player blushes, resulting into Boykisser flirting with him for a bit, and later, he asks for the player if wanted to know anything about himself, in which the player asks for what kind-of music he likes. Boykisser responds to like the "Silly Music" genre that makes him go "chipi chapa" around. The player doesn't understand what he meant, but find his quirkiness kind-of charming, and then talks about their personal music taste too, in which Boykisser afirms to not heard about those genres due to not being well versed into it, and promises to give it a go in some time. The waitress Ethel comes by to see if they're ready to order anything, in which the player asks for Boykisser what he wants, and happy responds salmon, in which makes the player and Ethel a little startled and confused by the sudden outbust respond, in which Boykisser says sorry for it, and saying that he was just hungry and likes to eat fish. Ethel then writes down the orders and goes heads to the kitchen, while the player was a little confuse and ask for what happen in there. Boykisser responds that he cant help but be really excited, as since he responds for him ""being a silly cat". Leaving the situation aside, the player asks if he knows or hangs around with other felines, in which Boykisser responds excitelly that does, saying that he's friends with Kapi - PaperKitty's character and main opponent in the Friday Night Funkin' mod, VS. KAPI - Arcade Showdown - and mentions that usually hang out at the arcade together, and even invites the player in case want to join in if it's into playing games. After this, Boykisser mentions to be friends with Eek! The Cat, in which by coincidence, mentions that both shares the same favorite song. Boykisser then says that he has non-feline friends as well, mentioning two characters that are best friends with him: Pomni from The Amazing Digital Circus and Gegagedigedagedago, with both images of them appearing in transparent on the left. Boykisser says that the player likely knows them, saying that "they're pretty famous around here", and admit saying that didn't been places as such because of them, and saying that Gegagedigedagedago gets really awkward, and Pomni is usually pretty timid and confused, but saying that they're really kind people when get to know them more. Player recalls to know Gegagedigedagedago, as mentioning that "he's a well known hero around these parts", while also heard about Pomni, questioning if was the girl that "randomly showed up one day". Boykisser then continues mentioning having a roommate fox called Lyan - Mauzymice's boyfriend character - in which mentions being confused with himself. The waitress Ethel comes with the food (a salmon with ROBLOX Man Face attached into it) and drinks that has been ordered, and she asks if wanted anything else. The player responds no, but when tried to ask with Boykisser, he quickly eats the sushi, and decides to request for more salmons in excitement. The player notices it and hopes that somehow Boykisser pays for the foods, as since themselves can't afford it. Ethan then goes on the kitchen and comes back to give more salmon to Boykisser,  which he eats all in one bite while Loud Nigra's scream plays follow by the Heavy's "nom" sound from Team Fortress 2.  In excitement, Boykisser asks for more before player decides to calm him down and convince him that he's getting too much. Boykisser apologies in advance, saying that he got "a little carried away" and that he "was in a trance". He quickly thanks the player to avoid to picking up as since he doesn't know to control himself when comes to fish food, in which the player tell them to no need and that they understand, and asks if he'd like to split the payment check, in which Boykisser says to not need, as since he got money for his portion, and says in regards to picking up more fish later, in which the player mentions that he can't guarantee for more fish about it. After this, the player asks if Boykisser wanted to go for somewhere else for the rest of the night, in which he accepts, but depends over the transportation that they're gonna take, as since he didn't brought a car. He asks if the player wanted to call a taxi, or wanted to walk together, follow by two carded videos to choose: "Taxi to the City - A Date with Boykisser!" and "Peaceful Walk in the Park - A Date with Boykisser!". The rip ends afterwards.  References[] Throughout from the entire rip, a single song plays in the background, being "It's Raining Somewhere Else (Alpha Mix) - Undertale". Boykisser's voice sounds are taken from dewperland's Boykisser voice-over videos, while the images of his are taken from artworks associated with Boykisser, being by first appearances:    Time  Image  Source   0:33  "butterflies in my stomach"  @DarkKolaa   0:57  "It’s just a small crush"   1:04  "Meow"  @mauzymice   1:14  "blep"  @aarelthings   Few other minor things is also referenced:  Boykisser mentioning that the "Silly Music" genre makes him "chipi chapa" around is a reference to the lyrics of "Dubidubidu" by Christell, and by extension, references the video "Сhipi Сhipi Chapa Chapa (But it's boyKisser - FULL)" by Kuowom; Boykisser mentioning sharing a favorite song with Eek! The Cat references to "The Penis (Eek!)", as well the usage of the track under the Eek! The Cat rips; Boykisser being friends with Gegagedigedagedago and Pomni reference "Boykisser, Pomni, & Gegagedigedagedago but it's Famous Console Startups"; Mentions of Gegagedigedagedago being a hero references the e∩Ω story arc; The mentions of Pomni "showing up in one day" it's a likely parallel to the events of The Amazing Digital Circus episode, "PILOT"; The mentions of Boykisser's roommate, Lyan, being confused to him is a reference to the amount of usage of Mauzymice's Lyan animations for Boykisser memes, despite both Silly Cat and Lyan being different person; The usage of the "Cat" sound from Mario Paint by 3:33 references to "Boykisser" by Studi01.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_-_Poker_Night_at_the_Inventory;;;This is an original live-action skit created by several rippers during Super MAGFest 2025. It depicts a tournament of a poker-like card game, played mostly with flash cards. The skit begins with Franklin and his friend Carl John Smith IV entering a hotel room where the tournament is held, in which there are several people excitedly betting on the ongoing match. Mark, a highly skilled poker player, defeats Bartholomew, and is slated to face Gork in the final match of the tournament. Carl and Franklin watch the match eagerly, although Franklin's inexperience with the game's rules causes him a lot of confusion. Mark begins the match by playing the "splash", "drink", and "frog" cards as his first hand, followed by playing a "snail" card. Gork then plays a "swim" card, which Mark counters by flipping his "snail" card, causing Gork to shout angrily in disbelief. As the spectators comprehend the sudden twist of events, Gork makes a plea to the Dealer to rig the game in his favor, which Dealer refuses. As the game continues, Mark, now overconfident from his imminent victory, taunts at Gork to forfeit the match. Gork responds to Mark's mockery by mentioning that him losing the game would result in his family's death, which Mark bluntly rebuffs by playing a "fish" card. Seeing that Franklin is struggling to follow the game's events, Carl attempts to explain to him Mark's strategies up to that point. Unfortunately, his detailed explanations only serve to further overwhelm and confuse Franklin. With the match nearing its conclusion, Gork is projected to lose the tournament to Mark. In the face of this, Gork appears to forfeit the match, tearfully walking away from Mark. However, just as Dealer is about to call the match in Mark's favor, Gork suddenly retaliates with a "THE LITERAL ROCK", with all the spectators looking on in awe. With this new revelation, Gork is declared the winner of the tournament, with all of his spectators cheering for his victory. As Carl and Franklin leave the hotel room, Franklin, utterly bewildered, questions Carl about the events that he witnessed.

As per the initial thumbnail and title, the rip begins in the style of a start of a fusion collab, with the advertised track playing set to various footage of Minecraft including the sun rising up as the first shot and with animals moving around in some of the following shots. At 0:08, the rip is interrupted by a skit parody of a AdamzoneTopMarks video on Minecraft News, this one being about the "new" Alpha v0.2.9 of Minecraft. The skit also uses a similar map used in The Susie ARG version of "Minecraft with Gadget" by The Joke-Explainer™ 7000, including making several references to bits of said video, such as pieces related to steps of the "FOOLS" branch of the ARG. The skit begins with GameChap and BertieChap in their house with a maid from the "Little Maid Mod" Minecraft mod that are used in several of AdamzoneTopMarks's videos, as they do the usual style of introduction they both do in their videos. The two explain that this video will be about exploring Alpha v0.2.9 of Minecraft, with Notch giving them the patch notes out of the house. The city's empty, green for a week, and it doesn't look like new shipments are on the way.  The sky is green and later it turns red.  My poop disaster is playing havoc with the power grid and the weather's cold.  In other words, I guess that means CCC isn't coming this year.  I'm not sure what I'll be looking for out there, but maybe I'm just holding on to the foolish hope that some places aren't green.  When the news still worked, I turned that shit off, cause that's boring as hell, I'm not gonna lie.  I ain't listening to all that, so I'm walking for a bit.  The only thing left is to walk.   The two decide to turn it off after finding it uninteresting and hating it. Going down the other staircase, they then come across a room where the path seems to end to a black void. GameChap then claims to see someone during this. Across the void is another door that doesn't have a button, leaving the room with no choice but to find a button. They then go back to the chapel, but not before stopping at another picture of Nostalgia Critic and Inspector Gadget fighting. GameChap attempts to enter a room, however only turns back, due to being a room they already went through. At 3:29:15, they come across the room they saw during the looping "APPROACHING THE TERMINAL 150m AHEAD" with all the gold still there, only for Israphel to take them all, however they don't react much to him this time compared to previous times.  Crossing several crafting table rows and heading up to an upper section, they head down a hallway with an armor stand in front that leads to a cooperative puzzle section, with Herobrine briefly appearing right as they enter. After solving the simple puzzle, they feel rejuvenated as they are walking through a long hallway, ending with an armor stand with a grey helmet on. The hallway ends at a dark room with only a house from earlier in it. As they approach, they notice there is only a cake inside, though see the only way to open the doors is if both stand on pressure plates. Once inside they notice a button the back that activates TNT that forms a hole. Falling down, BertieChap manages to find a button after the fall and they start heading back, but not before panicking due to seeing clouds in the "ARENA".  After some wandering around, including figuring out which direction to go, revisiting the door with sunlight at the end, going around some stairwells to the furnace room, and seeing where the "BUTTONS" door lead to, they find the door and enter it. They then head up a stairwell that leads to a sign reading "GOOGLE DRIVE ROOM <---". The room only contains a Google Drive link that they read out "1EPgHJoxDZpFxTEfI66M901qEiuReQKpr". During this, they panic whenever the "E" is read, one of the "6"s uses the red version of glowstone, and are fine around "e", making reference to "e (Euler's Number)" during this. At the end of the room, two signs above exit are shown reading "______________/______________/_____________/__?" and "Thank you for visiting!". They then assume the letters and numbers they read can be used as a link to fill out the blank sign. Exiting that room, they come across a room that houses more pictures with Inspector Gadget, "Like the Haltmann Works Company" one, several melons and pumpkins near the ceiling on either side, and two buttons on diamond blocks with signs above them reading "OPEN DOOR" and "CLOSE DOOR", the former also having another sign near it reading "gamechap press this button > not the other one".  BertieChap then tells GameChap to check out a similar white room with the "NEVER HAD SEX" signs, this time with them changed to read "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/". They then decide to leave, though there is no button nearby to exit, only for BertieChap to break the door instead to leave. They then realize the melons have disappeared, leaving only a sign saying "my melons now :)", though the pumpkins remain. After pressing the left button, GameChap wonders how the sign knows his name, believing it to just be the mayor. As they approach the corner, they are teleported back to the "gaget" section from earlier. GameChap and BertieChap decide to go to the door with sunlight at the end, seeing that as the true ending. During the walk to the door, they notice a walled off section with an item frame with a brick on it.  After a bit of wandering around to find the "ARENA", at 3:43:43, they finally reach the door and make their way through both doors. Once they fully exit, the two notice they are instead surrounded by a large wheat field, with the pyramid they exited instead being replaced by a small structure, similar to the ending of Portal 2. Turning around, they see that both Ogg and Notch are there as well, as they all celebrate, including stomping on the wheat. Ogg then starts throwing poop around, similar to the "poop disaster" from earlier, before placing a Noaka block from earlier down, puzzling GameChap and BertieChap.  At 3:45:25, TNT then goes off, as BertieChap then blows up the place, referencing the endings of AdamzoneTopMarks videos that usually have something blowing up by BertieChap, usually with GameChap blaming BertieChap for it, killing GameChap in the process, though BertieChap claims to not be responsible. He then respawns back in the pyramid in one of the rooms in the corridor along with Notch and BertieChap, before giving chase to BertieChap while swinging his gold sword, also referencing the usually endings of AdamzoneTopMarks videos. At 3:46:06, GameChap then does the sign off he does in his videos, right before the rip fades out. BertieChap ends it with saying "Mr. Mayor's gonna be quite mad for what we've done.", another reference to the usual endings of AdamzoneTopMarks videos.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/PlayStation_Startup_()_-_Console%2FBIOS_Music;;;This is based on Hitogata, an urban legend about a Japanese train safety PSA. The rip starts with the PlayStation startup that is edited to appear to be playing on a TV that also gets cutoff before it fully ends. At 0:18, a disclaimer in Japanese appears, warning about the software still being in development and issues with disk may occur. At 0:26, the game in question is shown to be the PlayStation port of Densha de GO! with the games opening cutscene and title screen shown. At 0:55, the player tries to select a train, however three of the options are shown to still be under development, leaving the top left one as the only option. After viewing the regular instructions about how to play the game, gameplay proceeds normally at first, with the player exiting the first station and heading to the next station. At 3:02, the player applies the brakes too late, causing them to miss the platform and lose all their bonus time. As in the real game, a red train icon reading "Time is up" appears. At 3:26, gameplay restarts but begins to deviate heavily; almost all of the HUD elements are corrupted except for the speedometer, which constantly switches between 0km/h and 130km/h, the sky is pitch black, and the tracks are completely straight. As well, there is almost nothing else surrounding the track, with only the ground, telegraph poles, a couple of houses, and station platforms present. The ground is also shown to be disappearing right as it passes the screen on the lower half. At 4:45, the player approaches the station, where a person is present on the track. At 4:50, the train collides with the person, the screen goes black, a crashing sound is heard, and the train icon has blood splatter added over it. At 4:55, the distance of the train stopping is shown with it stopping right at the accident, blood surrounding the crash, and no other HUD elements appearing. At 5:01, the "Time is up" screen appears again, followed by the game over screen. At 5:12, a recreation of Hitogata is shown with the background consisting of a train station, with the text shown changed to "パスト/ザー/デヅレー/フャー/ウンダースタンディング" (which roughly translates to "Past the desire for understanding"). At 5:40, an "ADDRESS ERROR" screen is shown before the rip ends.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/A_History_of_Boxing_-_Frog_Fractions;;;The commentary in the advertised track is replaced with the entirety of the commentary from "Car Doors of Time ~ Side Story - Mr Rental: The Video Game". The background music is extended to be able to fit the length of the commentary.     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Car_Doors_of_Time_~_Side_Story_-_Mr_Rental:_The_Video_Game;;;Similar to "Behind the Scenes - Mr Rental: The Video Game", this rip is a lore explanation video narrated by JoeBro, explaining the full story of the PAINT Branch of The Susie ARG.   2B and 9S[] After the events of NieR: Automata's true ending, 2B and 9S live happily ever after in their home dimension. Elsewhere, The Voice Inside Your Head decides to summon 2B using the Figment Transportation Device, planning on making her watch Haltmann and keep him in line. only for a Garlic Taco portal to appear. As 2B is about to be sucked in, 9S jumps in the way, falling into the portal and landing in the Central Canon Continuum. He lands in SiIva's house and is apprehended by The Voice's troops. Despite the setback, The Voice recruits 9S anyway, assuming the latter had hacked the Figment Transportation Device to summon himself in 2B's place. In secret, 9S tries to reverse the Figment Transportation Device's programming to send him home, only to be caught. He launches the undercooked program, causing the device to malfunction and send him to Mundus from Skyrim. Elsewhere, 2B is picked by Eggnog and sent to the Microsoft Paint universe. He instructs 2B to find the Crappily Drawn Car and never stop driving it. This leads into 2B's cameo appearance in "Opening Scene - Waluigi's Tacostand", which happens during Mr. Rent's flashback to Mr. Own at The Fucking Store, as well as "Story Mode - Mr Rental: The Video Game" and "Story Mode - Looney Tunes", which reuse the NBG's initial concepts of the car being able to travel between both worlds, with the addition of it being able to travel back 1 minute into the past when it swaps universes. 2B steals Mr. Own's car, rams into him, sending them both to the Looney Tunes universe. 2B loses the car, and steals Mr. Rental's, running him over and sending them both back to the Microsoft Paint universe. 2B loses the car, and the loop repeats until the multiverse redirects 2B to the CCC to avoid a paradox. Both cars merge into one, becoming a Figment and losing its power. This leads to the events of "The Life and Times of Wade L.D. - A SiIvaGunner Christmas Comeback Crisis Side Story", where 2B steals the Garlic Taco from Haltmann Works Company. She seeks out Wade L.D. to help protect her from the police force hunting her down, eventually respecting Wade and offering to help him escape. The police end up chasing them across dimensions, with Wade sacrificing his life to help 2B escape. Elsewhere, 9S finds the Elder Scroll and uses its power to tear through space-time to send a message. This message reaches Eggnog, who finds 2B during the events of "Ransomware - Undertale 2" and sends her to Mundus. 2B and 9S reunite and use the Elder Scroll's power to return home. 9S broadcasts a follow-up message thanking Eggnog for his help.  Gegagedi and Numberphile[] After the events of "Golden Ratio - e" and the e∩Ω arc as a whole, Gegagedi was in an emotionally numb state after killing Numberphile. In "The Problem - e", he and his friends, still in the Coordinate Plane, looked through Numberphile's computer, noticing he had received an e-mail from a yet-to-be-revealed Susie Haltmann, warning him that he would die. The computer then got another e-mail; 9S' thank you message to Eggnog. A pop-up appeared, stating that a T-coordinate needed to be entered to forward it. Susie, who had perceived everything and was telling this narrative through the ARG, knew that Gegaedi would find the message and instructed him to fill in the correct coordinates, using her e-mail to Numberphile as clues, as well as the message in the description. With help from the audience, in "The Solution - e", Gegagedi deciphered the date the e-mail was supposed to be sent as January 31, 2017 at 9:30AM PST, translating to 1485883800 in T-coordinates. The message was sent back in time to that date for Eggnog to find, which is what causes him to go find 2B and help her in the first place. Seeing the mention of a car, Eggnog knew it was the Crappily Drawn Car from the Microsoft Paint universe due to his status as an anomaly. Back in the Coordinate Plane, Susie sent another e-mail to Gegagedi, encouraging him to forgive himself and tell him it might not be too late to save Numberphile, breaking him out of his stupor and leading into "It's time for a feast...", where he is filled with newfound hope.  Mr. Rent and Waluigi[] During 2B's travels across the multiverse, she went to the Kirby Fighters universe and got a Garlic Taco from Waluigi. This sent her to the Kirby Fighters Gameboy universe, leading to the events of "Main Theme - Kirby Fighters". Grey Kirby jumps through the open portal 2B left, going to the colorful universe and moving in with his counterpart. In "Main Theme - Kirby Fighters 2", the two Kirbys go to Waluigi's Tacostand. Grey Kirby samples one of Waluigi's tacos, which is so hot that he spits fire at him. Angered, Waluigi picks a fight, only for Pink Kirby to snatch a garlic taco, which opens a wormhole and sends Waluigi to the CCC. But, due to the Garlic Taco's time-warping properties, he goes to after 2B first arrived in the CCC. Mr. Rent, who was in the backseat of the Crappily Drawn Car when 2B stole it, was also sent to the CCC. As he got out of the car, Waluigi fell onto him. The resulting collision energy causes Mr. Rent and Waluigi's memories to be rewritten, making it seem like they've known each other for years. The two move in together and Waluigi gets a job working for El Bean, leading into "Opening Scene - Waluigi's Tacostand". Waluigi creates a taco for the "first time", leading to a portal opening. El Bean fires Waluigi and covers the portal with a blanket. El Bean made his rounds across Grandiose City, stopping by SiIva's house, while in the past, The Voice was attempting to summon 2B. His instance of Parsec ate his input to summon 2B, but coincidentally, the garlic taco portal from El Bean's truck was connected to the NieR universe. Pushing 2B out of the way of the portal, 9S was brought into the CCC at the truck's future point in space (SiIva's house) but at a previous point in time, before the taco was created.  Conclusion[] Despite everything having no consequences to the main story, the narrator concludes that it's okay to have fun with a story and not have it be consistent. Since the main story goes against having anomalies to avoid plot contrivances, stories and worlds away from it can have all the fun with anomalies instead. Art is about what is taken away from it and enjoying making it.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Overworld_()_-_Super_Mario_Bros._2;;;The video is presented in the format of "Thread Simulators", with the advertised track playing in the background as text-to-speech voices read social media posts. In this case, the video shows 4chan posts dated October 11, 2018, the day after the Unregistered HyperCam 2 Takeover. The first post is a response to a supposed leak of the cast of the King for Another Day Tournament as seen in the image which led to the discovery of this video (itself a reference to "The Grinch Leak"), and the user posts their own "actual leak", which refers to the fake contestants seen in the image. At 1:57, the main melody of the advertised track is removed and the video shows another post, which is actually a text log written by the SiIva A.I., read by the text-to-speech voice "Wiseguy" from Voice Forge, the same voice used for SiIvaGunner. The A.I. reports that the testing on the King for a Day Tournament and Unregistered HyperCam 2's event was successful, and that the quality of his own data stream has improved over the past few months, hypothesizing that the virus within his system had a positive effect on his level of sapience and the sophistication of the parallel universe. The A.I. proposes that he should investigate the virus further, using the greater processing power granted by a recent upgrade to its CPU. He observes that this upgrade resulted in a series of glitches leading to a temporary shutdown in April, during which the channel fell back to the personality model of Gadgetini Clone 2.0, whose parts were used in the construction of the A.I., causing the channel to appear to be taken over by Inspector Gadget. This had an effect on the parallel universe, in which Inspector Gadget took physical form and the Nostalgia Critic of that universe led a rebellion to temporarily gain control of the channel. The A.I. attempts to delete Inspector Gadget from its systems, but fails and simply suppresses the incident. He then decides to conduct a secondary controlled test with a larger control group due to the success of King for a Day, and initiates a "backup antivirus program". The video ends with a third post responding with "take your meds schizo".  ARG[] There are two codes that can be found in the video:  The first code is found in the image name of the last 4chan post. Inputting this string ("-BgZFNlO9TM") as a YouTube video ID leads to the video "Bad Ending - Despicable Me: Minion Rush", which is a dead end. The second code is found via combining the unique IDs of all the 4chan posts ("05210611610", "90780691120", "98089072065") in order. Taking 3 numbers at a time from the combined string produces a series of numbers that can be interpreted as decimal codes for ASCII characters. Inputting the resultant string ("4jtmNEpbYHA") as a YouTube video ID leads to the video "Secret Ending - Despicable Me: Minion Rush", which is needed for the next step in the ARG. Later, in the tournament bracket found in "test" from News Flash! SiIvaGunner: King for a Day Tournament, this log is paired with "Beyond the Gate", focusing on Unregistered HyperCam 2. Throughout the post, there are numbers embedded within some of Unregistered HyperCam 2's dialogue. Taking each number in order of appearance and combining them, similar to the step regarding this log, yields the number "420". This number is then combined with others found within the tournament bracket to lead to the final News Flash! post.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/One-Winged_Angel_-_Kingdom_Hearts:_Chain_of_Memories_II_Final_Mix;;;No elements of the advertised track are present. "Astronaut in the Ocean" is pitch-shifted and mashed up with the instrumental to "Thick Of It", with heavy amounts of reverb gradually applied throughout the rip. Starting at 0:12, the mashup gradually becomes unsynced as well, as "Astronaut in the Ocean" has a BPM of 150, whereas "Thick Of It" has a BPM of 146. At 2:23 and 4:59, the vocals to "Thick Of It" are added to the rip. At 2:37 and 5:17, the mashup suddenly cuts out. At 2:41 and 5:29, it cuts to part way through a heavily reverbed "Laughing Baby Bubbling Remix", before cutting out at 2:50. At 2:55, the mashup very briefly resumes before being cutoff and then fully resuming after. At 5:48, the unsynced mashup is slowed and pitched down significantly, and is played for the rest of the rip before abruptly ending. The overall length is meant to give the impression of the rip using the actual "One-Winged Angel". Additionally, the arranger credits play off the crediting of "Thick Of It".

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Story_Mode_-_Looney_Tunes;;;The rip begins with a parody of the Looney Tunes intro accompanied by "Looney Tunes Theme", which is present in most rips of this game. The episode is titled "CAR TROUBLES". As the title card shows up on screen, an arranagement of "Main Menu/Map" from Hotel Mario begins playing. Mr Rental greets the viewer, stating that he has had a long day at work, but made it just in time for the "big game." As he walks over to his car, a crude drawing of 2B first seen in "Final Destination - Super Smash Bros. UItimate" runs into his car and drives away. Mr Rental runs after the car and eventually runs infront of it, attempting to stop her, but instead gets hit by the car as 2B drives it into him. As he gets hit, a rapidly-growing portal appears on top of him, then the video abruptly cuts into the world from Mr Rental: The Video Game. The video shows the sky as a portal opens and Mr Rental falls out of it onto the sidewalk. Mr Rental gets up and looks off towards the scenery. A narrator describes what happened before the video cuts to a parody of the story selection screen from Sonic Adventure 2 while "Advertise: SA2 ... in the groove" from said game plays. The only option is "Follow Mr. Rental" on the right side of the screen. An endcard featuring the video "Mr. Rental selected!" appears on the left. The rip continues on this still for 15 seconds until the video ends.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Story_Mode_-_Mr_Rental:_The_Video_Game;;;The rip begins with a crude drawing of Eminem walking down the street, singing "The Real Shim Shady" to himself. Suddenly, Mr Own comes from the left side of the screen and shoots Eminem with a Remington 870 Express Tactical. The video then cuts to Eminem's point of view, who opens his eyes to see Mr Own standing above him, wielding spaghetti in his hand. Mr Own says "heard you like mom's spaghetti, bitch" before smashing the spaghetti into Eminem's face, which is implied to have killed him. Afterwards, the video cuts to Mr Own walking back home, remarking about how he has banned another mashup while "Thank You For Your Patience" from Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator plays. This is when a crude drawing of 2B from NieR: Automata, previously featured in "Final Destination - Super Smash Bros. UItimate", runs by and trips Mr Own, causing him to get angry and leading to him attempting to ban her while the Skrillex and Nero remix of "Holdin' On" by I SEE MONSTAS plays. 2B breaks into a nearby car while dodging shots from Mr Own, who proceeds to start the car and then drive it directly into him. The video swirls and has its colors distorted. The video cuts to the scenery of Looney Tunes, where Mr Own falls out of a portal into the street. Mr Own looks around confused and then walks off-screen, while a narrator describes what has happened. From here, the video cuts to a parody of the story selection screen from Sonic Adventure 2 while "Advertise: SA2 ... in the groove" from said game plays. The only option is "Follow Mr. Own" on the left side of the screen. At 1:07, an endcard featuring the video "Mr. Own selected!" appears on the right. The rip continues on this still for 20 seconds until the video ends.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/FACE_-_Yume_Nikki;;;The rip's title is based on "Yume Nikki OST: FACE (Extended)" by DontBleedOnTheSuits, a upload of "I Don't Want to See It!", which plays during the advertised game's "FACE" event. "I Don't Want to See It!" plays over a black screen with vibrating specks, zooming in on a face[Whose face?] before the rip cuts to a different visual of a black screen with some areas covered with gray squares and others with white squares in a random pattern at 0:20. The camera begins occasionally panning left and moving forward, with beeps played at regular intervals. At 0:30, the camera begins moving towards a white rectangle in the distance. When the camera reaches the white rectangle, it begins moving away, but also occasionally turns to notice the rectangle's position seemingly changing and/or moving closer on its own. At 1:04, the rectangle is extremely close to the camera, causing the visuals to rapidly zoom out to reveal a grayscale version of the earlier face before abruptly ending. The description of the rip uses the same format as rips uploaded during the Reboot.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Adventure_Tours:_Frosty's_Theme_-_Mario_%26_Sonic_at_the_Olympic_Winter_Games_(DS);;;The advertised track is mashed up with the instrumental to "Shrek" by Xasper.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Bob-omb_Battlefield_-_Super_64_DS;;;This rip uses "Bob-omb Battlefield" from Super Mario 64 DS, with the metadata removing all mention of Mario, referencing the April Fools' Day 2021 event. This is based on "hl2 stalker scream" by marinkunize (a jumpscare-laden edit of "MOVIE FREE (ORIGINAL SOURCE) [TOO HOT FOR YOUTUBE]" by diddy) with the following main changes, most of which reference the aforementioned event:  The music used in said video, an arrangement of the advertised track, has its melody changed to "Meet the Flintstones". This is likely a reference to "Throwback Galaxy (Beta Mix) - Super Mario Galaxy 2". The Mario and Luigi footage from the 2016 Kids' Choice Awards is edited to remove Mario. All footage with Luigi is similarly color-corrected like the aforementioned video, though this time to make Luigi purple. The other videos used are changed to the following: Mario in jail from Super Mario Sunshine, though with his eyes recolored to be orange. "Luigi Pentagram Meme / a joke Horrorbrew named Luigi Doll" is a video named "Luigi Doll Comes to Life" about a Luigi plush on a pentagram that begins to rise. Similar Luigi jumpscares are used in this rip, accompanied by the Half-Life 2 stalker scream sound effect, as well as two different jumpscares from Five Nights at Wario's: Return to the Factory and Five Nights at Wario's: Trapped Within. The opening line is changed to "Hello, I'm Luigi!" from "The Lost Nintendo Sex Ed. Tape" by the2toms. The text-to-speech is changed to the following, with the last line being sped up and played only in the right audio channel:  Do you want to set my brother free? Set my brother free at freemoviesfree dot com If you don't want to set my brother free then fuck you. To undo his doom, use a one-up shroom!   Additionally, a link to the image "RedRewards" (itself a reference to the image "Purple Prizes", which features a fake method of unlocking Waluigi in Super Mario 64 DS) is linked in the description instead of the playlist link. The rip starts with "Hotaru no Hikari" by Foo-san, infamous for being the video that plays when trying to view a deleted video on Nico Nico Douga, but with the flute melody changed to "Meet the Flintstones" and the voice replaced with "Wiseguy" from Voice Forge, SiIvaGunner's voice. From 0:00 to 0:09, text the bottom right corner reads:  ♪フリントストーン: Hoyt Curtin The Japanese text here is the Japanese name for The Flintstones. From 0:02 to 0:20, text scrolls up while SiIvaGunner says it out loud:   本日はニコニコ動画に 御アクセス頂き、 ありがとうございます。 大変申し訳ありませんが、 この動画はアップロード者が削除した為、 こ覧になることか出来ません。 またの御アクセスをお待ちしております。   Which means:  Thank you for visiting Nico Nico Douga. This video has been deleted by the uploader and is no longer available. We hope to see you again. At 0:19, the SiIvaGunner logo scrolls up, before stopping in the middle of the screen at 0:21. At 0:23, a clip from "TOTINO BOY" is played with the censor noice beep replaced by the last flute of "Hotaro no Hikari", leading into an 音MAD set to "Shisso Ensemble" by beatMARIO/COOL&CREATE, which is a remix of the advertised track.     Time  Description   0:23-0:34  Elements of "679" by Fetty Wap are mashed up, pitch-shifted and arranged to the track. The lyrics are displayed at the bottom of the video in Impact font. At 0:25, the video format shrinks in size before coming back to normal. At 0:29, the video framed on Fetty Wap's head on the lyric "Press rewind to see that ass one more". At 0:30, the music clip change to "The Soda Thief" by Logan Paul on "I got the soda". The "us" at 0:34 is stretch up.   0:35-0:44  Clips from the "Christmas in July" commercial are pitch-shifted and arranged to the track. The HHGregg supermarket and HH are shown on a pink background, with Japanese text reading "7月のクリスマスセール開催中！全品お買い得！" (Christmas sale in July is on now! Great deals on all items!). At 0:38, a character from "タミフルリバー三姉妹" by ツナマヨ is flipped around HH before being ejected by HH, and explodes.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/%E5%A4%9C%E3%81%AB%E9%A7%86%E3%81%91%E3%82%8B_-_X_PARK;;;The rip begins by showing a picture of a karaoke room, often used in "Yoru ni kakeru" 音MADs, with the visuals of the karaoke version of the advertised track played on the background screen and an image of the Nostalgia Critic shown on the right. Additionally, audio of the Nostalgia Critic's intro is also played, followed by a clip of the Nostalgia Critic saying "I love whores" from the video "Captain N: The Game Master", with Japanese text translating these audio clips shown at the bottom right. At 0:06, an image of Batman from Batman & Robin appears on the left, with the Nostalgia Critic image then changed to one facing Batman. At 0:07, audio from the video "Batman & Robin" is pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track, with the visuals from the karaoke version of the advertised track from earlier moving to the foreground and the visuals from "Batman & Robin" faintly added in the background. Additionally, text of the pitch-shifted clips is added to the visuals, formatted to resemble the scrolling behavior of typical karaoke machines. At 0:23, visuals from Batman & Robin are also faintly added in the background.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Yoshi's_Tropical_Island_(JP_Version)_-_Mario_Party;;;This is a YTPMV centered around McDonald's "Ran Ran Ru" Commercials and the advertised track. Starting at 0:40, several minigames from the advertised game ("Knock Block Tower" at 0:40, "Hot Bob-omb" at 0:42, and "Tightrope Treachery" at 0:45) are shown, with various images of Ronald McDonald, the aforementioned ads, and other fast food chains added to the visuals. In "Knock Block Tower", the main character, wooden boxes, and rocks are replaced by Ronald McDonald, McDonald's hamburgers, and KFC nuggets respectively. In "Hot Bob-omb", the four players are replaced by Ronald McDonald, Maō (satan), the altered version of the grandpa from Werther's Original, the witch from Nerunerunerune candy ad, and Fernandes-Kun 2gou from Japanese TV show Hirunandes, precisely this clip with Ronald McDonald; the Bob-omb is replaced by McDonald's french fries (commonly associated in the 音MAD community with the "The sound of McDonald's fries being fried" video). The use of Ronald McDonald, Werther's Original, and Nerunerunerune references "The Three Major Religions on NND", due to the three fads becoming popular on Nico Nico Douga at around the same time. In "Tightrope Treachery", the character on the ropes is replaced by Ronald while the three other players on the boats are replaced by the KFC logo. At 1:00, the visuals return to normal.     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Devilman_no_Uta_-_Devilman_(PS1);;;At 0:07, the melody changes to "Tatakae! Casshern" from Casshan. At 1:01, the melody changes to "Yuke! Tiger Mask" from Tiger Mask. At 1:37, the melody changes to "Youkoso! Japari Park" from Kemono Friends.

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Zen_Garden_(NTSC_Version)_-_Plants_vs._Zombies;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This is based on the Japanese whiskey commercial for Zen, a running gag in the MADs community, playing off the title of the advertised track. Like most MADs that use the commercial, the rip begins with the unedited commercial. At 0:27, the commercial transitions to the Zen Garden, with pots featuring an unknown woman, a Zen whiskey bottle, a mantis shrimp from another zen whisky ad, and a flower beginning to grow as the only flower pots shown, and the background consisting of a frame from the Zen commercial with the moon seen near the end visible at the top. The advertised track also plays during this, with clips from the Zen commercial pitch-shifted and arranged to the advertised track. At 0:52, the music from the first ad is pitch-shifted while Hiroyuki Sanada from the same ad fly behind the window. At 1:21, the flower pot with a flower asks for food, with a mouse appearing from the top with said food and giving it to the flower. The flower then develops into the head of the man mainly seen in the Zen commercial, before the rip fades out.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Circus_(Clean_Version)_-_Five_Nights_at_Freddy's;;;Immediately after the click, the first note of the advertised track is stretched out, with the thumbnail fading out as the game's title moves to the center and transitions to a parody of the official MV for "Letter to the Black World" by Frog96 ft. Kasane Teto at 0:02; the lyrics are split into four rows to match the lettering of the game's title and uses a similar font. At 0:11, additional text is added, flashing between "SEIZURE WARNING" and "光過敏性 / 発作の警告" ("Photosensitivity / Seizure warning"). At 0:15, "Se Piscar Já Era" is mashed up with "Letter to the Black World" with the trumpets of the former standing in for the bleeps of the latter, with the censor boxes showing a heavily posterized rendition of "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo". At 0:32, the lyrics of "Se Piscar Já Era" are added to the mashup with the text changed to match, and the background changes to the visuals of "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo". The melody of "Letter to the Black World" is also changed to "Se Piscar Já Era". At 0:54, the text reverts back to the original "Five Nights at Freddy's" title before the rip ends. The mix name references the bleep-heavy nature of "Letter to the Black World", and the "Composer" line lists "Teto "Dickman" Kasane", a play of Kasane Teto and Tito Dick.

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/File_Select_(Fairy_Fountain)_(NTSC_Version)_-_The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Phantom_Hourglass;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This rip as a whole references the Nico Nico Douga tag "性的なイタズラをしてみたシリーズ (Sexual Pranks Series)". Similar to videos with the tag, the rip begins by zooming out on this image of the Great Fairy of Power from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, with "Kokoro No Album Ni" from To Heart playing. At 0:04, the rip is interrupted by a "PARN!" voice clip from "My Beautiful Life (part 2)" (associated with the "Hissu Amoto San / Airmoto" trend), with the visuals suddenly switching to the aforementioned video. At 0:06, the rip becomes a 音MAD centered around the aforementioned video and the advertised track, with the fountain from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time shown in the background as well. At 0:32, the Soka Gakkai flag (also associated with "Hissu Amoto San / Airmoto") is also overlaid over the fountain in the background.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Theme_of_the_FM-ians_-_Mega_Man_Star_Force;;;The melody has been changed to "BGM09" from Chargeman Ken!, also known as the "Murder Record" theme used in the 16th episode of the aforementioned anime.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Train_%22Ticket_to_Ride%22_(JP_Version)_-_Touch_Detective_2%C2%BD;;;The advertised track initially increases in pitch and tempo, before a snippet from "ライアーダンサー (Liar Dancer)" by masarada ft. Kasane Teto is mashed up with the track at 0:05, transitioning into an arrangement of "ライアーダンサー (Liar Dancer)" in the style and instruments of the advertised track. Additionally, the rip's visuals show the black bars at the top of the thumbnail gradually moving along with multiple instances of Funghis appearing on the sides of the video as the background changes to the colors used in "ライアーダンサー (Liar Dancer)"'s official music video, animated to sync with the MV. Additionally, the rip was part of the final four rips of Lost Media Day which shared their titles with SiIvaGunner's four lost rips.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Because_I_Love_You_(Alpha_Mix)_-_Earthbound;;;This is an arrangement of "The Great Pumpkin Waltz (Alternate Take 2)" from It's The Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown in the style of the advertised track. The title deliberately lists the game title as Earthbound (with a lowercase b), to match the removed title of the lost rip.     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Lost_in_Thoughts_All_Alone_-_Fire_Emblem_Fates;;;This rip as a whole references the removed rip of the same name. The rip begins by showing the ripper's computer screen in VLC media player with what seems to be the original file for the aforementioned removed rip; "lost in thoughts all alone.mp4". The ripper then clicks on the file to play it, with the advertised track then playing, with the thumbnail of the rip taking up the whole computer screen. At 0:38, the lostwave song "Curly Toes" is pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track. The rip is abruptly cut off when the camera turns to reveal the fruit from Splat the Fruit as the rip ends.

The inclusion of "Smooth" references the rip's mix name and the copypasta associated with "Smooth", 'I’d Rather Be Listening to Grammy-Award Winning 1999 Summer Hit Smooth By Santana Feat. Rob Thomas of Matchbox Twenty'.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Credits_-_Kekcroc;;;This is an arrangement of LSuperSonicQ's intro/outro theme using Sega Genesis instruments. The composer line in the description credits "jaxcheese", who made the LSuperSonicQ theme.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/STRM_CREDITS_-_Initial_D:_EX;;;There is no actual track titled "STRM_CREDITS" in Initial D: EX, as the aforementioned game does not exist. Instead, the rip uses "Rage your dream" by m.o.v.e, a song often used as the ending theme in the Initial D anime. The choice of title likely references "STRM_MARIOKART" and "SEQ_MARIOKART", placeholder audio files for Nintendo DS and Nintendo 3DS games. Also, the D: EX part of the title plays with FEX, the band behind the song used in the joke. "Rage your dream" is mashed up with "Subways Of Your Mind", with the mashup slightly compressed to match the quality of a Nintendo DS streamed track. From 0:00 to 0:20, the voice presenting the song from the live recording can be heard, mimicking what motsu (the m.o.v.e male vocalist) says in the original Rage your dream recording.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Green_Hill_Zone_(Tokyo_Toy_Show_Prototype)_-_Sonic_the_Hedgehog;;;This is an arrangement of "Lamú: Urusei Yatsura" by Noam Kaniel and Ciro Dammicco, also known as the opening theme to the Italian dub of Urusei Yatsura (titled Lamù, la ragazza dello spazio), using the instruments of a version of "Green Hill Zone" heard in prerelease content for Sonic the Hedgehog (note the faster speed and higher-pitched backing instrument compared to the final version of "Green Hill Zone"). Both elements tie into Lost Media Day: the Tokyo Toy Show prototype of Sonic the Hedgehog is considered to be lost media (since it was not found in Sega's archives despite searching), and "Lamú: Urusei Yatsura" was considered to be lostwave, as it had no known authorship before 2020 despite being released in the 1980s.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Hitogata_-_Polaris_Chord;;;No elements of the advertised track are present. Instead, the rip is based on a lost Japanese railroad crossing PSA of the same name as the advertised track and the various recreations made of the PSA. Like the recreations, this uses the bells of a Japanese railroad crossing, though with "Shikairo Days" from My Deer Friend Nokotan pitch-shifted and arranged to the bells. Instead of the thumbnail, the rip uses images of Torako Koshi and Noko Shikanoko from My Deer Friend Nokotan in front of a scene from Episode 2 of said anime, "Deer Meets Darkness Girl", with them flashing in a manner that matches most recreations of the PSA. The background and characters are also edited to match the colors of said recreations. At 0:10, the text "地球上では2秒に1頭の割合で鹿が死んでいる。" ("Every two seconds, a deer dies around the world.") appears over, with a voice reading said text, referencing similar text of said recreations as the rest of the rip fades to black.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Happiness_World_-_SOUND_VOLTEX_EXCEED_GEAR;;;Starting at 0:24, the rip transitions to a recreation of the official music video of the advertised track themed around "Cotton Eye Joe" and the Roblox Chicken Nugget, with the vocals to "Cotton Eye Joe" by Rednex and audio from the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" video pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track as well. In particular, segments that originally featured Houshou Marine in the original music video now feature the "Cotton Eye Joe" character from "COTTON EYE JOE (RELOADED)" by Harris & Ford (with the background changed to be mostly green), while segments that originally featured Shirakami Fubuki in the original music video now feature the Max Design Pro version of the Roblox Chicken Nugget (with the background changed to orange). In both backgrounds, the silhouettes are changed to (in no particular order) banjos, beer jugs, cacti, cowboy hats, longhorn cattle, violins, wheels, and the original Roblox Chicken Nugget, and the new lyrics are shown on-screen in a similar style to the original music video. At 0:48, 3D YouTube play buttons replace the Fubuki-themed television sets from the original music video. Starting at 0:53, anime versions of the "Cotton Eye Joe" character and the Max Design Pro Roblox Chicken Nugget appear at the bottom right and left, where equivalent versions of Fubuki and Marine appeared in the original music video. At 0:57 and 1:28, the visuals from "COTTON EYE JOE (RELOADED)" are added to the rip. At 1:10, a visual of the original Roblox Chicken Nugget entering a white door inside a large bush is added to the rip. At 1:32, the visuals from "school rooftop funk shuffling @Leader Omega Nugget @Omega Pasta credits @Reborn Omega Teabag #chips #omeganugget #burpingnugget #omegachipswithcrab #omega #omegaverse #fyp #viral" by @wenochipswithcrab are added to the rip.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_-_Kiara's_Loading_Screen_Game;;;The rip plays gameplay footage of the advertised game, with the chicken drumsticks from the original game replaced with Chicken Drumstick from the Gegagedigedagedago series by GoLuB, and "Cotton Eye Joe" by Rednex pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track. At 0:16, the Gegagedigedagedago nugget used by Max Design Pro appears as the chicken drumsticks, with audio clips of JonTron saying "What?" from the video "Anti Drug Games" and of Kevin Hart saying "Help me, HELP ME!" from Kevin Hart: Let Me Explain pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track. At 0:29, the gameplay footage is grayed out, with the "HELP = Like Button" visual used by Max Design Pro in the center, the Max Design Pro Nugget at the bottom left, and the Like Timer Sound Effect used in Max Design Pro videos played alongside the advertised track. At 0:32, a cursor appears to click the Like Button twice, changing the Max Design Pro Nugget to its cowboy form, followed by the Max Design Pro Nugget moving behind Takanashi Kiara, several KFP appearing to chase Kiara off-screen and run around the Max Design Pro Nugget, a spotlight effect added to the visuals overall, and audio from the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" video pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Green_Hill_Zone_-_Sonic_the_Hedgehog_(2013);;;No elements of the advertised track are present. Instead, this is a recreation of the video from this Tweet by Google Play, with audio from the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" video and instruments from "Cotton Eye Joe" by Rednex arranged to "AI 2" by Vibe Mountain (the song used in the aforementioned Tweet's video) and the pixelated gameplay footage replaced with a similarly pixelated animation of the Roblox Chicken Nugget in the scrapped Sand Shower Zone level meant for Sonic the Hedgehog 2. Additionally, the official @GiIvaSunner Twitter account reposted the content of this video to Twitter with the same exact caption as the Google Play tweet, though the link has been replaced with a tinyurl link that leads to the playlist for the game.[3]  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Laid_to_Rest_-_Assassin's_Creed_III;;;No elements of the advertised track are present. Iann Dior, the song used in the original video. The choice of the advertised track's name and the joke is a reference to Omega Lays' fate from the "e∩Ω" story arc.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Golden_Ratio_-_e;;;This rip serves as the penultimate episode of the e∩Ω story arc, taking place after "Thrash Machine (Beta Version) - Deltarune". The rip begins with a recreation of the e thumbnail, before zooming out to show The numberphile and Charlie, The Steak standing in front of the screen shown in "Waterfall (Short Mix) - Undertale", in the same square plane used in the aforementioned rip. The numberphile is at the coordinates "(4.2, 0, 1.8)", while Charlie is at the coordinates "(-4.1, -0.4, 5.2)". At 0:04, an "e" portal opens up, revealing the canyon background used in the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" series by GoLuB. Gegagedigedagedago himself peeks into the portal, which then turns into a square to reveal Hamood Habibi and several other characters from "Tombstone & Nugget Town - Wanted", who sing "Cotton Eye Joe" by Rednex, the cover by TikToker @razioff, the turkey from "Gegagedigedagedago 5" by Gchmch, and a fart sound effect associated with the Brainless Kitty. At 0:13, it cuts back to The numberphile, staring in disbelief as Charlie turns to look at him. He turns off the screen in front of him before the rip transitions back to the other characters, now in the same plane, though without any coordinates to them. Gegagedigedagedago steps forward and starts singing the cover by @razioff, only for The numberphile to cut him off with "No, e!", summoning an "e" tile from the rip "Gameplay - 2048". Gegagedigedagedago pulls out a knife with the Roblox Man Face, previously seen in the rip "Tsurupettan (Beta Mix) - Umineko no Naku Koro ni", and jumps at The numberphile, doing a freeze frame at 0:24 as the other characters begin to move closer. This transitions into an elaborate fight sequence set to "Quality Assurance" from The SilvaGunner Christmas Comeback Crisis, with various sources arranged to it:     The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help! (melodyswap)  ???   2:24  "Hamood Habibi"  Muhammad Ghaloum   2:45  "OI OI OI Bakugou"  La Memerano   2:58  "Tutorial (Part 1) - π"  TimmyTurnersGrandDad   3:10  "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago"  @razioff, @wenonugget   "Mega Man"  Jay Eazy   ??? (melodyswap)  ???   3:23  "e (Euler's Number)"  Numberphile   3:37  "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago"  @razioff, @wenonugget  Before Gegagedigedagedago can attack, The numberphile teleports away, summoning an "e" tile before being attacked by the sushi character from the "Gegagedigedagedago" series, who bites at The numberphile's head numerous times. He quickly begins shaking and throws the two of them away. At 0:37, the rip cuts to the canyon outside the coordinate plane, with the bread cowboy character from "Tombstone & Nugget Town - Wanted" in front of the portal, watching the fight. The numberphile is shown to be standing at the coordinates "(6.4, 0, -43.2)", as he throws "e" tiles at the turkey, before the machine from "Thrash Machine (Beta Version) - Deltarune" appears and begins shooting lasers at The numberphile, though they don't seem to have any effect. The numberphile then throws an "e" tile at the machine, which disappears upon contact with the tile. The numberphile claps his hands and does an "e" blast, sending Hamood Habibi and the turkey away before he jumps up and flies off. At 0:57, the "camera" moves to the right to reveal the FL Studio logo edit of the Roblox chicken nugget from "World 1 Map (Alpha Version) - Kirby's Adventure". At 1:02, it cuts to Charlie and Gegagedigedagedago playing a game of chess. Gegagedigedagedago wins the match and Charlie is edited to look sad, moving away as the rip zooms in on Gegagedigedagedago. At 1:22, it zooms back out to show Omega Crab Lays from "Waterfall (Short Mix) - Undertale" and Chicken Drumstick from "Open Sesame Tofu! (In-Game Version) - MOTHER 3" floating above the "e" as ghosts, referencing the events of their aforementioned rips. At 1:28, it cuts back to The numberphile, who opens up a different "e" portal that sends out three clones of himself from "Main Theme - Manhole-e" that attack the other characters. At 1:42, the sushi character returns, dropping down with a parachute before rescuing the others by eating the clones. The numberphile begins throwing "e" more tiles in the background as the rip cuts back to the canyon at 1:54. The bread cowboy character leaves to get the other sheriff characters from the start of "Gegagedigedagedago 5", riding back to the portal entrance on horses. At 2:10, it cuts to them returning to the portal, unrolling a piece of paper that reads "YOU CAN DO IT IT, GEDAGEDIGEDAGEDAGO!" before holding it up at the entrance. The rip cuts back to the fight at 2:20, with the other characters coming in to acknowledge the message. At 2:35, The numberphile summons another "e" tile and throws it, creating a red "e" portal that summons Red from Larve. However, Charlie, now edited to look angry, throws his own "e" tile at Red and sends him away, causing The numberphile to look at him in shock. At 2:52, Red appears in the field from "Tutorial - Bad Tsunko no Doki Doki Omikuji", this time with Hana-Maru in between two tombstones for Pandaba and Tsunko in the background (referencing the events of the aforementioned rip) and Badtz-Maru standing next to Red. Badtz-Maru gets mad and gifts Red a bomb that explodes on him, causing him to disintegrate. At 2:58, the "that takes care of that!/congratulations!" screen is briefly shown before switching to the text "Meanwhile, far away in the coordinate plane...", which transitions into the next scene. The milk character is then shown navigating a maze inside the pie used in the π thumbnail, with the Matt Parker/Dancing Banana fusion from "Tutorial (Part 1) - π" on the right. The digits of π are displayed one by one from the top left corner as they are said, in a similar manner to "Tutorial (Part 1) - π Music Extended" by BrawlBRSTMs3 X, much like the aforementioned rip. At 3:08, the milk character escapes the maze and takes out the Matt Parker/Dancing Banana fusion. Finally, at 3:09, the rip fades into a Friday Night Funkin'-styled battle between The numberphile (using the same character sprites from "Satin Panties (Week 7 Update) - Friday Night Funkin'") and Gegagedigedagedago. At 3:50, the music ends shortly before The numberphile dies, similar to how the player character dies with blue balls despite winning the level in most Friday Night Funkin' rips, as Gegagedigedagedago's face changes to a more depressed one and Hamood Habibi appears from the right. The rip then fades to black shortly after. Additionally, the title references how the golden ratio is another common mathematical constant that is included in the "e (Eular's Number)" video, the composer credit is for Razi Irawani, the real name of the person who did the cover of "Cotton Eye Joe" associated with Gegagedigedagedago, and the catchphrase has several of the "e"s changed to "ℯ".

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Thrash_Machine_(Beta_Version)_-_Deltarune;;;This rip continues the e∩Ω story arc, taking place after "Tsurupettan (Beta Mix) - Umineko no Naku Koro ni". The rip begins by showing a back alley resembling the in-game location where the advertised track plays, with "Cotton Eye Joe" by Rednex and the cover by @razioff pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track. A Whoopee cushion with the Roblox Man Face represents the bush and an Among Us crewmate with realistic feet and the Roblox Man Face, the original Roblox Chicken Nugget, and the Man Face Chicken Drumstick from "Gegagedigedagedago" by GoLuB represent Ralsei, Kris, and Lancer (and are recolored to match the respective character). After this, the rip parodies the original sequence from the advertised game, with several changes made to better suit the story arc, including:  Changing the beginning text to "Create a machine to gedash Your own ahh / Presented by Chicken wing industries /(Which Was Just Made up Right Now, Cuh!)" Changing the SOUL icon to a red Roblox Chicken Nugget Changing the flavor text and item labels of several items in the menu, with the Roblox Man Face added to some sprites as well The styles are now "OMEGA", "SWEEZY", "YUTE", "freaky", "x-Factor", and "SHOOTIN' MECHANISM'S" Under the "HEAD" mechanism, the menu options are now the following: SPLOO: An off-the-cuff gun-sizzle that has a green aura with flies, my G! SCHWANG: A balkan ween reserved for rage-induced episodes, yo! HEAT: Watch out for that spicy jit! It'll make you blush, my bimbap broski! The sprite has Joe Biden's face added instead JIT: Poop from a butt. Your credit score is headed down the drizzle, my cuh! The sprite is of Baby Incredible Under the "BODY" mechanism, the menu options are now the following: PLAIN: Yo, what? Ain't that like that cuh that flies around going "hey swee-bop?" WHEEL: Another word for circle or something like that. I'm not too sure. The sprite is of a Wii Wheel instead BLOCK: Mi amigo, this is the utmost powish compendium of cuhworthy pecks. The sprite is of a drawing of a Minecraft dirt block JIT: Just looking at this is making your credit score plummet, mi amigo! The sprite is of a Galaxy Gas whipped cream dispenser Under the "SHOE" mechanism, the menu options are now the following: SNEAK: Air Jordan 11 Low Cool Grey (2021) on StockX.com. Visit now! The sprite is of the Air Jordan 11 Low Cool Grey (2021) as described in the flavor text A.WHL: Cuh, this is Andrew's Wheel The sprite is of a wheel with 8 legs around it TREADED: Past tense of trea The sprite is of the Air Jordan 13 with a Walmart logo JIT: Your credit score's toast. The sprite is of a piece of buttered toast with shoe straps and a price tag of $1000 The final selected options are JIT for the "HEAD" mechanism, BLOCK for the "BODY" mechanism, and TREADED for the "SHOE" mechanism. After the options are confirmed via the text "This is your machine. / Is that bussin?", the created machine appears from the left with a spotlight applied to it. At 1:19, the visuals transition to an edit of the advertised game title that says "omegarune", before zooming out to reveal Young Gedagedi (from the rip "Main Theme - Young Seldom") printing out the created machine from earlier (with the "Gegagedigedagedago printer" sound from "Gegagedigedagedago 5" by GoLuB used). The camera then pans to reveal the Roblox Chicken Nugget nodding in approval, with another printer shown creating "e" tiles used by The numberphile.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay_-_Charlie%2C_The_Steak;;;This rip continues the e∩Ω story arc, taking place after "Game with Rabbit Set Up (Alternate Version) - Othello World". At the start, the rip shows someone playing Charlie, The Steak and using a blow torch on him. At 0:19, after Charlie is flung away with a spatula, it cuts to an image of a factory that has the Charlie, The Steak logo on it in some spots, with Charlie exiting the factory and saying "I'm on vacation" from "Vacation" by Dirty Heads. He then moves down a bit, before saying "Ei" and pulling out an "e" tile used in the rip "Gameplay - 2048" and throwing it, causing it to transform to the "e" from the thumbnail of e and changing to a white square, accompanied by the sound of the nether portal from Minecraft. Charlie then enters the white square, before the rip zooms out to reveal Hamood Habibi was watching and then moves to get better look at what is on the other side of the white square. At 0:38, it fades to Charlie moving on the same square plane used used in "Waterfall (Short Mix) - Undertale", including the same coordinates, with "There She Is" from Portal 2 playing, and the background behind Hamood being the canyon background used in the "Gegagedigedagedago" series by GoLuB. At 0:40, the rip cuts to "The numberphile fusion with James Grime / Jay Eazy from the rip "Main Theme (Alternate) - e", who is at the coordinates "(4.2, 0, 1.8)", and is standing next to a large "e". The numberphile says "e", as it greets Charlie, who moves to the coordinates "(4.5, -0.4, -0.7)", and Charlie responds back with "E E Ei". The numberphile then says "Wait here", as he jumps into the "e", which opens to reveal the background used in "Main Theme (Alternate) - e" and The numberphile jumps using the same sound effect in "Gameplay - 2048". The numberphile coordinates also change as he jumps, before fading out. At 0:47 Charlie says "D", while he waits for The numberphile to return.  At 0:48, The numberphile returns, this time also having the same screen he used in the rip "Waterfall (Short Mix) - Undertale", though this time the screen shows the canyon background, as he positions himself at the coordinates "(-1.9, 0, 22.8)" and says "Ok?". The rip then zooms in on the screen, which changes to reveal The numberphile's plans, which consist of killing the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" and all of his friends / other characters in the series by GoLuB. The roasted chicken character that appears is also the same one from "Gegagedigedagedago 5" by Gchmch. Charlie then laughs after hearing the plans, using the same one from "Hello, Friend! - Hello Kitty Island Adventure", before cutting back to Hamood, who is running away from the white square, as the rip zooms out to show the whole desert background used.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Stage_Performance_-_Maroon_GO;;;This rip is mostly a "Cotton Eye Joe"/"Roblox Chicken Nugget"-themed parody of "Sweetest Goodbye" by Maroon 5, with audio from the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" video pitch-shifted and mashed up with the rip as well. At 2:57, "Harlem Shake" is also mashed up with the rip. The visuals initially show a Sony Vegas project file of the rip, with an edited version of the thumbnail containing the Roblox Chicken Nugget as its main visual and various assets in the side menu. Overlaid on top of these visuals is another copy of the edited thumbnail, the text "lyrics will be real in 24 seconds" on the left, and the watermark "real watermark.com" at the top center. At 0:01, the ripper maximizes the video in the project file, revealing a screenshot of a Microsoft Word file containing another screenshot of a Google Image search for the image used on the Wikipedia article "Thrust stage". At 0:24, the lyrics to the aforementioned parody appear in a text file on the left, as the Roblox Chicken Nugget begins to dance to the melody of the rip. The ripper also begins adding additional elements to the rip, including copies of the Travis Scott x McDonald's plushie version of the Roblox Chicken Nugget with smiling mouth asset from Battle for Dream Island at 0:28 and 1:05 (and moving the mouth asset to the melody of the rip), copies of the original Roblox Chicken Nugget on the thumbnail at 1:03, 2:08, and 2:57 (which also move to the melody of the rip), and a Google image search for this image from the restaurant Harlem Shake at 2:57 (which moves across the screen). At 3:34, the text file of the lyrics is removed, with Charlie, The Steak (also with the smiling mouth asset added and moved to the melody of the rip) added at the top right and "Vacation" by Dirty Heads added to the mashup. At 3:55, the music stops, with the thumbnail removed and Charlie holding the note longer. When the plushie Roblox Chicken Nuggets have their mouths turned upside down to express their discontent, Charlie says "I'm sorry, I'll leave if you want me to... wah..." as the rip ends.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Tutorial_-_Bad_Tsunko_no_Doki_Doki_Omikuji;;;This is a continuation of the rip "Intro Cutscene - Bad Tsunko no Doki Doki Omikuji". At the start, a frame from the game where Tsunko is standing next to a rope and door is shown and edited with the following:  Tsunko is replaced with The numberphile fusion with James Grime / Jay Eazy from the rip "Main Theme (Alternate) - e". The door instead has the "e" from the thumbnail of e. Pochi is removed from the bottom right. At the door, The numberphile says several of James Grime's opening lines of the "e (Euler's Number)" video, before pressing the top button to open the door and reveal Pandaba inside it. The numberphile then says "e" again and pulls the rope, which sends down an "e" tile used in "Gameplay - 2048" on Pandaba, with both then disappearing, in a manner that matches some of the events in "Waterfall (Short Mix) - Undertale". At 0:07, a clip of Charlie, The Steak from the teaser trailer for his titular game appears on the right, with The numberphile then looking at him and Charlie saying "Ei" from "Vacation" by Dirty Heads. The two then have a back and forth over "e" and "Ei", in a manner similar to "Title Theme & Ending - e", before The numberphile says "Well, you right, thanks a lot." At 0:20, it cuts to The numberphile and Charlie, The Steak in a field with Hana-Maru and Badtz-Maru in the background, as The numberphile is sentenced-mixed to say, "What if I offer you an "e"?", before giving a gift to Charlie. Charlie then opens the gift, to reveal it was an "e" tile. At 0:25, Tsunko appears from the right, with the two then looking at her, Charlie saying "Ei", and The numberphile saying back "No, e!". Charlie then throws the "e" tile at Tsunko, as they both disappear as well. The numberphile then tells Charlie that "If you're not trying to deliberately avoid terms of "e", you're making it hard for yourself. It's the natural language, ok?". Charlie only responds with "Ei", right before the rip abruptly ends.

The video's first title and original thumbnail were made to give the impression of a Homestuck theme specifically:  The video was uploaded on November 11th (11/11), a significant date in Homestuck.
