 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Sugu_Ni_Kese_-_Shin_Megami_Tensei;;;"Sugu Ni Kese" is not an actual track in Shin Megami Tensei; the track name refers to an urban legend associated with the advertised game, which purportedly states that there is a small chance of the game's title sequence freezing and displaying a wall of red text saying "Sugu ni Kese" repeatedly. The rip begins by playing snippets of the intro sequence of the advertised game interspersed with the text "Sugu Ni Kese", followed by gameplay footage of the initial portions of the game. "Demo" from the advertised game initially serves as the backing track, before switching to "Dream" from the advertised game (with elements of "Title" from the advertised game incorporated) at 0:04. At 0:44, the original text is changed to "TURN IT OFF TURN IT OFF TURN IT OFF TURN IT OFF", before switching to a battle from the advertised game. During the battle, the sound effects and visuals are arranged to "Demon Appears" from the advertised game, with the text "すぐにきけ" ("Sugu Ni kike", meaning "listen now") occasionally appearing on-screen. At 1:19, a wall of text repeating "すぐにきけ" slowly fades in, before switching to another battle, this time against Jack Frost. During this battle, an original arrangement using elements of "Battle" from the advertised game plays, with the original text replaced with random characters, and the text "すぐにきけ" appearing more frequently on-screen and to the melody of the arrangement. At 2:21, the rip suddenly switches to and plays the title sequence of the advertised game, followed by switching to a wall of text repeating "すぐにきけ", as described in the original urban legend.     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Memory%3Dentryrrrr%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F_-_My_House;;;This rip references "Take On Me but it's in the Super Mario 64 Soundfont (Music Video)", and continues the story from said rip, "Mail for the Mario Brothers (Demo Version) - Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door", and "Pathetic House (In-Game Version) - Undertale". At the start, an animated ripped up paper used as a dialogue box is shown with Brainless Kitty talking, using the font from Paper Mario, and set to "Quiet Water" from Undertale making this a direct follow up to "Pathetic House (In-Game Version) - Undertale":   Is this some kind of joke?  It had been weeks since anyone had last heard from Silentó, but in my paws, clear as day, was a letter written by him.  Parsing the contents one more time, I took the fastest route to his house I knew.   At 0:15, a paper is shown with a pencil-drawn Paper Mario wrap pipe, before the visuals and music fade out. At 0:22, the advertised track begins playing, with it also mixed with the instrumental of "Take On Me" and "Take On Me but it's in the Super Mario 64 Soundfont (Music Video)", as it fades into a pencil-drawn image of Mario's house from Paper Mario, from the perspective of Brainless Kitty, as it continues talking, this time also making comments on several things around the house as it explores it, with them highlighted in blue as Brainless Kitty talks about them:   Here I am.  It's been a while since I last visited this place, before Silentó's big victory even. I haven't had much need to since I moved out.  An old rundown place like this can barely house a cat, let alone a person.  [Mario's name on the house is then highlighted in blue as Brainless Kitty describes it.]  I see he still hasn't changed that sign. I don't expect the previous owner to be all too happy about that.  [Door is then highlighted in blue, as a sound of a knock plays.]  No answer.  Guess I'll just have to use my old key   At 1:04, the visuals then fade to black again, as it switches over to the interior of Mario's house, with Brainless Kitty continuing to make comments in similar manner:   It's almost exactly how I remember it. Though there's a chilling lack of Silentó anywhere to be found. He must be out of town.  [The cabinets on the right are then highlighted in blue.]  Probably shouldn't be rummaging through his stuff until I know what's up.  [A picture of the Undertale thumbnail from "Pathetic House (Sigma Mix) - Undertale" is then highlighted in blue, as the vocals from "Pollyanna - EarthBound Beginnings/MOTHER" are added to the rip, referencing both the rip "Pollyanna - MOTHER 1+2" and the appearance of "Pollyanna" in "Take On Me but it's in the Super Mario 64 Soundfont (Music Video)". Brainless Kitty also references the Undertale rip being the first appearance of him on the channel.]  It's a painting of where Silentó's first found me.  Ahhhh... to be nothing more than your average humble brainless again. Though I supposed being able to think is better than that.  [The doorway across the room is then highlighted in blue.]  Better stop dawdling and check in here.   At 1:51, the visuals fade to black again, as the sound of foot steps plays to indicate Brainless Kitty walking over to Mario's bedroom. At 1:53, the visuals fade into a pencil-drawn Mario's bedroom, with iMac G3 also on his desk, referencing "Mail for the Mario Brothers (Demo Version) - Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door". Brainless Kitty continues:   The feeling of emptiness I got when I first entered the house multiplied exponentially when I stepped foot in the bedroom.  I couldn't shake the feeling that I wasn't supposed to be here.  [The shelves on the left are highlighted in blue. Brainless Kitty makes note of a camera that appears to be positioned in a manner to match the bedroom shot from "Mail for the Mario Brothers (Demo Version) - Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door".]  The shelves are too high up for a kitty to reach. Really they're almost too high up to see clearly.  I can just barely make out what seems to be a picture of me and Silentó.  Above that are a couple of plates from the previous owners and... a camera? It looks like it's still on, but why?  [The iMac G3 is then highlighted in blue. Brainless Kitty also makes a comment referencing how in the aforementioned rip, Silentó was able to use the iMac G3 despite no obvious sign of a mouse or keyboard.]  I'm not quite sure how Silentó still uses this prehistoric piece of junk. Especially without a mouse and keyboard.  Looks like there's something taped to it.   At 3:07, the visuals fade to black again, before fading into a closer pencil-drawn shot of the iMac G3 with a note over the screen:   It seems like he left a note. It looks like it hasn't been touched in quite some time.  It reads...  [The visuals fade to black as the note is read.]  "DON'T TURN ON COMPUTER"  "conscious waning ability to think decaying fighting sleep he's back don't be fooled"  "He"? Did Silentó mean... How could this have happened?  Whether Silentó meant that or not, he's missing and clearly needs my help.  [The visuals and audio cut to black.]  There's no time to waste.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/PlayStation_Startup_(Alpha_Mix)_-_Console%2FBIOS_Music;;;This rip is both based on and references Lethal Company. The rip starts by playing a modified version of the PlayStation startup, with "SONY" replaced by "SIIVA" and "PlayStation" replaced with "Play Again?". At 0:18, the rip plays an arrangement of "Intro Company Speech" from Lethal Company using the instruments of the advertised track, with the visuals switching to a recreation of the startup screen for Lethal Company. The player initially attempts to select "ONLINE (RECOMMENDED)", but is shown the following screen:  ONLINE CURRENTLY UNAVAILABLEPLEASE ASSURE YOUR CONSOLE IS CONNECTED TO BOTH THE I-MODE ADAPTOR AND AN I-MODE PHONE THEN TRY AGAIN.EXIT MENU After returning to the main startup screen, the player selects "SINGLEPLAYER", taking them a recreation of the title screen for Lethal Company. At 1:34, the player selects "HOST", with the music switching to an arrangement of "Company Building Music" from Lethal Company using the instruments of the advertised track and the visuals switching to gameplay footage of a PlayStation-style demake of Lethal Company. The player moves around the environment, exploring the area until 2:44, entering a door as the music stops. At 2:58, the music resumes as the player is seen inside a new area. The player continues to explore this new area until 4:53, entering another area as the music stops again. At 5:02, the rip plays an arrangement of "Boombox Song 5" from Lethal Company using the instruments of the advertised track, as the player is dropped into another new area. The player explores this new area until 6:17, where they are shown entering another area as the rip gradually ends.

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Commercial_Theme_-_8-Bit_Beast's_Haunted_House;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.Missing: Identify the images.   This rip mimics the format of videos purporting to have visual evidence of a particular cryptid, with the focus in this video being on the 8-Bit Beast. "Dodongo's Cavern" from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time plays throughout the rip. The rip begins by presenting a series of Windows Movie Maker slides with the following text:  Castle BeastCAUGHT ON CAMERA!!!The Castle Beast is a noctural creature that hangs around forests and old buildings like castles.Sometimes it also appears during the day when the weather is bad.It can be recognized by the very distinct roars it makes, which start by going up and down wildly for for a second.(youll know when you hear it)Its often said that witnessing the beast may give you very bad luck for awhile.I've compiled all the proof i could find of it's existence.WARNING!!!! These pictures are 100% REAL!!! Viewer discretion is advised! At 0:50, the visuals transition to a series of images that the video claims is proof that the 8-Bit Beast exists. Each image includes text describing the image and an edit to include the 8-Bit Beast somewhere on the image. The images are:  This image of the Castle of Silves, with the 8-Bit Beast at the top right of the castle ("Old picture of the beast") This image of Burgajet Castle, with the 8-Bit Beast at the center of the castle's top row of windows ("(Look at the window)") An unknown image, with the 8-Bit Beast in the middle ("Recent photo I think") An unknown image, with the 8-Bit Beast at the top center and pointed out via a red circle, arrow and the text "WTF?" written out ("noticed by photographer") An unknown image, with the 8-Bit Beast at the center left ("when you see it... o.o") An unknown image, with the 8-Bit Beast in the middle ("looks fake...lol") An unknown image, with the 8-Bit Beast at the center left ("hiding or maybe creeping") An unknown image, with the 8-Bit Beast in the top right window ("House sighting??? / better watch out") At 1:45, the credits roll, with the following text:  CreditsVideoMePicturesInternetMusicLegend of Zelda Ocarina of Time-Dodongo CavernRate 5 starsand subscribe

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Good_Night_SiIva_Swim;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.Missing: There are several minor details in the visuals.   This is based on the "Atlanta" Adult Swim sign-off, which itself uses elements from the "America" Adult Swim sign-off. Because this is the final video of the Cartoon Network Day & Adult Swim Night 2 event, the sign-off additionally doubles as a conclusion to event as a whole, parallel to 6:00 AM (a parody of Cartoon Network's "Good Morning" sign-on) being used as the opening. In this bumper, the music from the aforementioned sign-offs is arranged to "Meet the Flintstones" and "Title Theme & Ending" is also played over that plays "The Star-Spangled Banner", referencing the music of the original bumper. At 0:13, Loud Nigra is pitch-shifted to the music. The music is accompanied by a scenery pan of Grandiose City, similar to how the original sign-offs showed a scenery pan of Atlanta and American landmarks respectively. At 0:34, the visuals zoom in on The Voice Inside Your Head's tower with the [siiva swim] logo on it, followed by an announcer saying "This concludes our broadcast day, Thanks for watching [siiva swim].". At 0:41, the owl from the "Atlanta" sign-off is shown in SiIvaGunner's color scheme, followed by the [siiva swim] logo on a black screen as the video ends.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_-_Tim_and_Eric_Awesome_Game%2C_Greater_Job!;;;This is a spoof of the show Tim and Eric Awesome Show, Great Job!, using similar sketch comedy, bizarre spoof commercials, and editing to that of the show. The rip presents these sketches under a show with a similar title of "Joe and Jackson Awesome Show, Grand Job!". Throughout the rip, the "[siiva swim]" logo appears on the bottom right after the opening bumper.  Opening Bumper[] At the start, the rip begins with text in the style of Adult Swim's bumpers with the following:   The show you are about to watch  was inspired by two comedians.  Maybe a little too inspired.  It was made in under a month  and cost Joe to lose his job.  That was a joke.  Enjoy the show.   SwampAss Ad[] At 0:13, it goes to the first sketch, which is an ad for a product called "SwampAss" (Sweet Watery ALL Mnatural Purified Air Savory Scent), a cosmetic item designed to give you a bad smell on desired area. Dave Matthews, the creator of the product, also makes an appearance during the ad. At 1:03, the ad zooms out to someone watching it on his TV, initially confused why anyone would want to buy it, before deciding to get it after seeing the only side effect shown being sex, lots of sex, and penis. Immediately afterwards, the viewer broke character and reaches to turn off the camera.  Joe and Jackson Awesome Show, Grand Job! intro[] At 1:17, the rip goes into a parody of the intro for Tim and Eric Awesome Show, Great Job! with the following changes:  All lines of "Tim and Eric" are changed to "Joe and Jackson", with the parody intro also featuring them. At 1:23, the saxophone plays "Totino's", referencing the song originating from the Tim and Eric "TOTINO BOY" video. At 1:27, the fax machine is changed to a TI-84 graphing calculator, followed by the hotdog being changed to a bunch of Totino pizza rolls, and the cats being changed to chickens. Joe and Jackson Awesome Show, Grand Job! opening (part 1)[] At 1:38, it cuts to Joe and Jackson setting up their microphone while standing in front of a greenscreen. At 1:44, it then cuts to a signal screen, before cutting back to Joe and Jackson after the microphone is set up and the greenscreen begins showing a outside location at a farm. Joe and Jackson thank both the SiIvaGunner team and "everyone's local fire department", before Joe decides to "gift" Jackson a fisheye lens. Joe then explains that the fisheye lens will be used as a way to transition to the next sketch, though initially nothing happens after he says "Check it out!", though Joe then takes off the cover and then the camera zooms in on the lens after Joe says, "Check it out!" again. There is a brief pause as the two bicker about the use of the lens before the next sketch begins.  Doug Toppfive's Airs List (part 1)[] At 2:38, it goes to the next sketch, which is a top 10 list by Doug Toppfive about the top 10 airs. During each point, Doug would discuss the air in question and what makes it so important, usually being nonsensical. It is also during this that the "Channel 7" logo first appears on the bottom right corner. The airs listed during this part of the sketch are:   10. Helium 9. Supply Air 8. Hydrogen 7. Indoor Air   Our Thirty Year Old Virgin Anchor (part 1)[] At 3:54, the list is then interrupted by an "Our Thirty Year Old Virgin" breaking news segment with Artie Flopshark. Artie begins in a middle of a news story about the deaths of several infants in a fire at a hospital, before he is handed a new paper about the breaking news and begins exclaiming about how Ed, Edd n Eddy has been taken off Netflix. The rip then goes to a reporter standing at a park named Dr. Freddy Fazz Flap, who says that isn't his name. They continue to discuss the matter, before Dr. Fazz Flap screws up his lines and then cuts to the next sketch.  Channel 7 Kid Break[] At 4:37, the rip then cuts to a sketch titled "Channel 7 Kid Break" that involves someone doing a rap about going to the store for his mother in order to get lights for her decor, before deciding to also get her veggies and peas. During this, the person is greenscreen over supermarket locations and outside at an empty parking out. The rap abruptly ends as the person begins repeating "I got her peas", due to sounding similar to "herpes", and the greenscreen from the opening sketch is briefly shown.  Joe and Jackson Awesome Show, Grand Job! opening (part 2)[] At 5:11, it cuts back to Joe and Jackson at the greenscreen set up arguing about the use of the fish eyes lens for transitions. The bit abruptly ends right as the two begin to appear to kiss each other.  Dr. Testy's Dog Removal Ad[] At 5:35, it cuts to a sketch based on various Tim and Eric Awesome Show, Great Job! fake ads starring Tim and Eric. In this sketch, it's Joe, as Dr. Testy Vick Mison, and Jackson, as Rick Mison, on a place called "Dr. Testy Vick Mison's Mice & Dog Removal", which is a store based around killing people's dogs and mice. During the ad, Vick and Rick kick and kill various dogs and mice in various ways, including eating parts of their bodies. At 6:29, Rick also kicks and kills a grandma in a wheelchair as well. At 6:44, the ad closes with "Grand Job!", referencing "Great Job!" used in similar manner on Tim and Eric Awesome Show, Great Job!, followed by Eric Andre screaming and the visuals morphing to the next sketch.  Doug Toppfive's Airs List (part 2)[] At 6:48, it cuts back to Doug Toppfive's Top 10 Airs List, continuing where it left off, though also skipping the numbers 5, 3, and 2.   6. Hot Air 4. Argon 1. Oxygen   After the list, Doug thanks his cousin Adam for helping him in making the sketch.  Joe's British Impression[] At 7:54, it cuts to a title card for the sketch with "JOE'S/BRITISH/IMPRESSION" over the United Kingdom flag. At 7:57, it cuts to Joe standing in front of a greenscreen and acting as if he is in the United Kingdom while doing an impression of a British person, which includes him meeting Michael Rosen, supposedly entering his house and showing off unbrushed teeth, and "f***ing love Wallace & Gromit". At 8:36, Joe's face flies off to the "Our Thirty Year Old Virgin Anchor" logo, as a transition back to the "Our Thirty Year Old Virgin Anchor" sketch.  Our Thirty Year Old Virgin Anchor (part 2)[] At 8:38, it cuts back to Dr. Fazz, this time walking around and asking several people about how they feel about Ed, Edd n Eddy being taken off Netflix. Several times Dr. Fazz says and makes mention to Ed, Edd n Eddy being an "Italian show" and huge part of Italian culture. Dr. Fazz also interviews a woman, though instead asks about if she wants a divorce and if she loves spaghetti. The sketch ends with someone saying that the show was an "Italian Touchdown" followed by the visuals zooming out to a title card with the said line in the Italy flag, the "Channel 7" logo in the background, and Plank from Ed, Edd n Eddy appearing on the top left.  The Pillgruns[] At 9:39, it then cuts a parody of the "The Pillgrums" sketch from the Tim and Eric Awesome Show, Great Job! episode "Tennis" with the following main changes:  The sketch is presented with the director Rodney Adams and a 3D model of Grunner as one of the actors. The movie shown is instead "The Pillgruns" by Haltman Works. The movie's poster also contains the following: The tagline is "THE WORLD'S FASTEST GRUNNER". The main stars are Grunner, Rodney Adams, and Wesley Willis. The credited costars are "VINESAUCE JOEL CHARLES MATINE JOHN DOUGLESS KANYE EASTRYAN REYNOLDS FRANK REYNOLDS SOME POOR BASTARD NAMED JOHN SETH MACDONALD KINGASSRIPPER ERIC ANDRE CHA WARDON MY CRACKDEALER DAVID WHOSE THE ONE DUDE FROM 12 OZ MOUSE?" A Cannes-inspired award blurb reads "GRAND MOVIE OF THE YEAR". Unlike the original sketch, there is nothing that takes the place of Grunner's 3D model when he briefly isn't present when the camera turns to face him at 10:06. Before a clip from the movie is shown, Rodney initially gets confused when it seems there isn't a clip, then starts yelling at an unseen crewmember. The clip of the movie instead shows Rodney as a Pilgrim and Grunner, both standing on Tetra's pirate ship from The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker, approaching Bedrock and seeing cavemen eating Totino's Pizza Rolls. The featured Totino's Pizza Rolls brands include: Pepperoni Flavored Mini Snack Bites Faze Clan Orange Chicken Pepperoni 90 count 160 rolls Triple Cheese Grunner's brain is triggered by "Totino's", and shows Chip tha Ripper replacing Chippy as a pun on the character's name, edited to have slanted eyebrows, a beard, and a blue shirt saying "QUALITY BABY.", and walking in a 100 Pizza Roll Totino's bag. After he is circled and the line "There's my Chippy" plays, he screams using Loud Nigra and Prettyboy Floyd yelling towards the end of "S.L.A.B. Freestyle". Joe and Jackson Awesome Show, Grand Job! conclusion[] At 10:52, the sketches end back at Joe and Jackson standing in front of the greenscreen, discussing how they were unsure how to end the rip and hoping that the viewers found them to be funny. After several seconds of silence from the two with Joe vigorously rubbing his temple, it then cuts to the credits for the rip.     https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Opening_-_SiIva_Planet;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   The rip plays the "Hello Everybody" intro bumper for the 2012 revival of Cartoon Planet, with the audio pitch-shifted to "Meet the Flintstones", and all mentions of "Cartoon Planet" sentence-mixed to say "SiIva Planet" alongside the VoiceForge "Wiseguy" text-to-speech program (the voice for SiIvaGunner). At 0:10, Vinesauce Joel's reaction to 7 GRAND DAD is briefly added to the rip. At 0:12, the audio is pitch-shifted to "Megalovania". At 0:18, "Gangnam Style" is briefly added to the rip. At 0:21, a voice clip of maxmoefoe saying "Stop!" is added to the rip, followed by "Title Theme & Ending" playing alongside the bumper.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/The_Dawn_is_Your_Enemy_SiIva_Swim;;;This is based on "AS: The Dawn Is Your Enemy (FULL BUMP WITH WINK)" by Ikjleio, which itself is based on a creepypasta about a supposed extended version of the "The Dawn is Your Enemy" bumper. "Final Hours" from The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask is arranged to an extended version of the opening for "Violence Is A Menace" by Bola Adekimi, the music featured in the original video. As well, the original image of the bumper is used, with the sun with a face changed to the Moon from The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask.  At 0:44, Nicolas Cage in the "Not the bees!" scene from The Wicker Man begins playing, as the eyes on the top fade to Cage's, the moon fades into the surprised Cage face from the beginning of Face/Off, and "THE DAWN IS YOUR ENEMY" text fades into "WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE NUMBERS RUN OUT?", referencing a line from Knowing. Starting at 0:51, several Nicolas Cage screaming clips during the aforementioned scene begin playing, as well as the line "THIS IS MURDER! MURDER! YOU'LL ALL BE GUILTY! AND YOU'RE DOING IT FOR NOTHING! KILLING ME WON'T BRING BACK YOUR GOD DAMN HONEY!", also from The Wicker Man, replicating the screams that are heard in the original video. At 1:10, the Nicolas Cage face winks, before shortly cutting to a signal screen, like it does in the original creepypasta. The appearance of Nicolas Cage with The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask references the heavy association of the two sources on the channel.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Mission_Clear_(Steam_Version)_-_Sonic_Adventure_DX;;;The "Bird Up!" intro jingle is mashed up with and arranged to the advertised track.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Ring_Ring_Ring!_-_Little_Busters!;;;At 0:11, 1:30, and 2:55, the advertised track is mashed up with "Easy to Breathe" from Jack Stauber's OPAL. At 0:32, the image of a house is changed to the album cover for ., which is edited to match the shape of the original house image.

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Secret_Ending_-_Despicable_Me:_Minion_Rush;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   The video opens with someone filming a person in a Minion costume, with the lights turning on few seconds after, while "Get Lucky" by Daft Punk ft. Pharrell Williams & Nile Rodgers plays in the background. The cameraman gets closer to the Minion, before the video starts glitching.  It transitions into the video "minion dave - what does the fox say" by Bridgette P, with a string of text, faintly written at the top of the screen: "UzhZKUJj".  Seconds later, the video glitches again, changing back to the Minion footage, with it panting and saying "I gotta get... Someone, help me!", before turning around and showing its' tied hands. During this segment, "Minions March" from the Despicable Me OST plays in the background. Then, the video glitches yet again and transitions into the video "Zakopane" by Jakiś Kanał, which is a phone recording of a bootleg Minion toy dancing to "Bara Bará Bere Berê".  Once again, the video glitches into the Minion footage, with it being freed and standing up, while a distorted voice speaks in the background, saying "Are you ready to listen now? Are you ready to dance?". Soon after, another glitch transition occurs, switching into an unknown video, which is a vertical video of a green screen Minion GIF, with three captions, one at the top reading "minion dance", one at the bottom reading "bottom text" and one diagonally in the center reading "https://forms.gle", while "Return Of The Tres" by Delinquent Habits plays in the background and a TikTok text-to-speech voice says "What shenanigans is that Minion up to? Look at him go. She is so cute. I wish I could dance like him. Finally, the video glitches back into the Minion costume recording, with it dancing to "Party Rock Anthem". It then "throws" an object at the cameraman, which causes it to glitch one last time, revealing another string of text reading "LRkPFvKZ7", with a faint picture of the Minion person in the background.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_-_9:05;;;There is no actual track titled "Main Theme" in 9:05, as the game is a text-based style game with no music. Instead, the rip shows someone playing 9:05, initially with the text unchanged, with them answering the phone, taking a shower, getting new clothes, and then heading down to the living room. However, at 1:53, when the player enters "go south", the text begins to heavily deviate; instead of saying "The front door is closed." when going south, it jumps to the "Driveway" text that appears after exiting the house. An extra section is also added to the "Driveway" text where it describes a person strolling on the sidewalk whose stated description matches that of The numberphile fusion with James Grime / Jay Eazy from "Main Theme (Alternate) - e". The player then decides to go on the sidewalk to which it gives more matching description and The numberphile begins saying several lines from the "e (Euler's Number)" video.  The player then attempts to enter the car, however The numberphile then pulls the letter "e", which appears to be the "e" tiles used in the rip "Gameplay - 2048" and act in a manner that matches some of the events in the rip "Waterfall (Short Mix) - Undertale", then throws one at the player, though misses, and one at the car, with the car collapsing into dust once the "e" tile has been thrown at it. The player then enters "go east" however game says it isn't good idea, given the "e" tiles, and says "What does he want you to do?" The player then responds with "give watch to man" to which The numberphile responds with "Wow, thanks a lot!", before pocketing the watch and jumping away, in a manner that matches how he jumps in the rip "Gameplay - 2048". The last line shown is "What was the point of that?" At 3:26, it abruptly begins scrolling back up and zooms in on the "e" of "spare", right before the rip ends. Additionally, playing off the title of the rip, the rip was also uploaded at 9:05 AM PDT.

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Hogan's_Alley_Music_-_Game_A_~_Miss_~_Success_~_SHARP_SHOOTER!;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   At the start, it is a YTPMV set to the four jingles, using sources related to the "E E Ei" meme. As well, gameplay of Hogan's Alley is shown with the targets changed to related chracters:  "Game A" is set to "Vacation" by Dirty Heads, accompanied by Red from Larve, two deepfaked Charlie, The Steaks on either side, and the targets moving into view from Hogan's Alley. "Miss" is set to "OI OI OI Bakugou" by La Memerano, accompanied by Red from Larve and the "MISS" screen from Hogan's Alley. "Success" is set to an unknown song, accompanied by the "Zesty Ei Ei Ei" variant of Charlie, The Steak and a correct target being shot screen shown. "SHARP SHOOTER!" is set to "Ei Ei Ei Estoy De Vacaciones" by Vristok, accompanied by a 3D model of Super Meat Boy from "Ei Ei Ei MEME PARODIA ORIGINAL Estoy de Vacaciones #eieiei #meme #robloxmemes" by vristok and the "SHARPSHOOTER!" screen from Hogan's Alley. At 0:16, the visuals switch to gameplay from Simple Marble Race, a game usually seen in various "E E Ei" memes, that uses the four previous characters, with the images taken from the rip itself, referred to as "Ei Ei Ei", "Oi Oi Oi", "Zesty Ei Ei Ei", and "Spanish Ei Ei Ei" respectively, and each accompanied by each respective YTPMV audio of the four jingles they were set to whenever one is in the lead over the others.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Mail_for_the_Mario_Brothers_(Demo_Version)_-_Paper_Mario:_The_Thousand-Year_Door;;;This rip continues the story of the "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)" section of the rip "Take On Me but it's in the Super Mario 64 Soundfont (Music Video)". "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)" is pitch-shifted and arranged to the advertised track. At 0:53, the thumbnail fades into Mario's house from Paper Mario with the same clip art of a newspaper on the steps of Mario's house used in the aforementioned rip. At 0:58, the music begins to fade out, as several alternating gifs of Silentó dancing appear from the right. He moves to go to the front door, then fades out to represent him entering the house. At 1:07, a slide transition is used to show a 3D model of the interior of Mario's house, with Silentó fading in from the door, before moving over to the next room. At 1:13, the rip briefly cuts to static, before showing Mario's bedroom with an iMac G3 edited onto the desk, and Silentó moves to the computer. At 1:16, the music begins to muffle, as the visuals also slightly go into grayscale, before zooming in on Silentó and fading to black.  At 1:23, it shows a computer monitor at the Google homepage, with Silentó's face as the user avatar on the top right, as the mouse moves over to switch to Gmail. At 1:28, the monitor quickly fades to black before showing Silentó's inbox, which mostly consists of various read messages sent by Steven Cymatics, the CEO of sample and plugin provider Cymatics.fm, which refer to various Cymatics.fm transactions made by Silentó. The only other message is an unread message from "Purb" with the subject "SMILE! Cot loves you!", sent at 2:10PM. The mouse then slowly moves over to click on the unread message, before the visuals fade to black again and then show the contents of the message, revealing "Purb"'s email to be "prplebk@kitties4u.com":   Hello!  What bright times ahead  a new age!  See my attached file to see what awaits the future!   Spread the word.  .           .      д   At 1:45, the screen slowly scrolls down, with a sound of a heart beating on each scroll, to show an edit of the Paranormal Prickheads “Smile Dog” image from the ChainmailChasers ARG with the evil Brainless Kitty from the aforementioned rip replacing Smile.dog. The message itself also parodies the message in the "Smile Dog" creepypasta. This rip's story is continued in "Pathetic House (In-Game Version) - Undertale" and "memory=entryrrrr///// - My House".

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Snake_In_a_Box_-_Batman:_Arkham_Origins;;;A codec conversation between Solid Snake and Colonel Campbell plays over the advertised track starting at 0:06. The conversation is spliced together using clips from the Super Smash Bros. Brawl codec conversations. The first line is from Meta Knight's, followed by two lines from Wolf's, then two lines from Mario's, which is cut off by Snake screaming and Colonel Campbell's KO message. Additional sentence mixing is used to make both character's say "Batman". Snake uses clips from Wolf's ("bat") and Meta Knight's ("man"), and Colonel uses clips from Pokémon Trainer's ("bat") and Fox's ("man").

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Fresh_(Pico_Mix)_-_Friday_Night_Funkin';;;The rip plays gameplay footage of a modded version of the level with the following changes, many of which are shared with "Fresh - Friday Night Funkin'":  Daddy Dearest, Pico, and Nene are replaced with the crewmates from "Fresh - Friday Night Funkin'", with the crewmate replacing Nene (twerking crewmate) recolored pink and the crewmate replacing Pico (blue crewmate from "Among Drip" render) recolored lime and holding Pico's gun. The crewmate replacing Daddy Dearest (red crewmate from "Among Drip" render) is once again, used from the "Fresh" rip. The beatboxing segments have the beatboxing sounds replaced with Among Us sound effects. At 0:10, Pico's vocal melody is changed to sing "Impostor Imperceptible (Among Us)" by NerdOut. At 0:27 and 0:59, Daddy Dearest's vocal melody is changed to sing "AirPod Shotty", with Pico's vocal melody responding in kind. At 0:36 and 1:08, the "sus, sus" voice clip from "Among Us in Real Life" is briefly mashed up with the rip. At 0:42, Pico's vocal melody is also changed to sing "Among Us in Real Life". As is customary with most Friday Night Funkin' rips, Pico dies with blue balls despite winning the level; in this case, the death animation is changed to reference the impostor kill animation from Among Us. The Red crewmate, reused from "Fresh - Friday Night Funkin'".The Red crewmate's up pose, also reused from "Fresh - Friday Night Funkin'".The Pink crewmate, as seen in this rip.The Pink crewmate revealing as an Impostor and killing the Green Crewmate.The Green crewmate, as seen in this rip.The Green crewmate's game-over animation.

Like the original rip, this is a spoof of YouTube shipping AMVs, animated music videos, using the advertised track, though with several changes from the original:  The Nutshack theme is mashed up with the advertised track. The ship this time is of Tito Dick x Pumpkin. The dialogue follows the same story as in the original rip, with Tito and Pumpkin talking about their feelings for each other, before they go on a date and have sex. Similar edits of images are used as in the original rip, sometimes being the same images from the original, with Tito's head and images Pumpkins pasted over characters and people in them.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/We_Will_Rock_You_vs._Robot_Rock_-_DJ_Hero;;;At 0:06, "Se Piscar Já Era" is mashed up with the advertised track, made to match up with the usage of Queen's "We Will Rock You" in the intro of "Se Piscar Já Era". Starting at 0:38, when the beat of "Se Piscar Já Era" drops, its horns are arranged and pitch-shifted to the melody of Daft Punk's "Robot Rock" in the advertised track. Additionally, the rip shows visuals primarily centered around "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo" by SORRIZO RONALDO. At the start, the thumbnail image is intercut with footage from the video in sync with the audio. At 0:17, the logo fades out and the video begins showing several images of logo edits and seizure warnings from other rips featuring "Se Piscar Já Era":  "Intro Theme (OST Mix) - Mundial Ronaldinho Soccer 64". "Jurassic Meow - Garten of Banban 4" "Gang-Plank Galleon (PAL-M Version) - Super Smash Bros. UItimate" "Main Theme - Twister Ice Fun" "Bad Apple!! feat.nomico - SOUND VOLTEX III GRAVITY WARS" "Main Theme - Five Nights at Freddy's 3" "Unwelcome School (BR Version) - Blue Archive" "Wonder Flower: Funny (Demo Version) - Super Mario Bros. Wonder" "Yoshi Star Galaxy (OST Mix) - Super Mario Galaxy 2" "Puzzle Room (Rhythm Code) (PAL-M Version) - Kirby Planet Robobot" "Amalgam (Singapore Airlines Version) - Undertale" "Checker Dance (NTSC Version) - Deltarune" "Sauna - Persona 4" "Baby Park mas é o Sorrizo Ronaldo que chegou" "Raceways mas é o Sampley de Guitarra" "Yo, Go Crazy! (In-Game Version) - Shantae and the Pirate's Curse" At 0:38, a silhouette of the advertised game's logo appears, followed by a crude drawing resembling the logo with text reading "SEIZURE WARNING :)", before cutting to visuals from "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo". Starting at 0:53, the video is intercut with footage from the music video for "We Will Rock You". At 1:20, the album cover art of Daft Punk's Human After All is shown intermittently. At 2:06, when the advertised track says "We rock", the video briefly shows an image of the Wii console followed by the video of "The Rock's Eyebrow Raise". At 2:40, footage of Bowser laughing from the opening cutscene of Hotel Mario is shown in sync with the audio. Instead of the regular catchphrase used in the Independence Day of Brazil 2024 event, the video description uses "Por favor vá pra puta que pariu.", referencing the lyrics of "Se Piscar Já Era".  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Want_You_Gone_(PAL-M_Version)_-_Portal_2;;;This is an electronic forró-style arrangement of the advertised track using samples used by Os Barões da Pisadinha, with the original vocals of the track initially mashed up with the arrangement. Starting at 0:24, vocals from "Desce do Cavalo" by Os Barões da Pisadinha are mashed up with the arrangement, and are arranged and pitch-shifted to the vocal melody of the track during the chorus. From 1:26 to 1:44, the track's original vocals appear, accompanied by Os Barões da Pisadinha vocals. The rip ends with audio from the end of a live performance from Os Barões da Pisadinha. Additionally, at 0:24, the logo in the thumbnail transitions to an edited variant, with the text changed to read "PAREDÃO 2" and stylized depictions of Rodrigo and Felipe Barão in an orange portal to the left. Instead of the regular catchphrase used in the Independence Day of Brazil 2024 event, the video description uses "Por favor desça do cavalo.", referencing the lyrics of "Desce do Cavalo".       The edited logo used in the rip.   
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Great_Fairy's_Fountain_(OST_Version)_-_The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Ocarina_of_Time;;;Vocals from "Faz o sample de Guitarra" are arranged and pitch-shifted to the advertised track. At the beginning, the title credits from the video appear, with visual effects matching the audio. The video then shows DJ Marquinho from the image in the video in front of the yellow background of the thumbnail image, flipping in sync with the audio and with the words "Faz o sample" appearing to the right. At 0:16, DJ Marquinho is mirrored and overlaid on top of the video. At 0:26, the video fades into showing "DJ André Marques Manda AQUELE Ao Vivo" by eduardobm, which becomes transparent as the previous visuals repeat. At 0:53, the video fades into an edited version of the advertised game's logo, with the text changed to read "The Sample of Zelda: Guitar of Time". Instead of the regular catchphrase used in the Independence Day of Brazil 2024 event, the video description uses "Por favor bote na cabeça.", referencing the lyrics of "Faz o sample de Guitarra".  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Raft_Ride_(130_BPM)_-_The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Link's_Awakening;;;This rip features part of an FL Studio recreation of "Party Rock Anthem". Starting just before the first chorus, a guitar loop from later in the "Party Rock Anthem" remake has been added and is rapidly pitch-shifted and layered over itself to resemble the notes from the start of "Raft Ride". This is interrupted by the voice that says "shake that". Afterwards, the chorus has the melody and chords switched to those of "Raft Ride". The rip at first seems to loop over at 0:18, but then at 0:47, the entire rip is put under the default FL Studio effect Pitcher, causing it to sound slightly distorted (as Pitcher is an autotuning effect and is not meant to be used on full mixes), and is additionally raised 7 semitones via the usage of another default effect, Pitch Shifter. At 0:56, the relatively infamous FL Studio effect Soundgoodizer is also added to the mix. At 0:58, the final instance of the low beep is given an unnecessary amount of reverb for no reason. During the fade out of the rip, the tempo briefly switches to 100 BPM, and then 80 BPM before returning to 130 BPM, and some of the layered guitar loops are muted. The mix name references "Party Rock Anthem" (and the rip itself) being 130 BPM.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Senatus_-_Last_Bible_III;;;"Don't Laugh" by Winx and Loud Nigra screams are pitch-shifted and arranged to the advertised track. "Don't Laugh" is also edited to move around both audio channels throughout. Instead of the thumbnail, a YouTube 360-degree video version is used with the Last Bible III logo in the center, a chain that wraps around the VR video, and a rainbow effect applied over, though the effect only lasts up to red before reversing back to the yellow used on the thumbnail. As well, "Don’t Laugh" is represented by this TikTok video by @vidzardtv which uses "Don’t Laugh" and is associated with the "AI Rick Laughing" meme, while Loud Nigra is represented by an image of the head of Josh Hutcherson associated with the "Josh Hutcherson "Whistle" Edit" meme and the body of the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" meme, with Josh's face also deep faked to go with the Loud Nigra screams. The Josh deep faked face also could be in reference to "#CapCut #coems #coems🤑 #omegaverse #omeganugget #omeganuggetlover #omega" by @theofficialomegagrape. On top of this, the sources visually appear in a manner to match the audio moving to different channels of each respective source in the rip itself.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Bopeebo_(Weekend_1_Update)_-_Friday_Night_Funkin';;;This rip plays gameplay footage of a modded version of the level with the following changes:  Boyfriend is replaced with the Brainless Kitty. The fart sound associated with Brainless Kitty is pitch-shifted to the advertised track during Boyfriend's verse. At 0:22, the "cat" instrument from Mario Paint arranges the background vocals during Boyfriend's verse, with "Boykisser" by Studi01, which samples said instrument, mashed up as well. At 1:33, several copies of the Brainless Kitty character icon fill the screen in the style of the Weekend 1 Update's new transition animation.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Tema_da_Gaba%C3%A7%C3%A3o_de_Sune%C3%A3o_-_Toca_Pisadinha;;;"Tema da Gabação de Suneão" is neither a track in the advertised game nor a song by Os Barões da Pisadinha, the inspiration behind the advertised game. Instead, this is an electronic forró-style arrangement of "Suneo's Bragging Theme" using samples used by Os Barões da Pisadinha. The advertised track's title translates to "Theme of Bragging of Suneão" in Brazilian Portuguese, with "Suneão" being a combination of Suneo and Barão, while the credited composer is the composer for the music used in Doraemon (1979), including "Suneo's Bragging Theme".

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Jack-in-the-Box_Zombie_Theme_-_Plants_vs._Zombies;;;Audio from the Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago video is pitch-shifted over the advertised track. In addition, Jack-in-the-Box Zombie's jack-in-the-box is shown in front of the thumbnail with the same deepfake animation used in the Roblox Chicken Nugget video applied to it. During the note where the word 'pop' in "Pop Goes the Weasel" would be, the chip on a toilet from the "Chips 'Farting'" section of "Gegagedigedagedago + Memes" by GoLuB appears and is sampled instead. This sequence loops three times. It begins to loop a fourth time but at 0:19, the jack-in-the-box springs open, with ROBLOX Man face (a.k.a. Gegagedigedagedago's face) added to the jester inside the box. Immediately afterwards, audio of JonTron saying "What?" from the video "Anti Drug Games" (a source frequently used in Max Design Pro's Gegagedigedagedago videos alongside Kevin Hart saying "Help me, HELP ME!" from Kevin Hart: Let Me Explain) plays, accompanied by a shocked face associated with the aforementioned Kevin Hart clip appearing on the jester. A stock explosion effect then plays, which leaves a hole in the thumbnail. The SpongeBob SquarePants Roblox Chicken Nugget from the video "Gegagedigedagedago SpongeBob" by GoLuB slides up from the bottom of the hole but the rip abruptly ends as soon as it reaches the center.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/This_Stinks..._-_Wedding_Peach;;;At 0:17, the melody changes to "100 Sunny".  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Headspin_(Title_Track)_-_Shower_With_Your_Dad_Simulator_2015:_Do_You_Still_Shower_With_Your_Dad%3F;;;The advertised track is mashed up with "That's Enough" from Jet Set Radio.  Fake-out[] Alongside the release of this rip, several elements of the channel were updated as a fake-out for "Go and Take a Shower Day", which had been announced in "SiIvaGunner: 7 Fact Extravaganza" and mentioned again in "SiIva Direct 6.4.2024":  "Shower Time Ballad - MOTHER 3" was made the featured video. The banner was changed to feature: A shower head is added above the lighthouse. Grand Dad, Nozomi, and Tito Dick have shower caps added. A pool of soap bubbles is added at the bottom of the lighthouse. The hidden rectangle at the bottom left has a bar of soap added.        Several playlists with music featuring the word "Shower" were updated: Love Live! School idol festival ("Shangri-La Shower") MOTHER 3 ("Shower Time Ballad") Out Run ("Magical Sound Shower") SOUND VOLTEX IV HEAVENLY HAVEN ("Poppin' Shower") These changes were reverted four hours later with the release of "This Stinks... - Wedding Peach", accompanied by "Mission Failed - Kirby's Dream Land 3" being made the channel trailer and featured video.     
    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Hurt.ogg_-_Minecraft_2.0;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.Missing: Images and video sources of Mike Matei   No elements of the advertised track are present. The rip begins with using the rip "hurt.ogg - Minecraft". At 0:05, the rip cuts to Inspector Gadget from "Minecraft with Gadget" edited over "A Sorry Announcement.", as a voiceover similar to Gadget's voice in said video reads out parody of "So Sorry.", Logan Paul's infamous apology video created to respond to his suicide forest controversy, this time with the lines changed to reference "Minecraft with Gadget":   I have made a severe and continuous lapse in my judgement, and I don’t expect to be forgiven. I’m simply here to apologize.  What I did to Mike Matei on that day was obviously unplanned. The reactions you saw on tape were raw; they were unfiltered. I didn't know how to react or how to feel. I should have never posted the video. I should have put the cameras down and stopped recording what I was going through.  There's a lot of things I should have done differently but I didn't. And for that, from the bottom of my heart, I am sorry.  I want to apologize to the internet. I want to apologize to anyone who has seen the video. I want to apologize to anyone who has been affected or touched by mental illness, or depression, or being named Jerome. But most importantly, I want to apologize to the victim and his family.  For my fans who are defending my actions, please don't. I don’t deserve to be defended. The goal with my content is always to entertain; to push the boundaries, to be all-inclusive. In the world I live in, I share almost everything I do. The intent is never to be heartless, cruel, or malicious.  Like I said, I made a huge mistake. I don’t expect to be forgiven, I’m just here to apologize.  I'm ashamed of myself. I’m disappointed in myself. And I promise to be better. I will be better. Thank you.   The Inspector Gadget theme plays during this. At 0:24, 0:38, 0:45, and 1:07, the rip shows the original "Minecraft with Gadget" video, including a frame from "Calm - Minecraft". At 1:10, the Inspector Gadget theme ends, as white noise begins to become louder. Starting at 1:19, several slowed down clips of Mike Matei raging during games begin to be added. At 1:25, several images of Mike Matei begin to fade in.  At 1:39, the rip abruptly cuts an image of Mike Matei that was also used as the banner for April Fools' Day 2018, followed by flashing several clips of Mike raging. At 1:40, it cuts to the music video for "The Fall of Jake Paul", with Mike's face edited over Logan's and several lines from "Minecraft with Gadget" and different clips of Mike raging mixed with "The Fall of Jake Paul". At 1:47, the Cinemassacre logo appears, as a different image of Mike Matei, associated with the "Jigging Mike" meme appears to grab the logo and a chainsaw sound effect begins playing. This is then followed by several zoom in frames of said image of Mike with the Cinemassacre logo edited over the Inspector Gadget and a frame of Gadget from "Minecraft with Gadget". During these, the Cinemasscre logo is edited to intially remove "Cine", before the text fully changes to "imgur.com/D5xlSei". This is then followed up by Gadget shooting Mike with the chainsaw right before the rip ends. Additionally, the catchphrase is changed to reference both the catchphrase used for the April Fools' Day 2018 event (Go-Go-Gadget Channel Description!) and April Fools' Day 2022 (Please get your merch (link in channel description)).

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_-_Pocket_Hello_Kitty;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.Missing: Not sure if the unknown PicMix images have links (could not find them).   "Main Theme" is not an actual track, as Pocket Hello Kitty does not have any music. Instead, the rip plays "Hello Kitty" by slayyyter, with it mashed up with "ANTONYMPH". Additionally, the visuals display a slideshow of images related to Sanrio.  At the start, the visuals show a pink background with Hello Kitty at the bottom right. The text says "My sanriocore compilation / Music: Hello Kitty by Slayyyter / Subscribe for more sanrio! / Enjoy the video ^_^". At 0:14, the PicMix image "Hello Kitty Pink Glitter" is shown. At 0:22, the PicMix image "Sanrio Cinnamoroll Flying in the Sky" is shown. At 0:29, an unknown PicMix image featuring several Sanrio characters is shown. Desmond the Moon Bear is shown at the bottom between Keroppi and the Beatcats. At 0:36, a frame from "Level 974 (Kitty's House) - Escape the Backrooms" with a Glitterfy filter applied is shown. At 0:44, this GIF of Hello Kitty is shown. At 0:51, this GIF of Kuromi is shown. At 0:58, an unknown PicMix image featuring several Sanrio character plushes is shown. A plush of Momiji Inubashiri from Touhou 10: Mountain of Faith is shown between Kuromi and My Melody. At 1:05, an unknown PicMix image featuring the Windows XP desktop, Fluttershy in the center, and several Sanrio characters is shown, with the former two elements referencing the "ANTONYMPH" music video. Additional characters added include Noelle from Deltarune (left, right-center, referencing "Field of Hopes and Dreams (PAL Version) - Deltarune"), Gir from Invader Zim (bottom left, right), and Suneo from Doraemon (1979) (top right). At 1:13, the PicMix image "pompompurin loves macaroon" is shown. At 1:19, gameplay footage of Hello Kitty from Tomotoru: Hello Kitty Happy Life is briefly shown, with the clip "Kitty" from the Growing Up With Hello Kitty episode "Talking On The Phone" played as well. At 1:20, gameplay footage of the ROBLOX game My Hello Kitty Cafe is shown, with a headless character dancing in front of the titular cafe. At 1:27, an image of Hello Kitty is shown, with the background and Hello Kitty's bow cycling through several colors. At 1:31, more gameplay footage of My Hello Kitty Cafe is shown, with the headless character from 1:20 jumping in the entrance area of the Hello Kitty 50th Anniversary minigame. At 1:35, this edited image of My Melody from Tomotoru: Hello Kitty Happy Life with a Glitterfy filter applied is shown. At 1:42, this image of Hello Kitty is shown. At 1:49, this image of several Sanrio characters with ROBLOX Man faces added to them and a Glitterfy filter applied is shown. At 1:56, this image of Hello Kitty from Tomotoru: Hello Kitty Happy Life is shown. At 2:04, an unknown PicMix image featuring several Sanrio characters is shown. The GIFs "noelle dansen" and "blonk" from "Field of Hopes and Dreams (PAL Version) - Deltarune" are added in the center and bottom right respectively, and My Melody's face is changed to resemble the Awesome Face / Epic Smiley. At 2:11, an unknown PicMix image featuring Kuromi and several instances of My Melody is shown. The instance of My Melody at the bottom left has the ROBLOX Woman Face added to it, and the sideways instance of My Melody on the right has the Silly Cat's face added to it. At 2:17, this image of Hello Kitty is briefly shown, with the clips "Hello" and "Kitty" from the Growing Up With Hello Kitty episode "Talking On The Phone" played as well. At 2:18, the PicMix image "yeey" is shown. The Silly Cat is also added at the top left. At 2:25, the PicMix image "hello kitty Virgin Mary" is shown. At 2:33, an image of the advertised game is shown, with its gameplay being shown as well. At 2:40, an unknown PicMix image featuring several Sanrio characters and the text "See you soon!" is shown. At 2:46, this GIF of several Sanrio characters is shown in front of another unknown Hello Kitty image.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Spooks_-_Friday_Night_Funkin':_Vs._Alfie_-_Megamix!;;;The rip plays gameplay footage of a modded version of the level with the following changes, most of which reference Five Nights at Freddy's:  The lyrics and melody are changed to "Stuck Inside". Pooky's vocals, including all other jokes sung by him, are original. The onscreen captions for Pooky's verses are also changed to match. The background is changed to resemble the inside of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, with The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 in the rightmost drawing. In addition, the background characters are changed to Bonnie, Freddy Fazbear, Chica and Foxy. Pooky is recolored to be purple, referencing William Afton. At 1:14 and 3:06, the melody of the synth line changes to "Megalovania". At 1:27, Boyfriend's verse changes to a few melodies in quick succession: the "Saster motif" (a musical motif used in most Friday Night Funkin' songs by the composer Saster), "Gadget Room" at 1:35, and "Kyun! Vampire Girl" at 1:39. At 1:59, Pooky sings "MEGALOVANIA (ULTIMATE MIX) - Smash Bros. Ultimate Cover" by JunoSongs, with "beneath the skull and gym shorts" replaced with "this blanket's a disguise, i report!", while Boyfriend sings "Megalovania". At 2:16, Pooky's backing vocals sing "The Noble Haltmann". At 2:23, Pooky sings "Witch Doctor", while Boyfriend sings "Athletic Theme", referencing "Athletic Theme (PAL Version) - Super Mario World". As is customary with most Friday Night Funkin' rips, the player character suddenly dies despite winning the level. Pooky in this rip.The background animation.

As is customary with most Friday Night Funkin' rips, Boyfriend dies despite winning the level.

The background graffiti is changed to reference various hololive members, all of whom are from the JP branch (from left to right, top to bottom): The Tatsunoko symbol used by Kiryu Coco A potrait of Bibi, meant to represent Tokoyami Towa Two star and heart symbols, meant to represent Mano Aloe A shooting star, meant to represent Hoshimachi Suisei A Nousagi, meant to represent Usada Pekora A SSRB with big eyes like Whitty's, meant to represent Shishiro Botan A Nekko, meant to represent Momosuzu Nene The character "草" (kusa) A jester hat surrounded by a club and heart, meant to represent Omaru Polka Yukihana Lamy's flower pin A potrait of Neko, meant to represent Minato Aqua A potrait of Hoso-inu, meant to represent Inugami Korone A potrait of Listener, meant to represent Koronesuki, Korone's fanbase. The HoloX logo As is customary with most Friday Night Funkin' rips, Boyfriend dies with blue balls despite winning the level. The arrow key notes spritesThe background used in the mod.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Waterfall_(Short_Mix)_-_Undertale;;;At the start, the rip displays the TikTok video "school rooftop funk shuffling  @Leader Omega Nugget  @Omega Pasta  credits @Reborn Omega Teabag   #chips  #omeganugget  #burpingnugget  #omegachipswithcrab  #omega  #omegaverse  #fyp  #viral" by wenochipswithcrab, with the music of the TikTok video, "School Rooftop Funk" by DJZRX, having the melody changed to the advertised track. At 0:09, the TikTok video, with the exception of Omega Crab Lays, disappears, leaving just Omega Crab Lays on a square plane. At 0:10, they appear confused and the "Huh?" meme sound effect from ROBLOX plays.  At 0:12, the coordinates "(-20.6, 0, 56.3)" appears to the left of Omega Crab Lays, as the rip zooms out away from Omega Crab Lays. At 0:14, the zoom stops at The numberphile fusion with James Grime / Jay Eazy from the rip "Main Theme (Alternate) - e", who is on the same plane with the coordinates "(2.7, 0, 1.8)", referencing the first four digits of "e", and is standing in front of a screen with the upload schedule for rips at the time, which was 2 hours per rip. At the screen, The numberphile is scheduling certain rips that have their titles censored out, with the exception of numbers, and scheduling rips based on what number they have, though says "No" to rips with odd numbers in their titles:  At 0:14, the screen shows a rip with "9" at the end, to which The numberphile says "No" to. At 0:19, the screen shows a rip with two "2"s in the title, to which The numberphile schedules it at the first "2:00" time slot from the top. At 0:24, the screen shows a rip with an "8" near the front of the title, to which The numberphile schedules it at the first "8:00" time slot from the top. At 0:28, the screen shows a rip with "3" at the end, to which The numberphile says "No" to. At 0:33, the screen shows a rip with a "Two" near the front of the title, to which The numberphile schedules it at the second "2:00" time slot from the top. At 0:37, the screen shows a rip with a "IV" at the end, to which The numberphile schedules it at the second "4:00" time slot from the top. While this is happening, at 0:20, Omega Crab Lays moves closer to the The numberphile fusion with James Grime / Jay Eazy, until the coordinates say, with most of it cut off, "(-6.9, 0, 9.8)". At 0:33, The numberphile says "Cause there's a pattern, and that pattern does hold." At 0:37, Omega Crab Lays begins singing "Cotton Eye Joe" by Rednex, which startles The numberphile, causing the fusion's y-coordinate to briefly change to "0.3", "0.7", and "0.8", as it says "No" to Omega Crab Lays. Omega Crab Lays tries singing again at 0:42, though The numberphile again says "No" to it. At 0:46, Omega Crab Lays tries singing one last time, before The numberphile pulls out an "e" tile used in the rip "Gameplay - 2048", and throwing it at Omega Crab Lays, as it distorts and is sent to the canyon background used in the "Gegagedigedagedago" series by GoLuB. At 0:49, the distorted Omega Crab Layss appears alongside a croissant character, the ROBLOX chicken nugget, and the FL Studio logo edit of the ROBLOX chicken nugget from "World 1 Map (Alpha Version) - Kirby's Adventure", who is only visible right as the distorted Omega Crab Lays appears on the desert, to which the nugget responds with JonTron saying "What?" from "Anti Drug Games", as its face changes to a shocked expression.

At 0:30, the aforementioned subscribe button green screen video is added to the visuals. Starting at 0:33, the aforementioned TikTok randomly interrupts the video, with its audio sped up and pitch-shifted to "Megalovania".  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_(Put_Mix_Name_Here_Later)_-_Five_Nights_at_Freddy's;;;Like all other "Main Theme" rips from the Five Nights at Freddy's series, this rip uses "Five Nights at Freddy's 1 Song" instead of the actual "Main Theme" track.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/You_Don't_Know_What_I'm_Sayin'!_(super_sexy_not_geyyyyyyyyyyyyyy_version)_-_Watch_paint_dry;;;"You Don't Know What I'm Sayin'!" is not a real song; this rip serves as a remastered version of the rip "You Don't Know What I'm Sayin'! - Watch paint dry". As in the original rip, it is a mashup using the instrumental of "voiceless". In this version, both the vocals and instrumental of "Gangnam Style" (and other PSY songs) are used instead of just the vocals (except 0:00-0:14, 0:28-0:43, and 4:13-4:22), with the instrumental chords and structure being rearranged to match "voiceless". The rip also features:  The "I'm a" sample from "Gentleman" pitch-shifted to the guitar riff (0:00-0:28, 1:52-2:06, 2:47-3:01, 3:44-4:22). PSY sentence-mixed and pitch-shifted to the lyrics and melody of "voiceless" (0:56-1:52, 2:34-2:47, 3:01-3:44). The "eyyyy" pitch-shifted to the guitar solo, like in the original rip (3:44-4:16). The lead instrument from "New Face" pitch-shifted to the instrumental melody (2:06-2:47). In addition, the mix name references the joke and the rip "Main Theme (super remastered not gay version) - Metal Gear Solid". It could also reference the rip "The Flintstones (super remastered not unstylish version) - LEGO Dimensions", which was the first rip during PSY Day 7.

Wii is streamed, meaning that "Overworld Theme" nevertheless had to be remade from scratch before having the Gangnam Style MIDI "slapped" on.

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Radio_-_Interactive_Buddy;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This rip plays gameplay footage of a modded version of the game with the following changes:  The advertised track is mashed up with audio clips from the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" video, which stops at 0:14. The Interactive Buddy character is replaced with Gegagedigedagedago nugget, complete with proper facial expressions and limbs. Dialogue boxes have had their contents changed to read: "WHAT?", "Help Me!!", "HELP! ME!", "Gedagedigedagedago!". The gameplay continues until 0:47, where it's interrupted by audio clips of JonTron saying "What?" from the video "Anti Drug Games" and of Kevin Hart saying "Help me, HELP ME!" from Kevin Hart: Let Me Explain, zooming in on Gegagedigedagedago's surprised face. The video then shows a spoof of Max Design Pro's "like prompt", featuring the "Super Mario in Real Life" Vine on the left and the like button on the right, except the phrase "Super Mario" replaced with sped-up audio saying "Gegagedigedagedago". The like and the Vine are then "clicked" (complementary with a Vine Boom), causing the scenery to change to a real-life recording of someone[who?] in the bathroom, experiencing the Gegagedigedagedago nugget in real life. The person stops brushing their teeth in order to take the Gegagedigedagedago nugget back to the "Gegagedigedagedago World". They then proceed to take the nugget on their hand, which "sings" a snippet of "Wares - The Way Out (Chester)" from Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon (the aforementioned track mashed up with audio clips from the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" video), and show it various real life items as “Home Sweet Home” from EarthBound plays in the background:  At 1:29, the person shows a box of Oxo Chicken Stock Cubes, grabbing one and dropping it on the table. The nugget responds, as the person explains how a soup can be made using those cubes. Gegagedigedagedago responds again, trying to say "soup". At 1:44, the person shows a strawberry. The nugget responds with a picture of StrawberryClock inside a speech bubble, to which the person responds positively, as Gegagedigedagedago does as well with a clip of "Astronaut in the Ocean". At 1:52, the person shows a McDonald's Chicken McNuggets menu page on their laptop, which shocks Gegagedigedagedago as he exclaims "WHAT?" (using the aforementioned JonTron clip). They then apologize to the nugget. At 1:58, the person shows the video “Gegagedigedagedago 5” by GoLuB, which is paused on a frame of Gegagedigedagedago's friends on their laptop, asking if it misses them, to which the nugget responds with "Help me!" (using the aforementioned Kevin Hart clip). The person then proceeds to take Gegagedigedagedago to its home. The scenery changes to a grassy field and the person lets Gegagedigedagedago on the ground. The nugget says "Thank you" (what is the sound from?) then proceeds to take off into the sky, as the camera view goes up. The video then fades to black as credits roll, featuring only one name, that being "Gedagedigedagedago", attributed to "Gegagedigedagedago".  
    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Finale_(Omega_Version)_-_Undertale;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This is a mashup set to the advertised track centered around the "Gegagedigedagedago" meme, with elaborate animated visuals mostly based on the battle against Omega Flowey, which is partially accompanied by the advertised track. The rip begins with the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" video being mashed up with and pitch-shifted to the advertised track while being displayed over the thumbnail. At 0:10, six Omega Grapes, colored and positioned to represent the six human SOULs, are absorbed by Gegagedigedagedago, as Loud Nigra is pitch-shifted to the advertised track's backing chords. The visual fades to white at 0:18. At 0:19, a montage plays of Gegagedigedagedago wandering through 3D recreations of various sequential locations on Undertale's neutral route: Ruins, Snowdin, the bridge from MTT Resort to the CORE, New Home, and the Last Corridor. At 0:37, Gegagedigedagedago encounters Nikocado Avocado, represented as Omega Flowey with the following edits:  The head has Nikocado Avocado's hair. A picture of a mukbang food pile replaces the backmost tubes. A constantly warping picture of spaghetti noodles replaces the thorny stalks. A stock photo of two bread slices, a tomato, and a fork hanging from a clothesline replaces the vines. Nikocado Avocado's arms replace the arms. Various pictures of Nikocado Avocado replace the human face on the monitor. Nikocado unleashes a blast of green gas from his mouth, sending Gegagedigedagedago spinning down. The screen then cuts to Sad Omega Nugget spinning as Pomni from The Amazing Digital Circus and Silly Cat orbit around it in a 3D spherical motion, with "Gegagedigedagedago 2" by GoLuB and a shumeezy-style starfield animation in the background. At the same time, "Pomni Song MUSIC VIDEO (The Amazing Digital Circus)" by BENJIxScarlett and the "meow" sample from Mario Paint (in reference to "Boykisser (song)" by Studi01) and Loud Nigra are mashed up with and pitch-shifted to the advertised track, as well as an unknown sample at 0:50. In addition, various Undertale-style dialogue boxes are shown:  "*Omega Nugget called out to his friends..." "*He heard voices echoing in the distance!" "*We believe in you, cowboy!", spoken by Milk. "*Don't give up now, you got this!", spoken by Chicken Wing. "*Don't forget who you are, yeehaw!", spoken by Hamburger. At 0:58, Boykisser and Pomni are absorbed by Sad Omega Nugget, who changes back into Gegagedigedagedago and flashes the colors of the various SOULs. At 0:59, audio clips of JonTron saying "What?" from the video "Anti Drug Games", of Kevin Hart saying "HELP ME!" from Kevin Hart: Let Me Explain, of the Like Timer Sound Effect (all regularly used together in Max Design Pro's Gegagedigedagedago videos), and of a stock ding sound effect play, as the text "WHAT? HELP ME!" and increasingly close shots of Gegagedigedagedago's face flash onscreen and two like buttons appear on both sides of Gegagedigedagedago. At 1:00, elements from "Cotton Eye Joe" by Rednex are added to the track as Gegagedigedagedago fights Nikocado. Nikocado sends Omega Flowey's bombs, with Nikocado's face instead of Flowey's, which Gegagedigedagedago dodges. Gegagedigedagedago then presses the "FIGHT" button and inflicts damage on Nikocado. Nikocado then sends avocados, which Gegagedigedagedago also dodges. Gegagedigedagedago presses the "FIGHT" button and inflicts damage again. The Omega Grapes, moon, and sun from “#CapCut #coems #coems🤑 #omegaverse #omeganugget #omeganuggetlover #omega” by @theofficialomegagrape then manifest behind Gegagedigedagedago and send a sunbeam into the right eye of Nikocado's head. Nikocado sends out a group of scooter-riding Nikocados, which Gegagedigedagedago dodges. Gegagedigedagedago presses the "FIGHT" button and inflicts damage again. Various Gegagedigedagedago characters, as well as the ROBLOX Man-faced Brainless Kitty from "brainless (PAL Edition) - The Club (CCC)", then manifest behind Gegagedigedagedago as the dialogue "* Omega Nugget's friends lent him their strength!" appears. Gegagedigedagedago grows in size as the dialogue "* Omega Nugget grew to an incredible size!" appears, then attacks and inflicts damage on Nikocado four times. The ROBLOX Man Face appears behind Gegagedigedagedago as he flashes with the SOULs' colors, and a vortex effect is applied to the battle as the music briefly cuts out, returning with a scream sample from "Cotton Eye Joe" as the background flashes with the SOULs' colors and a pair of flashing laser beams shoot from Gegagedigedagedago's eyes and strike the two eyes behind Nikocado's head, causing Nikocado to also flash with the SOULs' colors. Gegagedigedagedago then sings along with vocal samples from "Cotton Eye Joe", accompanied by the corresponding visuals from "Cotton Eye Joe"'s music video with a circular crop, as the dialogue "* NIKOCADO's DEFENSE dropped to 0!" appears. The rip fades out at 1:41.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Megalo_Strike_Back_(Alternate_Version)_-_I_Miss_You_-_EarthBound_2012;;;The advertised track plays normally until 0:06, where a glass-breaking sound plays and the thumbnail shatters. At 0:08, the visuals switch to the Max Design Pro version of the Roblox Chicken Nugget with the microphone from Friday Night Funkin' against the Monument Valley image used in the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" video. The Roblox Chicken Nugget checks his microphone, with a thumbs-up emoji shown and a ding sound effect played. At 0:11, audio from the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" video is then pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track, with the lyrics shown at the top. At 0:17, the visuals switch to a different part of the Monument Valley image, where the original Roblox Chicken Nugget is shown. "Cotton Eye Joe" by Rednex is pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track, with the lyrics shown at the bottom. At 0:24, the visuals to another desert image, with the Max Design Pro version of the Roblox Chicken Nugget, audio from the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" video, and lyrics at the top used again, and additional characters added to the background, including:  Happy Happy Happy Cat (left) Smurf Cat (left-center) Sad Banana Cat (center) Dancing Toothless (right-center) At 0:30, the visuals switch to this image of a Badlands spawn in Minecraft, with the original Roblox Chicken Nugget, "Cotton Eye Joe", and lyrics at the top used again, and additional characters also added to the background, including:  Pomni from The Amazing Digital Circus (left) Frisk from "UNDERTALE THE MUSICAL" by LHUGUENY (left-center) "Normal Difficulty" face from Geometry Dash (top) Bear trash can from the "O Cholera Czy To Freddy Fazbear / Freddy Fazbear Har Har Har" meme (bottom-center) Chipi Chapa Cat (bottom-right) NikoAvocado (top-right, appears at 0:34 and disappears at 0:36) At 0:37, the visuals switch to a scene from Five Nights at Freddy's: The Movie of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, with Springtrap from "FNAF MOVIE THE MUSICAL" by LHUGUENY shown at the left. "Stuck Inside" is mashed up with the advertised track and pitch-shifted to "Main Theme" from The Amazing Digital Circus, with the advertised track itself also melodyswapped with "Main Theme". The "meow" sound effect from Mario Paint is also played several times, with each occurrence accompanied by an appearance of Silly Cat from the sides. At 0:44, the background changes to the hallway from The Amazing Digital Circus. At 0:46, the background changes to the vineyard from "FNAF MOVIE THE MUSICAL", with the camera panning to reveal Springtrap from "FIVE NIGHTS AT FREDDY'S 3 THE MUSICAL" by LHUGUENY at 0:47. At 0:49, Skibidi Toilets from the series by DaFuq!?Boom! appear from the top and fall along the sides as brief samples from "Give It To Me x Skibidi Bop Yes Yes Yes" by Fiki are pitch-shifted to the advertised track. At 0:50, the Max Design Pro and original Roblox Chicken Nuggets are shown against another desert image, with the upper half of the microphone broken off, the original Roblox Chicken Nugget edited to have large eyes, and notification bells appearing from the sides, accompanied by the bell sound from the standard YouTube "subscribe button and notification bell" template being pitch-shifted to the track. Audio clips of JonTron saying "What?" from the video "Anti Drug Games" and of Kevin Hart saying "Help me, HELP ME!" from Kevin Hart: Let Me Explain are played, with the camera zooming in on the Max Design Pro Roblox Chicken Nugget with each "What?". At 0:59, the standard YouTube "subscribe button and notification bell" template appears, changing the microphone and the original Roblox Chicken Nugget back to normal. At 1:04, the visuals repeat from the 0:11 mark, except with the Monument Valley image distorting. At 1:17, the rip loops from the 0:24 mark, except with "Stuck Inside" and all related visuals replaced with "Baby", which is also pitch-shifted to "Main Theme" in reference to "Main Theme - The Amazing Digital Circus". At 1:57, the rip loops from the 1:04 mark. It fades out at 2:11.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Sand_Canyon_1_(Sigma_Mix)_-_Kirby's_Dream_Land_3;;;This is a parody of the video "SPEED OF KIRB" by SpartaYoshi, with the following changes:  The Kirby used in the video is changed to Gegagedigedagedago. The SpartaYoshi watermark on the bottom right is replaced with a spoof SiIvaGunner watermark. While, as in the original video, the rip features a mashup of a censored version of "Speed of Sound" by Tech N9ne and the advertised track, in this rip the melody of the advertised track has been changed to "Cotton Eye Joe" by Rednex. The various locations Gegagedigedagedago goes to are changed to other locations: The first stage of The Flintstones: The Rescue of Dino & Hoppy/7 GRAND DAD. The main desert background used in various Gegagedigedagedago videos. A hallway in The Amazing Digital Circus. A screenshot from ESCAPE FROM BOYKISSER. The Tengami lighthouse, though color-corrected to match the colors of the Season 8 banner. The "Field of Hopes and Dreams" from Deltarune. The Wild East from Undertale Yellow. One of the themed "Snow halation" backgrounds from Love Live! School idol festival. Gameplay of "Raft Ride" from The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening. The mall used in the "Mega Man" TikTok video promotion, with "Man walking Green Screen background" by Reizol Innovation edited in the background and one of the posters in the background edited to feature a promotional image for SiIvaGunner All-Star Summer Festival 2021: Legends of the Western Sunset. Ponyville, with the ROBLOX chicken nugget running through the Sweet Apple Acres barn with an explosion gif. The animation of The numberphile fusion with James Grime / Jay Eazy running on the e thumbnail that is on the walls and floor from "Main Theme (Alternate) - e", with James Grime's face on both the thumbnail and The numberphile edited to be angry when the ROBLOX chicken nugget goes past him. "The Warning" section of Space Station 2 from VVVVVV. Footage of people dancing with the SiIvaGunner cutout from Super MAGFest 2024. Butter Barn from Fortnite. The music video for "Astronaut in the Ocean" with the ROBLOX chicken nugget edited to have an astronaut helmet on. The Wallsocket Horseshoe in Manchester, Michigan. The bonus stage from Sonic the Hedgehog 3 & Knuckles, with the ROBLOX chicken nugget opening the gumball machine and revealing an Xbox logo, referencing "Boykisser, Pomni, & Gegagedigedagedago but it's Famous Console Startups". The Backrooms, with the ROBLOX chicken nugget stopping and looking surprised when the Kirby from the aforementioned video passes by. A hallway in Baldi's Basics in Education and Learning. The FL Studio project file of audio for the rip, with the ROBLOX chicken nugget's body changing to the FL Studio logo, as seen in the rip "World 1 Map (Alpha Version) - Kirby's Adventure". Gameplay of "The Princess's Secret Slide" level in Super Mario 64 with the ROBLOX chicken nugget pasted over the Mario icon in the top right. The Kirby from the aforementioned video running over a flat Minecraft world with the ROBLOX chicken nugget running alongside it, as the two run past several locations together. One of the backgrounds that were used on the Silentó World website. A transition from Vib-Ribbon. Beanopolis from Fall Guys. gm_construct from Garry's Mod. The title screen from My House with the title removed. A crumpled up paper background used by MatPat. Bikini Atoll from SpongeBob SquarePants. The main background of "FUNNY BUDOTS 2020". A disco floor with the following characters: Nyami and Mimi from the pop'n music series GIR-elle The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 from this tweet by @deathgobrr "Nice Brainless" from the rip "Take On Me but it's in the Super Mario 64 Soundfont (Music Video)" Silento This gif of a dancing cat At 0:37, Charlie, The Steak pops up as everything behind him blurs.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Cotton_Eye_Joe_-_Just_Dance;;;The rip opens as a mashup of "The Hampsterdance Song" and the audio from the "Roblox Chicken Nugget / Gegagedigedagedago" meme, with the audio pitch-shifted to "The Hampsterdance Song"'s vocal melody.
