 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Mad_Mew_Mew_(NY_Version)_-_Undertale;;;Following from the rip "Mad Mew Mew (NTSC Version) - Undertale" and its sequels, this is a YTPMV set to the advertised track using various sources with elaborate visuals.     Time  Jokes   0:00-0:13  "wordle rap" is pitch-shifted, arranged to the advertised track, and displayed onscreen while flipping to the music, accompanied by on-screen sing-along lyrics in Wordle's color palette.   0:06  Two duplicate images of Brainless Kitty appear as fart sound effects are pitch-shifted to the advertised track.   0:08-0:13  "More One Night", the ED to Girls' Last Tour, is synced with the advertised track, while Girls' Last Tour's ending credits sequence is displayed onscreen.   0:14-0:16  "Right Foot Creep" is pitch-shifted and arranged to the advertised track, accompanied by sing-along lyrics and gameplay footage from Become Fumo, referencing the rip "Emote: Griddy - Become Fumo".   0:30-0:34  The same gameplay footage from Become Fumo, a gif of Cirno from Become Fumo, and two gifs of Kyōko from YuruYuri in reference to "wordle rap"'s visuals are displayed in quick succession.   0:34-0:35  "Subways Of Your Mind", which is visually represented by a question mark, and "Circus", which is visually represented by the Five Nights at Freddy's thumbnail, are synced with the advertised track, referencing the rip "Circus (HQ Audio) - Five Nights at Freddy's".   0:35-0:51  "Baby" is pitch-shifted and arranged to the advertised track as "Baby"'s music video is displayed onscreen, referencing the rip "Circus (Heardle Mix) - Five Nights at Freddy's".   0:44-0:51  Images of Justin Bieber and Carbuncle from Puyo Puyo appear and have the following exchange, referencing the "Did you know that 1 in 3 people are gay?" meme.  Justin Bieber: Hey Carbuncle, did you know that 1 in 3 people lost today's Wordle? Carbuncle: guuu, gugu gugu Justin Bieber: Me neither. [The Justin Bieber and Carbuncle images are replaced with images of them staring at the viewer.]     0:52-0:59  "Made a Word!" is pitch-shifted to the advertised track, accompanied by sing-along lyrics and the LeapFrog Word Whammer Fridge Phonics Set, which flips to the track. In the background, two more images of Brainless Kitty appear and fart sound effects are once again pitch-shifted to the advertised track. At 0:53, this video briefly appears. At 0:56, a horizontally-stretched image of Ikuyo Kita from Bocchi the Rock! briefly appears. At 0:57, this image of the dog from this video by speedyboyboy briefly appears.   1:00-1:07  At 0:59, clips of Carbuncle's "Gu" noises are pitch-shifted to the advertised track as "NYR2_128_JHN_4BAR_Syrup.wav" by Monster Rap Acapellas is mashed up with the track in the background. A game of Wordle is played as Carbuncle dances in the bottom right corner. Most of the words entered are references to previous "Mad Mew Mew" rips. The words entered are:   IDOLS, referencing "Mad Mew Mew (NTSC Version) - Undertale". CANNY, also referencing "Mad Mew Mew (NTSC Version) - Undertale". JUMBO, referencing "Mad Mew Mew (PAL Version) - Undertale". VIRUS, referencing "Mad Mew Mew (FR Version) - Undertale". BARON, referencing "Mad Mew Mew (PAL-M Version) - Undertale". SILVA, which turns out to be the answer to the Wordle.   1:03-1:04  "Mega Man" is pitch-shifted to the advertised track, with Jay Eazy's promotional TikTok video for "Mega Man" sliding across the screen as well.   1:03-1:07  The opening vocals from "Free Kawaii x Happy Anime Type Beat "Joy" Anime Beat" by Roko Tensei, which is sampled in "wordle rap", are mashed up with the track.  The rip loops over once at 1:07, and again at 2:15 before fading out. In addition, the mix name references the New York Times, who bought Wordle, which "Wordle Rap" is based on.

At 1:38, the Aperture Laboratories logo appears with the motto "now never, but NOW™" appearing under, imitating the Google logo and "know what's nearby" appearing in the same manner. At 1:46, the dancing Puppy Monkey Baby appears on the right. At 1:58, the motto changes to "PuppyMonkeyBaby™/bitch I licked it so it's mine". At 2:15, the Puppy Monkey Baby slides to the left. Three codes are already pre-written when the rip starts, all of which relate to balls in the game they work in:    Code  Game  Name  Source   02C-66B-F7A  Bases Loaded  2 balls and you walk  Galoob[2]   007-E1F-3BE  Revenge of the 'Gator  Infinite supply of balls  Galoob[3]   019-A3F-D5D  Penguin Wars  Don't get hurt by balls  Galoob[4]

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Character_Select_-_Mario_Hoops_3-on-3;;;The advertised track is mashed up with "Smoke on the Water" by Deep Purple and "Celebration" by Kool & The Gang. Additionally, "Smoke on the Water"'s vocals are sentence-mixed at various points throughout the rip, with various other sources additionally interspersed to punctuate certain lyrics:  At 0:19, "Frank Zappa and the Mothers" is sentence-mixed into "SiIvaGunner and the Grand Dads". At 0:28, a clip from "DK Rap" is inserted to create the line "But some stupid with a coconut gun". Starting at 0:36, Mario voice clips from the advertised game are interspersed throughout the rip. At 0:52, "They burned down the gambling house" is sentence-mixed into "They burned down the haunted house", which is followed by "gadunk"s from "Haunted House" at 0:58. At 1:21, the line "It seemed that we would lose the race" is followed by a clip from "Win the Race" by iteachvader. From 1:23 to 1:55, the advertised track's vocals are pitch-shifted to the melody of "Smoke on the Water". At 2:04, "The Rolling truck Stones thing just outside" is sentence-mixed into "The Rolling truck Flintstones just outside". At 2:41, a clip from "Just Lose It" by Eminem plays. Immediately after, "Stadium Rave A" from SpongeBob SquarePants is added to the mashup.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Tutorial_(Part_1)_-_%CF%80;;;This rip's metadata is taken from the TimmyTurnersGrandDad rip "Tutorial (Part 1) - π", an edit of "You Reposted in the Wrong Neighborhood" by 青SHOKK (a mashup of "Casin" by glue70 and "Shake That" by Eminem and Nate Dogg) with the "Shake That" vocals sentence-mixed to the digits of π. In this rip, "Casin" is mashed up with and pitch-shifted to "Lucid Dreamer", with the sentence-mixing from the aforementioned TTGD rip being reused but also pitch-shifted to "Lucid Dreamer". This also includes Vinesauce Joel saying "Seven?" from his reaction to 7 GRAND DAD whenever the "Shake That" vocals say "Seven". Unlike the TTGD rip, the vocals of "Shake That" are paused from 0:33 to 0:44, as well as the thumbnail fading in from black at the start. Additionally, the digits are displayed one at a time starting from the top left corner each time one is said, in a similar manner to "Tutorial (Part 1) - π Music Extended" by BrawlBRSTMs3 X (an updated version of the TTGD rip), though the digits are much larger in this rip (due to only 193 of them being said). At 1:40, The numberphile fusion with James Grime / Jay Eazy from "Main Theme (Alternate) - e" and Matt Parker's face from the thumbnail edited onto the limbs of the Dancing Banana GIF associated with the song "Peanut Butter Jelly Time" are placed at the bottom of the screen. Instead of a SiIvaGunner playlist, the video description links the Numberphile channel's "Matt Parker (standupmaths) on Numberphile" playlist, similarly to e rips.       A frame from the rip.   
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Everybody's_Favorite_Subject_-_Baldi's_Basics_Classic_Remastered;;;The main melody's instruments have been arranged such that, if each note is assigned a digit in order (starting with C and continuing until all digits have been assigned), the resulting melody spells out the digits of π.

Much like the other rips of e, this references James Grime's "e (Euler's Number)" video on the Numberphile YouTube channel. The rip starts by playing the Fire in the Booth version of "Man's Not Hot" by Big Shaq. At 0:06, Big Shaq is interrupted by James Grime from "e (Euler's Number)", with the "Numberphile" logo visible, referencing The numberphile fusion from the rip "Main Theme (Alternate) - e", who speaks over Big Shaq's singing. The visuals then freeze on a shot of Big Shaq looking to his left, before panning to a shot of the booth Big Shaq is in, with Charlie Sloth replaced with James Grime, the BBC Radio 1 sign replaced with the kid from the "9+10=21" Vine, and the Numberphile logo placed at the bottom right. As James continues explaining "e" from "e (Euler's Number)", an unknown clip of Big Shaq is played, where he talks about others correcting him when they don't know everything, with pans between Big Shaq and a still of James from "e (Euler's Number)" during the simulated conversation. At 0:19, James provokes Big Shaq by implying he would have called "2 + 2" something else, prompting Big Shaq to challenge James to jump in and produce his own mixtape. When James agrees, the rip's visuals change to James rapping about "e" using vocals from "e (Euler's Number)" and occasionally pans to Big Shaq looking nervous on the side. At 1:22, Big Shaq asks if James is done, followed by James sliding left off-screen. Much like the other e rips, the playlist link is for Numberphile channel's "James Grime on Numberphile" playlist. Unlike the other e rips, the composer line credits Michael Dapaah, the real name of Big Shaq.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Title_Theme_%26_Ending_-_e;;;Much like the other rips of e, this references James Grime's "e (Euler's Number)" video on the Numberphile YouTube channel.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay_-_2048;;;This is based off the main gameplay of 2048 having the player combine the same numbers in order to form larger numbers. This begins with normal gameplay of the advertised game. At 0:06, the sound of Minecraft footsteps on gravel play as The numberphile fusion with James Grime / Jay Eazy from the rip "Main Theme (Alternate) - e" appears on the right side of the board. At 0:09, James says "E", followed by him throwing an "e" tile onto the gameplay board.  At 0:14, the gameplay resumes, with a pitched up James saying "E" playing each time the board moves an "e" tile. At several points, The numberphile jumps with cartoon sound effects to the left side or the right side of the board and adds several "e" tiles to it. At 0:30, the player combines two of the "e" tiles to form a "2e" tile, this with with a higher pitch James saying "E" playing each time the tile is moved. At 0:43, the player combining the two other "e" tiles to form another "2e" tile which are then combined to form a "4e" tile, with an even higher pitched up James saying "E" each time the tile is moved. At 1:00, the player creates one last "2e" tile. At 1:08, following the board being fully filled, lines from "e (Euler's Number)" begin playing as the player receives a game over screen.      A frame from the rip.        Another frame from the rip.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_(Alternate)_-_e;;;Much like the other rips of e, this references James Grime's "e (Euler's Number)" video on the Numberphile YouTube channel. As well as this, instead of the thumbnail, it uses an edit of the Mega Man thumbnail with only the "E" in "MEGA" visible.       A frame from the rip.   At 0:16, it cuts to an animation based on Jay Eazy's promotional TikTok video for "Mega Man", with an image of James Grime from the aforementioned Numberphile video edited over the running legs of Jay Eazy from the TikTok video, and the floor and walls being made out of the thumbnail for e. As well as this, it plays "Mega Man" with various lyrics changed to lines from "e (Euler's Number)", including several instances of Jay Eazy saying the "e" vowel sound replaced with James Grime saying "e":   Eazy, woah I was never money smart, I'm math smart Makes me more intellgent Call me Mr. Math Festival I got hella constants Shorty pi, and her circle circumference Told her get a geometry She gon' make me divide with my dog like I'm Numberphile        Another frame from the rip.   In addition, much like the other e rips, the playlist link is for Numberphile channel's "James Grime on Numberphile" playlist, while the composer line is a play on James Grime and Jay Eazy.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Snow_Room_(Alternative_Mix)_-_Five_Nights_at_Freddy's;;;"Snow Room" is not an actual track in Five Nights at Freddy's. Similar to the mixless rip, this rip uses "Snow halation". "Snow halation" is mashed up with "A LITTLE THEORIZING" by The Stupendium. At 2:41, audio from "Goodbye Internet" by The Game Theorists is briefly played, while the melody changes to "Science Blaster". At 4:00, a clip from "Game Theory Finale: Real Ending (6/6)" by The Game Theorists plays. Additionally, starting at 0:08, the text on the thumbnail begins fading out, followed by the falling snow from "Snow halation" being overlaid over the thumbnail and the lyrics to "A LITTLE THEORIZING" being displayed in the game title's font at the bottom of the screen. At 1:41, the screen is briefly made brighter, following the lyrics "You're already bright enough", with a picture of MatPat being visible on the bottom left. At 3:12, the lyrics' font changes to Comic Sans for "sans is ness", followed by the endoskeletons in the thumbnail being edited to have Ness's hat. At  4:08, the visuals slowly fade to black, with Freddy's eyes fading last.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/0%C2%B2_Battle_-_Super_Smash_Bros._UItimate;;;This is an arrangement of the advertised track in the style of and using elements from "Mania" by Madeon. From 0:12 to 0:33, "Mt. Dedede" is also quoted. At 0:36, the thumbnail changes to a parody of the single covers for songs from Good Faith, the studio album that features "Mania", with the following details:  King Dedede and the background of the thumbnail are edited to resemble the album cover of Good Faith. On the right is a gray box featuring: The Super Smash Bros. Ultimate logo on the top right, replacing the "MADEON" logo. Headers reading "GAME", "SERIES - KIRBY", and "SONG - ZEROTWO BATTLE" in the Imperial alphabet used by Madeon in various media related to his music, with "Kirby/SERIES" under the "GAME" header and "0² Battle/SONG" under the "SERIES - KIRBY" header. A halftone-filtered image of the "Fountain of Dreams" stage, referencing similar images on the Good Faith single covers. Red text reading "0² Battle" that is warped, referencing similar text on the Good Faith single covers. The ESRB rating for Super Smash Bros. Ultimate on the bottom right. The text "018 / 2018", "Super Smash Bros. Ultimate -/"0² Battle", "smashbros.com", and "Bandi Namco Studios/Sora Ltd." placed on the left, referencing similar text on the Good Faith single covers.      The modified visuals seen in the rip.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Puzzle_Room_(Rhythm_Code)_(PAL-M_Version)_-_Kirby_Planet_Robobot;;;This rip heavily references the infamous removed rip "Puzzle Room - Kirby: Planet Robobot". At the start, "Se Piscar Já Era" is pitch-shifted and arranged to the advertised track. At 0:13, the advertised track switches to "Continue?" from Felix the Cat, as the text "FLASHING LIGHTS/WARNING" appears on the top and the "да" and "нет" options from the aforementioned rip appear on the bottom. At 0:18, the hand that appears in the aforementioned rip slowly rises up to initially pick the "нет" option, before sliding to the left to select the "да" and clicking on it.  At 0:27, the visuals and audio cut to black before fading to a mashup of "Russkij Pusskij", referencing the song appearing in the original "да" option, and "Se Piscar Já Era", with the visuals of the music video for "Russkij Pusskij" and "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo" appearing over each other. At 1:06, it fades to only "Russkij Pusskij" playing, before "Se Piscar Já Era" is mixed with the "Da Da Da!" lyric of "Russkij Pusskij". At 1:28, the visuals abruptly fade to black, before cutting back to the "да" and "нет" options, though without the "FLASHING LIGHTS/WARNING", with the hand sliding to the right to select the "нет" option. At 1:30, the visuals briefly fade to black, before cutting to an edit of one of the images used in "Se Piscar Já Era" with the "Hypernova Yourself" filter alongside the text "PUTA QUE/PARIU" (a line from "Se Piscar Já Era" that translates to "HOLY SHIT"), imitating the ending of the original rip, set to a mashup of "Game Over" from Felix the Cat and "Se Piscar Já Era".  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Gourmet_Race_(NTSC_Version)_-_Kirby_Super_Star;;;This is a parody of "久本雅美の頭がカービィのBGMに合わせて爆発したようです。", a MAD featuring sources from the "Hissu Amoto San / Airmoto" meme arranged to the advertised track.  Various "Bird Up!" skits from The Eric Andre Show are pitch-shifted to the advertised track, arranged and visualized in the same manner as the original MAD. Additionally, three ASCII emoticons representing a dashing Kirby are added into the channel catchphrase, in reference to a common type of comments left in various MADs of the advertised track in Nico Nico Douga.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Black_-_Homestuck;;;This rip is a remake of "Charles Barkley - Liquid Midnightslammin' (Homestuck: Black vs QCD: Space Jam)" by Icebrigade. At the start, audio from the scene from Wabbit Twouble that Big Chungus originates from plays, slowed down to match the sample of Eddie Morton's "I'm a Member of the Midnight Crew" from the advertised track. Starting at 0:04, "Space Jam" is mashed up with and pitch-shifted to the advertised track. At 1:22, the melody changes to "Space Jam". In addition, the thumbnail is edited to contain the following:  The title is changed to read "HOMERUN" with the Spirograph on the "O" changed to a basketball. The cover of "This Oceans Charles" by Charles Barkley, a book that appears in Homestuck, is added over the image. The head of Charles Barkley is edited over most of the characters, with some tinted to match the respective character and the Charles Barkley head on Karkat Vantas edited to appear angry. The Uber Bunny's head is replaced with an edited Bugs Bunny head. Dave Strider is replaced with the basketball player from the 6th comic of sweet bro and hella jeff, recolored to match Dave and with a comic sans "sports" added next to him from 10th comic of sweet bro and hella jeff. The scalemate heads are replaced with the heads from a LeBron James dog toy. The frogs Jade Harley is carrying are replaced with Michigan J. Frog. Gamzee Makara's outline is changed to resemble Mr. Swackhammer.      The thumbnail edit seen in the rip.   
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Staff_Roll_-_Final_Fantasy_XII:_Revenant_Wings;;;This is an arrangement of "Your Turn To Roll", also known as the intro to "Campaign One: Vox Machina" and "Campaign Two: The Mighty Nein" from Critical Role, using the instruments of the advertised track.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Panoramic_Feelings_-_Katana_Zero;;;This is a mashup between "Something About Us" and "Contact" by Daft Punk with the advertised track. At 0:40, part of the bassline from "Something About Us" fades in. At 1:13, more elements of "Something About Us" are added, including the main backing melody, synthesizers, and kick. At 2:19, "Something About Us" fades as the audio from the Apollo 17 mission used in "Contact" fades in. At 2:31, the whining synthesizer from "Contact" fades in until 2:50, when the drum break from "Contact" fades in. From 2:51 to 3:07, the backing melody of "Something About Us", the drum break from "Contact", and the main chords from advertised track are all present in a mashup where after every three beats, the other elements pause to let the drum break fill the space. These elements persist throughout the rip as the mashup continues. At 3:40, the section at 3:47 of "Contact" (specifically the hi-hats every beat and the melody played by the synthesizer) are mashed up with the main chords from the advertised track, which change every other beat to match the section from "Contact". At 4:12, the piano section from the advertised track plays unedited until the end of the rip.

At 0:11, the visuals fade into a parody of the thumbnail of "The Batman: Does Riddler Actually KNOW Batman = Bruce?" by New Rockstars, more commonly known as the meme "Does He Know?", playing off the similar title with "Does Your Mother Know", with the logo shrinking to the bottom left, the text fading to DOES HE/KNOW?", and a drawing of Dr. Robotnik based off the face of Riddler from the thumbnail appearing on the right. At 2:15, Dr. Robotnik's face animates into the Riddler face from the "HE KNOWS" edit of the thumbnail with the logo flashing to the text "HE KNOWS", as a laugh of Dr. Robotnik plays.  At 2:17, it cuts to various lines of Dr. Robotnik sentenced-mixed to and playing over the "Does Your Mother Know" arrangement, as the visuals switch to a parody of the music video for "Does Your Mother Know", with Dr. Robotnik playing the piano and Coconuts, Scratch, and Grounder singing on the microphones, with all also having the hairstyles of the respective ABBA members. At 2:43, the visuals and rip fade out to black.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Raft_Ride_(Live_Version)_-_The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Link's_Awakening;;;The video starts with several SiIvaGunner team members at Super MAGFest 2024 practicing with kazoos, one of which plays Giant Steps. A cosplayer of Hatsune Miku wearing a Grand Dad hat approaches them while holding a figurine of Link from The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening (Switch) on a raft and performs the advertised track on a kazoo, leading to several laughs from the members. At the end, one of the members says "Raft Ride Live Version".  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Reservation_Lost!_-_Gaylord_National_Resort_%26_Convention_Center;;;This rip heavily references liminal spaces, which refers to empty spaces that give off a sense of strangeness to them. Throughout the rip, various shots of certain places without people in them at the Gaylord National Resort & Convention Center are shown, with a heavily slowed down and edited version of "Stand On The Clouds" by Danny McCarthy, David Travis Edwards, and Ras Kass, a stock track used in promotional videos for the Gaylord Hotel, plays in the background. At 1:26, it cuts to someone starting to run from something while the camera shakes violently and at the ground before the rip cuts to black and the music cuts out.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Old_MacDonald_Had_a_Farm_(Beta_Mix)_-_Fisher-Price_Perfect_Fit;;;This rip is a counterpart to "Old MacDonald Had a Farm - Fisher-Price Perfect Fit", but themed to MAGFest instead of children's games. Most of the visuals used are reused from the aforementioned rip. This begins much like the aforementioned rip with an arrangement of "INDUSTRY BABY", in the style of the advertised track with the vocals of the Moonies' cover of "INDUSTRY BABY" added over, and with the visuals from the original rip, though with the cutscene from Hotel Mario of Mario and Luigi entering Bowser's Seizures Palace Hotel, followed by the game's ending credits, playing on the bottom right. At 0:04, it begins with the first slander of the aforementioned rip, though with the Withered Foxy jumpscare from Five Nights at Freddy's 2 briefly playing over. At 0:09, an Action Movie FX missile exploding animation plays over as new slanders with a theme of MAGfest are displayed.    Time  Text  Visual  Explanation   0:09  Heboyi when he realizes his set has been hacked by the Fisher-Price hacker for a 2nd time  A Sad SpongeBob / Spunchbop edited sequence.  Heboyi's Chipspace set had a running gag where the "Fisher-Price hacker" would play some of his Fisher-Price Perfect Fit rips.   0:14  Original rip fans when they realize it's personalized  The OMG Cat GIF.  Viewers watching Heboyi's set live at MAGFest expected to see the original rip "Old MacDonald Had a Farm - Fisher-Price Perfect Fit", not a special version for the convention.   0:19  Average siiva fan when it'll be a decade until they can go to the rave  A clip from the Breaking Bad episode "Ozymandias" where Walter White collapses to the ground in despair.  The rave at the top floor of the Gaylord hotel is restricted to attendees aged 21 and older.   0:24  CVS Breakfast  A clip from The Garden of Words where Takao Akizuki and Yukino Yukari make omurice.  The CVS Phamacy in National Harbor is a popular place to get quick, inexpensive food.   0:28  Washing Machine Game Fans seeing DDR Fans  Footage of Luigi's Death Stare in Mario Kart 8.  The design of maimai arcade machines resembles a washing machine.   0:33  How it feels to be a Junior Badge  Clip from KIDS of the player character walking around a large group of people with all other people avoiding close distance with the player.  Junior badges are rare and only handed to attendees aged 6-12, so an attendee wearing one is likely to feel special.   0:38  Back of the room during panels  A scene from Luigi's Mansion 3 where Luigi reads a book and immediately falls asleep.  Refers to how disinterested many people appear to be when they are more seated at the back of panels from the main stage.   0:43  Marketplace fans seeing gurshy anime women  The "Thug Tug" scene from The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie where a thug tries to goad an increasingly nervous SpongeBob and Patrick to sing the "I'm a Goofy Goober" song.  References the high chances it is to encounter people selling anime-related items, especially those related to attractive female characters.   0:48  Day 0 fans checking if registration is open Attempt Number 27  A clip from the Mickey Mouse Clubhouse episode "Mickey's Great Clubhouse Hunt" where Mickey sadly walks away.  On Day 0 of MAGFest, attendees are impatient to register their badge. The registration line doesn't open until late at night.   0:53  Day 1 Fans going to registration after sleeping in  The Beard Time Lapse GIF.  Starting around noon, the registration line becomes enormous.   0:57  18th floorers  The Donkey Kong's Sad Mine Cart Ride GIF from the Donkey Kong Country episode "Buried Treasure".  The elevators in the Gaylord get notoriously overloaded during MAGFest, and the 18th floor is the highest one to contain hotel rooms.   1:03  Game vendors when they realize no one will buy a $70 used DS game  A clip from the When she buys KFC instead of Popeyes video.  The merchandise hall at MAGFest has many obscure games at exorbitant prices.   1:07  Retro Game buyers learning about emulators  The Chef Skinner Reading a Letter GIF.  Refers to how retro games are also available on various emulators.   1:12  Bottle poachers when controller lickers enter the room  The Vince McMahon Surprised GIF.  It is often to encounter many people who will be keeping lots of bottles of water and people who lick game controllers during MAGfest   1:16  MAG Staff | SiIvaGunner Commenters  A clip from the Godzilla vs. Crocodile video.  References the "Iraq Veterans/SiIvaGunner Commenters" GIF from "7 Grand Dad Fusion Collab" that uses the same GIF.   1:21  average main stage fan  A clip from "itsmefraz episode 7" by Fraz.  "X Slander" videos usually end with an Average Fan vs. Average Enjoyer meme. In this case, the subjects are two stages that are found at MAGfest. This rip was originally showcased at the Chipspace stage.   1:27  Average Chipspace Fan  A GIF sequence of the GigaChad meme.  At 1:31, the visuals switch back the aforementioned rip, with the Fisher-Price Perfect Fit thumbnail flipping to "Hot Cross Buns | Nursery Rhymes | Super Simple Songs" by Super Simple Songs - Kids Songs pitch-shifted to the "INDUSTRY BABY" arrangement. On the last note, the thumbnail briefly changes to the "Brainless-Price Pathetic Fit" image from the aforementioned rip, before switching to an edit of the original image of the Brainless Kitty but redrawn to appear as The Joke-Explainer™ 7000, which originally appeared in "The SiIvaGunner 7th Anniversary Art Gallery", followed by the Marionette jumpscare being superimposed over the image.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_(PAL-M_Version)_-_Gaylord_National_Resort_%26_Convention_Center;;;This rip was uploaded on the first day of Super MAGFest 2024, a few hours before the POSE nightclub rave hosted by SiIvaGunner.[1] The rip plays "Stand On The Clouds" by Danny McCarthy, David Travis Edwards, and Ras Kass, a stock track used in promotional videos for the Gaylord Hotel. At 0:13, the rip becomes an electronic forró-style arrangement of the track using samples used by Os Barões da Pisadinha.

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Snow_halation_-_Love_Live!_School_idol_festival;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This is a mashup of the advertised track and the Nelly Furtado cover of "Crocodile Rock" by Elton John from Gnomeo & Juliet. Instead of the thumbnail, the rip begins with footage of μ's performing "Snow halation" from the Love Live! episode "Melody of the Heart". At 0:10, footage from the scene in Gnomeo & Juliet in which "Crocodile Rock" plays is superimposed over the Love Live! footage, transitioning into unedited footage from the scene. At 0:37, the "Cool Transition" text used in =3 is briefly superimposed over the footage to transition to the next part of the rip. From 0:38 to 0:57, the video shows several references to Season 7 events and memes in rapid succession. This section of the video acts as a send-off to Season 7, due to this being the last regular rip of the season (being followed by "One Last Chance", its soundtrack, and "...of Season 7"). Animated snow is displayed over this entire section (except for the last one, which already had snow).  At 0:38, Rodrigo Barão and Nozomi Toujou from the rip "Créditos - Toca Pisadinha", referencing The Pisadinhover, with IShowSpeed's infamous "Showing the Meat" stream playing in the background, referencing both "I Show The Meat" being introduced as a meme during the season and the Five Nights at Freddy's 3 8th Anniversary event. At 0:39, a clip of Luigi from "Super Mario Dance Bros" by JoeldinhoNoEnemies, referencing The Day of Luigi. At 0:41, horizontally-flipping footage from "Ruby Illusions - Final Boss (In-Game Version) (Beta Mix) - Sonic Mania", referencing April Fools' Day 2023. At 0:42, an image of Tito Dick over a clip of Patty Martin from Lucky Star, referencing Dick's Retribution and the Saidai Seichi Challenge, with a gif of circling birds appearing over Patty's head, referencing National Go Birding Day. At 0:44, an unknown video of an Opila Bird chase in a Garten of Banban-themed Minecraft mod, referencing the Garten of Banban 3, Garten of Banban 4, and Garten of Banban 6 events. At 0:46, Bottom G dancing from "Bumble Bee Dance #BOTTOMG #BrianMichaelHinds" by Brian Michael Hinds over the "Raft Ride" minigame and gameplay footage of Densha de GO!!, referencing the rip "Poem Panic - Tate's Journey" and the events "Raft Ride" Day and Densha de GO!! Day respectively. At 0:47, a clip of the South Park episode "Goth Kids 3: Dawn of the Posers" of goth characters on a school bus, referencing World Goth Day and South Park Day. At 0:48, a clip of the video "A SUPER Big Announcement", referencing National Go Fishing Day 2023. At 0:50, it cuts to the banner used for Bootleg Day, followed by the normal banner with PSY dancing on top of it, referencing PSY Day 8. At 0:51, the banner used for Barbie Day. At 0:52, the various banners used for Whip and Nae Nae Day Day (Part 2). At 0:53, the banner used for the ROBLOX 17th Anniversary, followed by the banner used for  the "What Makes You Beautiful" 12th Anniversary. At 0:54, sped up footage of "The Protegent Rap", referencing The SiIvaGunner Halloween Horror Special Part VI: The Cult of Proto. At 0:55, the video "Ryu from Streets™" by erarg, referencing Street Fighter Day. At 0:56, the music video for "Goomba Got Back", referencing "Goomba Got Back" Day. At 0:57, an unknown gif of workers in a factory, referencing Industrial Ripvolution. At 0:59, gameplay footage of a race starting on Frappe Snowland in Mario Kart 64, referencing the frequent ripping of "Frappe Snowland" during the return of The SilvaGunner Christmas Comeback Crisis. From 1:00 to 1:01, four gnome-related images are shown in succession:  A meme of David the Gnome with the text "HOW ABOUT I"/"SLAP YOUR SHIT". The "Slayer" meme image. Steve the gnome puking rainbows from the Gravity Falls episode "Tourist Trapped". The SoundCloud icon for "THE DJ KILLER KEEMSTAR ALBUM" by DJ Keemstar, referencing a meme about Keemstar being a gnome that originated with the Content Cop episode on Keemstar. From 1:02 to 1:04, more "Melody of the Heart" footage is displayed. From 1:04 to 1:07, more Gnomeo & Juliet footage is displayed. From  1:07 to 1:10, footage plays of the ripper displaying The Voice Inside Your Head from "Seasonal Return" on a computer, with his dialogue obscured by a Notepad window in which the ripper types "I fucking love Gnomeo & Juliet. Period.", is displayed. From 1:10 to 1:13, it cuts to a montage of various images over a crudely-stretched image of μ's' stage (panned from left to right):  The various images used for the thumbnails of the channel video game osts; from left to right, they are: Deji from "FAMILY RAP CYPHER 2016" by KSI Haiti Babii from "Haiti Babii Freestyle | Bootleg Kev & DJ Hed" by Real 92.3 LA Bowser from "Bowser Juice Infomercial" by SML Lil Yachty from "Lil Yachty Freestyle - XXL Freshman 2016" by XXL DaddySpeed from "I Show The Meat" by DaddySpeed Linkara Skibidi Toilet SpongeBob SquarePants ??? Cheezborger from Chikn Nuggit The four boys featured in "Purple Grape Soda" by roachmg777 Chuck Tamzarian edited into a catboy Drake Mickey Mouse Grandpa Joe from Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory Dr. Phil with a Guitar Hero guitar Jay Eazy Smol Nozomi edited to aim a gun at her head At 1:13, the rip flashes white to transition to a character-dedicated "Snow halation" rip with a gif of Mankini Gnome from the advertising campaign for Sherlock Gnomes in the center of μ's' stage, which plays at increasingly fast speeds in sync with the music, accompanied by three different snowfall animations. At 1:36, a popular "bukkakke" gif appears on both sides of the screen. At 2:01, Mankini Gnome fades out as the snowfall zooms out. At 2:05, Mike Stoklasa fades in as a truncated clip from the RedLetterMedia "Half in the Bag" episode "The Last Last Jedi Review" where Mike describes Mankini Gnome plays. The following captions then appear over Mike: "You can barely hear Mike because he was totally wrong. Sort of."/"Mike is so stupid." The screen then zooms in on Mike's face, then cuts back to "Melody of the Heart" footage and Gnomeo & Juliet footage. At 2:27, video footage plays of the ripper unsubscribing from SiIvaGunner. At 2:29, the character-dedicated "Snow halation" rip visual appears again, but the stage's lights are yellow, and Mankini Gnome is replaced with gifs of Gnomeo whipping and Juliet dabbing from the advertising campaign for Sherlock Gnomes. At 2:52, the screen fades with a flash of white to footage from the Gnomeo & Juliet scene. At 2:58, SiIvaGunner's hair and eyepatch are edited onto the fish, then fly off. At 3:01, "youve been gnomed.wmv" by  angie8051 zooms in, accompanied by "fart with extra reverb" by DairyOrange. The footage is then edited into reaction footage from Red Letter Media watching the ending of Resident Evil: Afterlife taken from the "Half in the Bag" episode "Resident Evil series Part 1", before ending abruptly.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Pocket_Diary_-_Kirby_Planet_Robobot;;;No elements of the advertised track appear in this rip. Instead, this is an animated parody of the plot of The SilvaGunner Christmas Comeback Crisis in the style of the "In a Nutshell" series by Solar Sands. The video goes over most of the events of the ten main episodes released at the time, using crude illustrations and text-to-speech voices for the characters. In the last split-second of the video, Grand Dad appears next to a logo for the eleventh episode, referencing how his appearance in said episode was the only thing revealed about it at the time. The choice of the advertised track, which plays in the Kirby Planet Robobot staff credits, references the significance of Kirby Planet Robobot as the inspiration for the plot of the Christmas Comeback Crisis.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Puzzle_Room_(Rhythm_Code)_(JP_Version)_-_Kirby_Planet_Robobot;;;This is an arrangement of "Lucid Dreamer" in the style of the advertised track, with the overdriven guitar from EarthBound also used as an instrument. Elements of "Russkij Pusskij" are additionally mashed up with and pitch-shifted to the arrangement starting at 0:02. The combination of "Puzzle Room", "Russkij Pusskij", and the overdriven guitar references "Puzzle Room (Rhythm Code) (Extended Ver.) - Kirby Planet Robobot", which features "Puzzle Room", "Russkij Pusskij", and "Megalo Strike Back".     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Rhythm_Route_-_Kirby_Planet_Robobot;;;The melody has been changed to "Becoming Popular (The Pony Everypony Should Know)" from the My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic episode "Sweet and Elite". At 0:29, the vocals from "The Type of Gamer Every Gamer Should Know / Becoming Popular" by The Gamer's Atlas, a parody of "Becoming Popular (The Pony Everypony Should Know)", are added to the rip as it fades out.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Ending_-_Breaking_the_Thing_at_the_Mall;;;There is no track called "Ending" in Breaking the Thing at the Mall, as the game has no music. Instead, this is a mashup of "Mega Man" by Jay Eazy and "Snow halation", with the former being pitch-shifted to the latter. During the intro, the lyric "S-R-G" is shortened to "S-G", and the sentence-mixed line "Eazy, no E" is added. The visual takes on the usual format for Character-dedicated Snow halation rips with μ's' stage panning down with animated snow as a relevant character, in this case Jay Eazy, appears on the left. Initially, the portrait sprite of Jay Eazy  from the advertised game appears. At 0:22, the screen flashes white to the music, and the sprite is replaced with a photo of Jay Eazy, switching to different photos at 0:34 and 0:36 in sync with the music. At 0:39, Jay Eazy flickers to the music. At 0:40, footage from the official music video for "Mega Man" plays with the animated snow in front of it. At 0:51, a frame of Jay Eazy from the promotional TikTok video appears, with TikTok-style singalong lyrics for the mashup appearing at the top left. At 1:01, the screen flashes white to the music, transitioning to an edit of the TikTok with Jay Eazy running down a road from the official music video for "Snow halation". At 1:06, it fades back into the character-dedicated Snow halation rip visual, with the stage lights changed to yellow, an animated still of Jay Eazy from the "Mega Man" music video, and animated TikTok-style singalong lyrics. At 1:14, the Jay Eazy photo stretches and fade-out, while "Yes Ma'am" by Jay Eazy is added to the mashup. At 1:18, another photo of Jay Eazy rises from the bottom and zooms in. Audio from the promotional TikTok is then mashed up with the track, accompanied by footage from "Snow halation"'s music video, then by footage from the TikTok with animated snow. At 1:27, "Piccolo" by Jay Eazy is mashed up with the track, accompanied by more footage from "Snow halation"'s music video, then by footage from "Piccolo"'s music video, both with singalong lyrics for the TikTok samples. At 1:33, various clips are played in quick succession: another promotional TikTok for "Mega Man", yet another promotional TikTok for "Mega Man", footage from "Piccolo"'s music video, "Snow halation"'s music video, and a reprise of the edit seen at 1:03. At 1:44, the visuals switch back to the character-dedicated Snow halation rip visual, with Jay Eazy replaced with a Mega Man 11 illustration of Mega Man. The visual pans up to the sky as Mega Man fades out, then fades to black.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_-_Mega_Man;;;There is no actual track titled "Main Theme" in Mega Man. This is a parody of Jay Eazy's promotional TikTok video for "Mega Man" done in the style of episodes from The SilvaGunner Christmas Comeback Crisis. There are also other changes made in the artwork used:  The mall display screen is changed to display the President Haltmann logo. The posters in the background are changed to feature the following: The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 and Wood Man from the SiIvaGunner All-Star Nuclear Winter Festival event. The SiIva A.I., The Voice Inside Your Head, Meta Knight, Smol Nozomi, and Santa Claus from The SilvaGunner Christmas Comeback Crisis, foreshadowing the episode "One Last Chance". The "Regal Cinemas" logo changed to "Legal". At 0:17, "Mega Man" is pitch-shifted and arranged to the rip "Here Come The Squeaks! (Alternate Version) - Kirby: Squeak Squad", a rip that was featured in the Christmas Comeback Crisis side story "I Wanna Thank Me", in the same style as the rip "Squeak Squad Theme (Kirby: Squeak Squad) (Alpha Mix) - Kirby Star Allies" with the lyric "S-R-G" shortened to "S-G".

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Christmas_Pain_in_Christmas_Town_(feat._Dave_Pino)_-_Hypnospace_Outlaw;;;Much like with the rips "SquisherZ (Aud2hsm Converter Trial) - Hypnospace Outlaw", "Awesome Rap Beat - Hypnospace Outlaw", and "Tension - Hypnospace Outlaw", this rip shows footage of a page made using the Hypnospace Productivity Suite, a page builder and music creator for Hypnospace Outlaw. The date on HypnOS' startup screen has been changed to "November 6, 1999 1-G02-234". The enforcer's desktop has the following details:  The desktop uses one of the Gray's Peak Cola Co. official Coolpunk wallpapers. Several files and applications, including HYPII's file and the SCG Soundscape Generator application, are placed around the desktop. The HSPD Enforcer Dashboard app is placed right above the right eye of the Shakespear statue sticker, referencing SiIvaGunner's eyepatch. Various stickers from the "Terry's General Store" page, specifically the "TERRYS HALLOWEEN STICKERS" pack and the stickers from the "Terry Sticker s" page, are scattered around the desktop. Seven SquisherZ stickers are also scattered around the desktop, specifically Leaka, Barfly, Oozurf, Gloyo, Mushi, Shellslop, and Hissslime. The enforcer's mouse trail is set to high and uses the "SquisherZ" sound effect from the SquisherZ Quest game. The enforcer's name is "smol". smol visits the "Coolpunk Paradise" zone and selects a page titled "Xmas Pain in Xmas Town", with the description "Music: Christmas Pain in Christmas Town/Composer: Chowder Man/Platform: HypnOS" in reference to the standard video description. The link takes smol to a Hypnospace Outlaw-style website based around "Snow halation", with the following details:  The URL of the website is "XMASPAIN", and the title of the page is "Xmas Pain in Xmas Town". The page has the snowflake trailing cursor used throughout "Coolpunk Paradise". The page plays a mashup of the advertised track and "Snow halation". The advertised track is pitch-shifted to "Snow halation" at 2:14 and 5:13. The background is of the stage that µ's perform "Snow halation" on. The top of the page has gifs of Smol Nozomi and Smol Honoka and two spinning stars, with animated text reading "Snow halation/"Christian" Rock and Roll?" in a style based on the text style from SHERRIHEALS and LOOKOUTMINISTRIES's page. Underneath are the boombox gif from the SquisherZ Quest game page, the microphone gif, and ARLAN_FER_OBBEE's "WITW Earl" Noble Smiley, as well as the text "vvv Sing along!! vvv", scrolling lyrics of "Snow halation", and HS_Music and HS_JoemanStreetTeam badges. smol scrolls all the way down until the stage is shown, redirecting to a similar page based on character-dedicated "Snow halation" rips with the URL "SNOWHALATION" and the title "Snow Halation". The page has the same image of the stage, but adds an image of The Chowder Man from the advertised track's music video on the right-hand side. At 0:55, smol moves the mouse so that the trailing cursor creates "snowfall". At 1:32, the page is reloaded to add animated snowfall to the background. At 2:30, a gif of Smol Nozomi appears on the stage. At 4:07, smol scrolls up to the top of the page, revealing a tableau of the following gifs and images that reflects the downfall of Coolpunk in the game:  Three tombstones in the foreground. The header illustration of Joeman drinking from X_NEO_ICY_X's "COOLPUNK PARADISE: OUR HOME" page, with the laughing skull gif used in "Linda's Horror Page" over his head. The "COOL" snowman gif originating from IcicleKid's page. A gif of Joeman originating from the "COOLFEST '99" page. The title gif from the "COOLPUNK IS DEAD" page over a spiral gif. In addition, various samples of other Coolpunk songs from the game are added to the mashup:    Time  Joke   4:07  "X-MAZ Medley (Coolpunk)" ("ho" and bell samples)   4:12, 4:21  "Chill It Right (Fre3zer)" ("R-R-Rhyme!" and "C'mon C'mon!" samples)   4:21  "Gotta Gotta" ("Gotta" sample)   4:34  "MxMaZZZZ" ("Merry Christmas!" sample)  At 4:28, smol scrolls back down to the stage. At 4:34, the stage turns yellow as in the original performance of "Snow halation", as gifs of all members of μ's in the style of Smol Nozomi appear on the stage, mostly in the same order as the original performance of "Snow halation", with The Chowder Man being slightly moved to the right. At the same time, the vocals of "Snow halation" are added in.  At 5:49, smol scrolls up once more to a flickering gif of Gumshoe Gooper playing the saxophone from AbbyWrites58's "Sandy 4 Leader!" page in the sky. At 6:00, smol decides to log off of HypnOS, ending the rip.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Demo_Track_3_-_Kirby_Planet_Robobot;;;The advertised track is mashed up with "Castle in the Sky" by DJ Satomi with the vocals pitch-shifted to "Meet the Flintstones" at 0:35. Starting at 0:03, various images of Smol Nozomi appear with impact text font of the respective lyrics appearing alongside each one, with most of the images being from The SilvaGunner Christmas Comeback Crisis as well as the following:  At 0:07, a frame of Smol Nozomi from the video "A Manic Announcement". At 0:09, an image of the usual banner of the Tengami lighthouse. At 0:16, the Smol Nozomi out of annotations from the video "#420AnnounceIt" briefly appears. At 0:21, drawn text is added reading "help how 2 fix" with arrows pointing to the impact font text being cut off. At 0:22, Smol Nozomi from one of the thumbnails for RIP². At 0:25, the Smol Nozomi from the rip "Wocky - Friday Night Funkin': VS. KAPI - Arcade Showdown". At 0:26, a drawn speech bubble is added reading "help". At 0:35, the Smol Nozomi and Kirby drawing from the rip "Midnight Moonlight (Forever-Sleeping Flower) - Kirby Triple Deluxe". At 0:42, it briefly cuts to "Kirby can dab." by supersonicman10 before an image of the "I Will Find You And I Will Kill You" meme with the impact font text "I DON" is shown for a frame before the rip ends.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Ned_(In-Game_Version)_-_Dicey_Dungeons;;;"Ned" is not an actual track in the game, but instead refers to the character. The rip displays gameplay footage of the advertised game, where the player character moves into the anvil space to enter Ned's blacksmith. Ned's hammering sounds are changed to sound like The Nutshack theme. The player has the modded upgrades "STOP SIGN", "COME ON AND SLAM", "SPIRIT PHONE", and "NICE SWORD". After equipping the "COME ON AND SLAM" upgrade, the player character returns to the main board as the rip ends. In addition, various elements, including the modded upgrades, reference various other Dicey Dungeons rips:  The HP number of 271828 is a reference to "e (Euler's Number)" in "Swing Me Another 6 - Dicey Dungeons". "STOP SIGN" is a reference to "Jack Black defines Octagon" in "Swing Me Another 6 - Dicey Dungeons" and "Tempting Fate - Dicey Dungeons". "COME ON AND SLAM" is a reference to "Space Jam" in "Fighting Chance - Dicey Dungeons". "SPIRIT PHONE" is a reference to "As Your Father I Expressly Forbid It" by Lemon Demon, a song from the album Spirit Phone, in "Lifeline - Dicey Dungeons". "NICE SWORD" is a reference to "mm2wood" in "Your Host For Tonight (Title) - Dicey Dungeons".

This rip served as the finale rip of the Goomba Got Back Day event, referencing the association of "Goomba Got Back" and "Predestined Fate" with VvvvvaVvvvvvr.     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Dancing_Mad_(Movement_4)_(Beta_Version)_-_Final_Fantasy_VI;;;The advertised track is pitch-shifted and mashed up with "Goomba Got Back", with instruments from "Goomba Got Back" arranged to the track. Frequently throughout the rip, AI vocals of Gaijin Goombah sing original lyrics based off "Goomba Got Back" set to the advertised track, with the AI voice additionally being used to recreate Kefka's laugh at 3:17 and 5:49. At 0:32, the melody is changed to "Goomba Got Back". At 1:43, the melody is briefly changed to "Farer of East" by SpellingPhailer, a song commissioned for Gaijin Goombah's show "Game Exchange".  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Peaches_(In-Film_Version)_-_The_Super_Mario_Bros._Movie;;;The vocals of the advertised track are replaced with sentence-mixed vocals of Gaijin Goombah, singing modified lyrics mostly referencing "Goomba Got Back". At 1:13, the instrumental of "Goomba Got Back" is added to the rip. Additionally, the visuals show a recording of the ripper's laptop screen, which moves around throughout the rip. In the background, a page with Gaijin Goombah's videos is open. Overlaid on the left is a modified version of the poster for The Super Mario Bros. Movie, with Bowser and Peach replaced with Gaijin Goombah and Akiterra Goombah, respectively, and the title changed to "The Super Goomba Got Back Movie". Overlaid on the right is an image of Akiterra Goombah next to a Golden Dash Mushroom from the Mario Kart series, with an additional image of SiIvaGunner's profile picture and a caption saying "SiIva Gunner" colored to match Gaijin Goombah's color scheme placed above it. A peach is placed in front of the screen as well, covering up part of Akiterra Goombah and is used at the end to zoom in to black.       A frame from the rip.   
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Baby_Got_Back_-_SingStar_'90s;;;The vocals of the advertised track are sentence-mixed to sing "Goomba Got Back", with the instruments also arranged to more resemble "Goomba Got Back". In addition, stock sound effects are used in place of the Mario sound effects, all of which reference how the original Mario sound effects were used in manner to reference certain innuendos, and the turntable scratching is replaced with scratching that uses an unedited clip from the advertised track.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Bereavement_(Alpha_Mix)_-_Undertale;;;"Goomba Got Back" is pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track. All of these are sources associated with VvvvvaVvvvvvr, due to "Goomba Got Back" being a meme on VvvvvaVvvvvvr.    Time  Song  Source   3:26-3:26  "Baby Got Book"  Dan Smith   4:26-4:42  "Reese's Puffs Rap"  RV & Terrance   4:42-4:59  "GHOST RIDE THE WHIP!"  PeanutButterGamer   4:59-5:21  "Scatman's World"  Scatman John  From 5:22 to 5:24, "Baby Got Back" by Sir Mix-A-Lot, "Baby Got Book", and "Goomba Got Back" are pitch-shifted to the track in quick succession. From 5:29 to 5:49, a cover of the lyrics from "Shawty Wanna Fuck" by Maxeboy that reference "Baby Got Back" are sung to the melody of the advertised track.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_-_Sailor_Moon;;;Instead of the static thumbnail, the thumbnail in the rip itself displays the animated logo seen in-game, with the light reflections moving horizontally. Additionally, the rip contains visuals resembling renders from the website "Nod to the Rhythm". The visuals use a photo of Gaijin Goombah, which nods to the melody of the rip. At 0:33, the captions change to a yellow Comic Sans font. At 1:03, the captions change back to the first style with the text "Look at this Galoomba".

"Goomba Got Back" is pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track, additionally being sentence-mixed to sing new lyrics. At 2:33, the original "Goomba Got Back" vocals are also mashed up, also bit-crushed to match the advertised track. At 4:31, an unknown source is briefly added to the advertised track.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Beware_the_Forest's_Mushrooms!_-_Hot_Goomba_Blowjob;;;"Goomba Got Back" is mashed up with and pitch-shifted to the advertised track. The mashup is accompanied by YTPMV-esque visuals using the "Goomba Got Back" video. The visuals repeatedly reference the "VIP先生"/"VIP Teacher" meme, which is based on "Mariotropolis" by tamat, a video that features a cover of the advertised track and footage from the 1927 film Metropolis. In addition, parts of the rip are based on the "VIP先生" YTPMV "キーボード先生 (Beware The Forest's Keyboard)" by Grambam36. At 0:14, the "Goomba Got Back" footage is in black and white, while the robot Maria from the Metropolis scene featured in the "Mariotropolis" video with Aki's head fades in.  At 0:22, the "Goomba Got Back" footage is again in black and white and intercut with the audience from the Metropolis scene. At 0:24, an "old film grain" filter is added to the footage, while a text card reading "ガイジン先生" ("Gaijin Teacher") with Aki appears. At 0:28, the ピンキー姉貴 Niconico meme appears, followed by Aki's face and the two together, accompanied by the audio associated with the meme ("Impact-38" from the Nash Music Library) being pitch-shifted to the advertised track. At 0:29, Aki twerking appears over footage from the Metropolis scene. At 0:31, soyjaks are pasted over the audience in the Metropolis scene. At 0:32, another "ガイジン先生" text card appears.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Better_Call_Saul_(Alternate_Version)_-_Breaking_Bad:_Criminal_Elements;;;Like the previous rip of this track, the rip does not actually contain any music from Breaking Bad: Criminal Elements. Instead, this is a mashup between the instrumental of the Better Call Saul main title theme by Little Barrie and the vocals of "Goomba Got Back", which are arranged and pitch-shifted to resemble those of the theme, along with the backing synth from "Goomba Got Back". The rip ends with audio of Gaijin Goombah saying "Jiggle physics", followed by high-pitched voice clips of Chuck McGill from the Better Call Saul episodes "Pimento" and "Chicanery" respectively, saying "--is sacred! This is not a game!" and "I am not crazy!" The pairing references the association of "Goomba Got Back" with VvvvvaVvvvvvr and the "Chuck" playlist on VvvvvaVvvvvvr that is used to post rips featuring Chuck McGill's testinomy.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Old_MacDonald_Had_a_Farm_-_Fisher-Price_Perfect_Fit;;;This is an arrangement of "INDUSTRY BABY" by Lil Nas X and Jack Harlow, in the style and instruments of the advertised track with the vocals of "Lil Nas X, Jack Harlow - INDUSTRY BABY | Official cover by The Moonies" by The Moonies Official added over. At 0:04, the visuals switch to a parody of the ""Fans Explaining" Montages / X Slander" meme, which often uses "INDUSTRY BABY" as a background song, with a theme of childhood-related subjects.     Time  Text  Visual  Explanation   0:04  Slide fans on a particularly sunny day  A GIF of a sped up skeleton burning with flames surrounding it.  Many playground slides are made of metal and become very hot when constantly exposed to sunlight.   0:09  Tag fans learning about pronouns  A clip from the Breaking Bad episode "Ozymandias" where Walter White collapses to the ground in despair.  Tag is a playground game in which several players chase other players and "tag" them, often by exclaiming "Tag, you're it!"   0:14  How macaroni looks when it's glued to a paper plate  A clip from The Garden of Words where Takao Akizuki and Yukino Yukari make omurice.  Macaroni art is a type of art commonly produced in arts and crafts classes in kindergarten.   0:19  Toy blocks fans seeing lego fans  Footage of "Luigi's Death Stare" in Mario Kart 8.  Toy blocks and Lego are two types of construction blocks popular with young children.   0:24  Hopscotch fans  Footage of a tumbleweed in a desert.  Hopscotch is a playground game which involves a player hopping through a pattern of spaces drawn on the ground.   0:28  How it feels to be a booger picker  Gameplay footage from KIDS, where the player character walking around a large group of people with all other people avoiding close distance with the player.  Nose picking is a common practice in young children which is considered socially deviant.   0:33  See N' Say fans when the cow goes moo  The "OMG Cat" GIF.  See 'n Say is an educational toy which, in the most popular iterations, depicts farm animals and their associated sounds.   0:38  Calmest interaction in four square  Footage of Reggie Fils-Aimé and Satoru Iwata fighting, taken directly from the Mii Fighter reveal trailer for Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and Wii U.  Four square is a playground game involving four players bouncing a ball to one another across four squares.   0:43  Back of the class during story time  A scene from Luigi's Mansion 3 where Luigi reads a book and immediately falls asleep.  It is common in kindergarten for teachers to read stories to their students, which can be boring for some children.   0:48  Swing fans after getting the biggest jump known to man  "eggman 3.gif" from the album 7 Somari Dad.  Swings are a common toy in playgrounds which frequently cause injury from excessive swinging.   0:52  Speak & Spell fans entering naughty words  The "Thug Tug" scene from The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie where a thug tries to goad an increasingly nervous SpongeBob and Patrick to sing the "I'm a Goofy Goober" song.  Speak & Spell is an educational toy made to help children learn spelling and pronunciation. The slander pokes fun at how often many people attempt to have Speak & Spell say naughty words.   0:57  Velcro fans when they're forced to switch to shoelaces  The "Sweaty Speedrunner" GIF.  Velcro shoes are a type of shoes commonly worn by young children before learning how to tie shoelaces.   1:02  Pokemon card fans when they came to trade but all they got was the teacher taking their belongings  A "Sad SpongeBob / Spunchbop" edited sequence.  The Pokémon Trading Card Game is a popular card game with young children, and teachers may confiscate their cards if they cause too much disruption during class.   1:07  Play-doh eaters when crayon munchers enter the room  The "Vince McMahon Surprised" GIF.  Play-Doh, a modeling compound, and crayons are often ingested by children due to their colorful appearances.   1:12  Crush-havers learning about cooties  The "Chef Skinner Reading a Letter" GIF.  Cooties is a fictional disease said to be spread when a child touches another child of the opposite sex.   1:16  iPad kids when confronted with 2+2 and the correct answer isn't skibidi  A video of Brainless Kitty.  "iPad kids" is a colloquial term for children from Generation Z and Generation Alpha. Skibidi Toilet is a popular meme among these demographics.   1:21  Groundskeepers when they have to fix the teatherball for the 5th time this month  A clip from the Mickey Mouse Clubhouse episode "Mickey's Great Clubhouse Hunt" where Mickey sadly walks away.  Tetherballs are a common toy in playgrounds which are frequently damaged due to strong force or injuries.   1:26  The bus ride home after everyone gets their recorders  The "Donkey Kong's Sad Mine Cart Ride" GIF from the Donkey Kong Country episode "Buried Treasure".  Recorders are musical instruments commonly used in elementary school music classes.   1:31  Seesaw fans in 20 years when they're asked why they can't have children  The "Anton Ego's Flashback" GIF.  Seesaws are a common toy in playgrounds which often cause injuries to children's groins.   1:36  Snack time fans when no one will trade for their carrots and broccoli  A clip from the "When she buys KFC instead of Popeyes" video.  Prescribed times for snacks are customary in schools, where vegetables are commonly served, which many children dislike.   1:40  Fans of troublemaking being struck with the fear of god  This "Screaming Jerma" GIF.  Many parents often use the fear of a god's punishment as a way of teaching children not to misbehave.   1:45  Teeball fans when they start picking grass and eating dandelions  This "Kid Hit By Giant Beach Ball" GIF.  It is common for children to become distracted by picking grass and dandelions during playground sports in grassy fields, such as tee-ball.   1:50  "I love to go on CoolMathGames!"  A clip from Toy Story 2 of an aisle full of identical Buzz Lightyear toys.  Cool Math Games is an online hosting site containing browser games commonly played by children. The slander pokes fun at how often many people visit Cool Math Games.   1:55  Hide and seek fans waiting for someone to find them  The "Beard Time Lapse" GIF.  Hide-and-seek is a playground game in which players hide to be found by designated seekers. A hiding player can stay hidden for a long time if they are secluded well enough.   2:00  Jack in the box fans after the 10th time  This "Startled / Shocked" GIF.  A jack-in-the-box is a children's toy consisting of a music box which reveals a figure after being sufficiently cranked.   2:04  Rubick's cube fans explaining how solving it is actually super simple  The "Ibai Llanos Explaining Things" GIF.  Rubik's Cubes are a popular 3D combination puzzle toy. Enthusiasts have developed several simplified methods for solving them quickly.   2:09  Silent reading time haters after one paragraph  A clip of Mr. Bean waiting from the movie Mr. Bean's Holiday.  Kindergarten classes often have designated times for silent reading, which can be boring for some children.   2:14  Teachers when they're asked where cursive went  The "Confused Travolta" GIF.  Cursive handwriting is often taught in school, though it is no longer a required teaching in many places and has declined in popularity over the years.   2:19  average mary had a little lamb fans  A clip from "itsmefraz episode 7" by Fraz.  "X Slander" videos usually end with an "Average Fan vs. Average Enjoyer" meme. In this case, the subjects are two popular nursery rhymes, "Mary Had a Little Lamb" and "Hot Cross Buns", the latter being a frequently used meme on the SiIvaGunner channel.   2:24  Average "Hot Cross Buns" Fan  A GIF sequence of the "GigaChad" meme.  At 2:29, the visuals switch back to the Fisher-Price Perfect Fit thumbnail, with "Hot Cross Buns | Nursery Rhymes | Super Simple Songs" by Super Simple Songs - Kids Songs pitch-shifted to the "INDUSTRY BABY" arrangement and the visuals flipping to go with the pitch-shifting. On the last note, the thumbnail changes to a crude edit; the text is edited to read "Brainless-Price Pathetic Fit", Brainless Kitty appears six times in the red trim and over the hyphen, and another image of a cat appears in the lower-left with a speech balloon that says "Hey!".       The thumbnail edit used at the end of the rip.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Life's_Like_a_Dollhouse_(Beta_Mix)_-_Tate's_Journey;;;This is a mashup of "Bumble Bee", a song frequently used in TikTok videos about Andrew Tate, and "Barbie World" by Nicki Minaj and Ice Spice from Barbie. This combination references "Life's Like a Dollhouse - Tate's Journey", which uses "Barbie Girl" by Aqua, which is directly sampled in "Barbie World".  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Human_Music_(Netflix_Edition)_-_Pocket_Mortys;;;The rip is just one second of silence. This is a subversion of the large amount of "Hot Cross Buns" rips being uploaded at the time of the rip's upload, due to "Hot Cross Buns" being an obvious joke to make with "Human Music". Under the channel catchphrase, an additional line has been added to the video description, "Joke: Hot Cross Buns", to dispel any ambiguity. The use of the abnormal mix name "Netflix Edition" also alludes to this, as most of the "Hot Cross Buns" rips around this time also used abnormal mix names. The inclusion of a "Joke:" line could also reference the rip "Beloved Tomboyish Girl (Alpha Mix) - Touhou 6: the Embodiment of Scarlet Devil".

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Underwater_Stage_(Unused)_-_Jerma's_Big_Adventure;;;There is no actual unused track titled "Underwater Stage" in Jerma's Big Adventure. At 0:44, Jerma985 singing "I Gotta Feeling" from his "Karaoke Night" stream is mashed up with "Drowning". At 0:54, the "Devil May Combust" clip from Jerma985's Devil May Cry stream plays, cutting off "Drowning". At 0:56, a clip from Jerma985's "WarioWare - Do It For Him" stream plays. At 1:00, "Drowning" resumes, again mashed up with the "Giant Enemy Spider", "AA EE OO", and "Jerma Rap" clips. At 1:15, another clip from Jerma985's "WarioWare - Do It For Him" stream  plays.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Raft_Ride_(Tesla_Arcade_Version)_(Unreleased)_-_The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Link's_Awakening;;;The melody has been changed to the main theme from Foodfight!. The mix name references similar mix names on OMORI rips of the unreleased PS Vita and Nintendo 3DS releases.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Ocean_-_Tate's_Journey;;;This is a recreation of "ron in the ocean" by TristoneThePerson (which itself is an animated version of "Friday Night Funkin' Vs. Bob - Folders In The Ocean (Ron x Astronaut In The Ocean Mashup)" by Furscorns) with the following changes:  "Bumble Bee" by Bambee replaces "Astronaut in the Ocean" in the video as the song that is pitch-shifted and mashed up with "Ron" from the Friday Night Funkin' mod literally every fnf mod ever (Vs Bob). At the start, TristoneThePerson is replaced with Tristan Tate, while the text in TristoneThePerson's watermark has been changed to "TRISTAN THE TATE". The brief visual of "Lego Ron" at 0:01 is replaced with an equivalent visual of a "Lego Tate" from "(NEW) ANDREW TATE LEGO RARE (READ DESCRIPTION)" by mr.bricc on Ebay with the caption "OMG LEGO ANDREW TATE". Instances of Ron throughout the video (except for the first, which is edited to not move to match the rip's mashup) are replaced with Andrew Tate, while a drawing of Grand Dad pops up from the bottom at 0:02 as Vinesauce Joel's reaction to 7 GRAND DAD is briefly played. The Wendy's logo at 0:07 is replaced with an image of "Tate's Bake Shop Chocolate Chip Cookies". The vocals of Boyfriend at 0:07 are changed to sing "Bumble Bee". The composer credit list contains references to Andrew Tate as well as the various jokes in the rip:  Tristan The Tate refers to the text found in the rip. Topgscorns is a combination of Top G, a term used to refer to Andrew Tate, and Furscorns, the creator of "Folders In The Ocean". Masked Alpha Wolf refers to Masked Wolf, the artist of "Astronaut in the Ocean", as well as the "alpha male" concept in reference to Andrew Tate's position as a manosphere influencer. Average Tate W-ildy is a combination of the "Average Tate W" meme and Wildy, the composer of "Ron".

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Guns_-_Friday_Night_Funkin';;;This rip plays gameplay footage of a modded version of the level with the following changes:  The advertised track is mashed up with "gec 2 Ü" by 100 gecs.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Hello%2C_Happy_Kingdom_-_Super_Mario_RPG_(Switch);;;The rip is a remake of "YTPMV - Scrub Scrub Scrub by King Harkinian" by NeoNintendo, a YTPMV that mashes up voice clips from Link: The Faces of Evil and Zelda: The Wand of Gamelon with the Super Mario RPG version of the advertised track. The rip arranges the same vocal clips into the same sentences as in "Scrub Scrub Scrub", using the advertised track as the backing music. Compared to "Scrub Scrub Scrub", the background music and sound effects from Link: The Faces of Evil and Zelda: The Wand of Gamelon have been removed, and techniques like pitch shifting and audio stretching have been applied to make the voice clips more closely match the music. Some additional elements have been added:  At 0:30 to 0:40 and 1:32 to 1:43, additional voice clips of King Harkinian can be heard in the background. At 1:12 to 1:43, King Harkinian is laughing in time to the music. At 1:55 to 2:15, Morshu's "mmm" voice clip is pitch-shifted into the melody of the advertised track. At 2:25, edited voice clips from author Don Beveridge's "Customerization Seminar", covered by RedLetterMedia in the Best of the Worst episode "Best of the Worst: The Black Spine Edition", are mashed up with the advertised track before the track fades out.

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Underworld_Map_Fusion_Collab;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.Missing: Missing two songs, one from SpongeBob Atlantis Squarepantis (DS), and one from a Senran Kagura title, as well as several visual descriptions.   The video begins with grayscale footage of Doraemon: Gigazombie no Gyakushuu's opening cutscene, accompanied by an original arrangement of "Underworld Map". At 0:27, the scene where Doraemon meets the game's protagonist in Doraemon: Gigazombie no Gyakushuu is displayed, and another original arrangement of "Underworld Map" begins playing. The overworld sprites of the protagonist, Doraemon, and Nobita Nobi then appear one by one, and several locations from Doraemon: Gigazombie no Gyakushuu scroll by in the background. The characters walk off-screen and the Doraemon: Gigazombie no Gyakushuu logo, accompanied by the text "- Underworld Map - Fusion Collab" descend into view, and remain in place for a majority of the video. Like most Fusion Collabs, this collaboration features a single track (in this case, "Underworld Map") played in other styles. Most feature a titular 8-bit pixel character drawn in the style of the style of Doraemon: Gigazombie no Gyakushuu's overworld sprites walking across the screen. At 17:21, the video fades to black before playing an edit of "Doraemon no Uta" (the opening theme to the original 1979 Doraemon anime), with its instrumental rearranged into "Underworld Map". "Doraemon no Uta"'s lyrics have also been replaced with original lyrics related to Doraemon: Gigazombie no Gyakushuu. The edit is accompanied by footage from Doraemon: Nobita and the Birth of Japan 2016 and captions displaying the lyrics.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Critical_Stop_(Service_Pack_2)_-_Windows_XP;;;This is an arrangement of "BIG SHOT" from Deltarune in the style of "Error" by Crystal, sampling several Windows XP sound effects including the advertised track. Several different vocal samples are used throughout the arrangement to imitate the vocal samples in "BIG SHOT". Starting at 0:25, "The Protegent Rap" is used. At 0:32 and throughout, a clip of Bonzi Buddy saying "Wow" is played at various pitches. From 1:15 to 1:30, the vocals from "Berdly vs Bill Gates. Epic Rap Battles: Video Games vs History." by Legend57 Rap Battles are added to the arrangement.

The rip ends with a clip of Katy Perry saying "Sex", followed by several Vine booms.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/PlayStation_Startup_(SCPH-1001_Version)_-_Console%2FBIOS_Music;;;This rip is both based on and heavily references My House. The rip begins with footage of the normal PlayStation startup. At 0:20, it cuts to the title screen of a modded version of Doom with the text "IF YOU HAVE A COPY OF THIS/YOU ARE NAUGHTY" added over the main menu, as an arrangement of the title screen song from Doom II plays using elements of the advertised track. The player begins the game and spawns into a demake of the house section of My House. An arrangement of "Entryway at the End of Time" from My House plays throughout the level. After spawning in, the person enters the house to fight off the various demons that are in the house, though finds that none of them move or attack him. At 2:00, they begin to encounter several doors that slide backwards instead of sideways, playing off the doors opening properly in the actual mod as one of the first signs that something is changing. At 3:23, the person heads back upstairs, only to notice a demon has respawned and several doors have disappeared, with blank walls cutouts in their place. At 3:55, the person begins to leave the house, briefly stopping to check for any differences before he completes the level by hopping the fence and stepping on the end-of-level teleporter. This causes the game to freeze before cutting to black, leading to a "ERROR F-WIPE NOT FOUND/PRESS X BUTTON TO CONTINUE" screen with the title music playing. At 4:51, it cuts to black again before fading back into the house level at 4:57, with the person going through the level again as the arrangement of "Entryway at the End of Time" plays and they encounter similar things they encountered the first time. At 5:25, the person picks up ammo. At 7:29, the person tries to exit the level again after clearing out the house, but finds that the teleporter no longer works. At 7:46, they decide to go back into the house to search around. At 8:04, the person goes into the bathtub to find a deep hole in it before the game freezes again and cuts to black, referencing a similar event that can be found in My House. At 8:19, it cuts to the player in The Poolrooms, one of the other sections of the map, including a section that resembles one of the art pieces by Jared Pike. The music switches to "memory=entryrrrr/////" from My House. At 9:02, the person climbs up a spiral staircase which leads to a door at the top. When the person tries to enter, it brings them to the sky section, which is supposed to feature a wedding ring but strangely doesn’t here. At 9:49, the person heads down another hole which leads to another crash. It then cuts to a similar crash screen as before, though the text is changed to "ERROR MAP02 NOT FOUND/CONTACT SEELER ERROR CODE-736".

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Desolate_Underworld_-_Five_Nights_at_Freddy's_3;;;No elements of the advertised track are present. Similar to "Trailer Theme - Five Nights at Freddy's 3" and "Main Menu - Five Nights at Freddy's 3", the rip instead emulates crudely-made YouTube Poop fan videos made by kids in the 2000s. It features "Spreingtrep" (a crude version of Springtrap from the advertised game based on the Spoderman meme), Sanic (colored to resemble its Sonic.exe counterpart), and King Harkinian from the CD-i Zelda games going to Bready's grandma's house to scare her.

Additionally, the video uses an edited version of the thumbnail with Bald Bull replaced with an illustration of Freddy Fazbear wearing boxing attire.      The image used in the rip   
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Introducing_Bald_Bull_-_Punch-Out!!;;;No elements of the advertised track are present; the title only reflects the rip being a prelude to "Bald Bull - Punch-Out!!", which was uploaded directly after. This rip contains an original arrangement that quotes elements of "Circus" and "Music Box" from Five Nights at Freddy's, and "Five Nights at Freddy's 1 Song". Additionally, instead of the thumbnail, the video uses an illustration of Freddy, Bonnie and Chica with the Punch-Out!! logo in the bottom left corner. This references the rip of the same name on GilvaSunner, which similarly uses an illustration of Bald Bull.      The image used in the rip

Rick Astley has a recorder instrument edited next to his mouth, referencing the common use of "Hot Cross Buns" as an aid in teaching the recorder.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/The_Raft_Ride_of_Terror;;;This is a "spooky" orchestral remix of "Raft Ride", with original vocals performed in a campy Bela Lugosi-inspired vampire voice. The remix has a layer of white noise to make it sound older. With each loop, the vocalist sings the "lyrics" to a different "Raft Ride" rip: "Raft Ride - The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening" at 0:07, "Raft Ride (cgbzelda.com Build) - The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening" at 0:30, and "Raft Ride (NTSC Mix) - The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening" at 0:53. At 1:15, a stock scream plays. The description includes the remix's lyrics. The line "The Raft Ride never ends" is a reference to various comments left on Raft Ride rips, which in turn reference the line "THE RIDE NEVER ENDS" from the RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 creation Mr. Bones' Wild Ride.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/%22POWER%22_of_%22NEO%22;;;This is an original remix of "Power of "NEO"" from Undertale that is cut comically short in a similar manner to the rip "Power of "NEO" - Undertale". The remix is given a lengthy buildup with Mettaton's "oh yes" voiceline being played at 0:20. The intro ends at 0:22, and like the original rip, it then gets cut off after 2 seconds by the explosion sound effect that plays when Mettaton NEO is defeated. The YouTube upload of the remix contains an additional 2 minutes of silence to give the illusion that it's a full remix of "Power of "NEO"". The album version removes this.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Bonus_Fleent;;;This is an original remix of "Bonus Screen - Super Mario World", with the melody off-key like the original. At 1:09, a sped-up Loud Nigra plays as the remix fades out.     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Metropolis_Zone_(According_to_a_13_year_old_with_a_laptop);;;At the start, the sounds of a schoolyard play in the background, and footsteps are heard. We hear a person sit down and start typing on a keyboard. A click is heard, and the opening of the rip "Metropolis Zone - Sonic the Hedgehog 2" plays with it edited to sound from a laptop speaker. At 0:17, the sound of someone's reaction to the rip plays, with them saying "Hey, wait a second... is this real?" At 0:24, it turns into a remix of the aforementioned rip with additional elements from "Rivulets" (from Sonic Before the Sequel) included. At 1:14, a brief sample of Vinesauce Joel's reaction to 7 GRAND DAD plays faintly, coinciding with the usage of "Meet the Flintstones".  At 1:21, it becomes a remix of "Downpour" from Sonic Before the Sequel, with the main melody of "Metropolis Zone" from Sonic the Hedgehog 2 included. At 2:03, it becomes an arrangement of "Prismatic" from Sonic Before the Sequel. Due to "Prismatic" originally referencing "Green Hill Zone" from Sonic the Hedgehog, several songs related to other "Green Hill Zone" rips are also referenced:    Time  Joke  Source   2:17  "Totino's"  Tim & Eric   2:23  "Fuck You"  CeeLo Green  The appearance of "Green Hill Zone" and "Totino's" references "Green Hill Zone Act 1 - Sonic Mania", while the appearance of "Fuck You" references the rip "Green Hill Zone - Super Smash Bros. Brawl". At 3:04, the melody changes back into "Metropolis Zone" from Sonic the Hedgehog 2. The remix then slowly returns back to the person's reaction to the rip: "Oh wait that's so cool, what? It's real? Ha ha! Aww it was secretly in the beta all along! Maybe? Ok, what else is there?" At 3:23, the person selects another rip which turns out to be the rip "Hill Top Zone - Sonic the Hedgehog 2", with the person reacting with "Oh" right before the remix ends.
