 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_-_Five_Nights_at_Freddy's_3;;;Like all other "Main Theme" rips from the Five Nights at Freddy's series, this rip uses "Die in a Fire", a song by The Living Tombstone about the advertised game. At the start, a seizure warning spoofing the content warning in Five Nights at Freddy's 3 is shown, reading "SEIZURE WARNING! This rip contains flashing lights, loud noises, and lots of jumpscares!". At 0:03, "Se Piscar Já Era" by SORRIZO RONALDO is mashed up with the instrumental to "Die in a Fire", with the thumbnail pulsing to the melody. At 0:18, the visuals to "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo" slowly fade in. At 0:32, the vocals from "Se Piscar Já Era" are sentence-mixed to sing "Die in a Fire", with the following additional visual changes:  The visuals from "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo" are shifted onto the monitor screen in the main office from the advertised game. The watermark that appears at the bottom left of "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo", which depicts an animation of Scorpion from Mortal Kombat dancing, is replaced by Springtrap, who is now doing the popular TikTok dance "Kolors" instead. The accompanying watermark text is changed to "SPRINGRONARMADILHA", mixing Springtrap and SORRIZO RONALDO's names and the literal translation for "trap" in Brazilian Portuguese. When the camera screen is pulled down, SORRIZO RONALDO's face is overlaid and edited to resemble the Phantom animatronics. The night and hour indicators in the top right are translated to Brazilian Portuguese. The lyrics to "Die in a Fire" are shown on-screen, written in a direct phonetic transcription in Brazilian Portuguese:AI HOUPE IU DAI IN A FÁIERHOUPE IUL BI STÁBIN DE HÁRTEHOUPE IUL GE SHÓTE EIN ESPÁIERHOUPE IUL BI TEIQUEN APÁRTEHOUPE DIS IS UÁT IUL DESÁIER At 0:49, the visuals change back to the thumbnail, except with the game name changed to say "500 Fotos Por Minuto", referencing one of the vocal samples used in "Se Piscar Já Era", and pulsing to the melody. At 1:01, the visuals transition to the Night 1 mini-game from the advertised game, with Freddy Fazbear replaced with a depiction of SORRIZO RONALDO in the same style. At 1:06, the visuals from "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo" are faded in the background again, before transitioning to the visuals from 0:32-1:01 again.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Fortress_-_Metal_Gear_Solid:_Portable_Ops;;;At the start, elements of "Raft Ride" are arranged to the advertised track.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Horror_(Original_Mix)_-_ROBLOX;;;The rip contains a poorly edited video of a top ten list of horrors, with the advertised track playing in the background. 10 characters (mostly from horror games) are listed, with their 'jumpscare' following after (exceptions being Banban and Papyrus):  builderman (from ROBLOX) Hellish Banban (from Garten of Banban 3) Banban (from Garten of Banban) Papyrus (from Undertale) Golden Freddy (from Five Nights at Freddy's) Bonnie the Bunny (from Five Nights at Freddy's) Huggy Wuggy (from Poppy Playtime) Freddy Fazbear (from Five Nights at Freddy's) Nabnab (from Garten of Banban 2) Springtrap (from Five Nights at Freddy's 3) Honorable mentions:  Jumbo Josh (from Garten of Banban) The Mimic (from Five Nights at Freddy's: Security Breach: RUIN) Papyrus' section is edited very badly, as he's initially given the name Sprigny Wingy and his proper name shows up during the jumpscare warning (his supposed jumpscare also doesn't show up). At #1, builderman (AKA David Baszucki) is shown to be a werewolf. This is a reference to a brief period of time (in late August 2023) where the david.baszucki ROBLOX account's avatar was changed to be a werewolf.  
    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Horror_(In-Game_Version)_-_ROBLOX;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This rip is mainly a recreation of a Family Guy meme of unknown origin (first known instance is a tweet by WitchDoctorDB). The advertised track plays faintly in the background. The melody of the Christian hymn "Amazing Grace" has been added. The visuals show footage of random ROBLOX gameplay clipped together, all involving characters dying or falling, with a shocked ROBLOX character interrupting every couple of seconds. At 0:39, "roblox inaproprite plase 2!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!.wmv" by Micheal P is shown.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/OMORIBOY_-_Item_Asylum;;;This is a spoof of the YTPMV "OMORIBOY the PIRATE!!! ☠️☠️☠️" by UUN4, which the advertised track is taken from, with the following changes:  The lead samples are replaced with samples from "Raining Tacos" by Parry Gripp. In addition, the samples are visually depicted in the upper right in the style of the "SOY" sample from the original YTPMV, using footage from "Raining Tacos - Parry Gripp & BooneBum" by ParryGripp and with the text "TACO". The main visuals are replaced with footage of the OMORIBOY emote from the advertised game, taken from "OMORIBOY (Item Asylum Emote) Side-by-Side Comparison" by Blooky. The Soy container in the top left sample is replaced with Bloxy Cola, with the accompanying "SOY" text changed to "COLA". The "BASS" sample on the bottom left is replaced with a ROBLOX Space Sandwich and its accompanying "nom nom nom" sound effect. The "ARP" sample is replaced with a default ROBLOX head and the old ROBLOX "oof" sound. The heads used for the readalong lyrics are replaced with a ROBLOX taco. At 0:20, the dancing soyjak footage is replaced with the visuals from the ROBLOX segment of "Caramelldansen Fusion Collab". The rip loops at 0:38. It fades out at 1:17.

At 0:50, ":3" in the same typeface appears in the bottom left and slowly zooms into the middle of the screen. The rip loops at 0:56. It fades out at 1:55.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Rave_DJ_-_Tower_Defense_Simulator;;;Several sources are mashed up with the advertised track, with the rip playing the original source's visuals, a recreation of the original source's visuals in ROBLOX, or other related visuals. Throughout the video, the Rave.dj logo appears at the bottom right.  At the start, "The Fall of Jake Paul" by Logan Paul ft. Why Don't We is mashed up with the advertised track, with the music video of "The Fall of Jake Paul" shown as well. Rave.dj-style credits appear reading "The Rave Of Dj Paul / Phoqus & Full Song Ft. Why Do Not We / 2023 Rave. Inc", with the incorrect credit for "The Fall of Jake Paul" taken from actual Rave.dj mashups featuring the song. At 0:10, the visuals switch to "The Fall of Jake Paul - Roblox Music Video" by KML Cyber. At 0:11, an image of Logan Paul's dog Kong da Savage in a ball pit is shown at the top left, while the vocals recreate the "Little bong" edit from the Rave.dj mashup "Barbie Jake Paul" by Ash. At 0:18, Inugami Korone saying "Wow" replaces the bark, with visuals from this clip of Inugami Korone shown at the top right. At 0:22, "Barbie Girl" by Aqua is mashed up with the advertised track, again in reference to "Barbie Jake Paul", with the visuals switching to "Aqua - BARBIE GIRL (Roblox Music Video)" by Veroet. "Kyoto" is also mashed up with the advertised track. At 0:28, "Greedy Greedy" is mashed up with the advertised track, with the visuals switching to the music video of "Greedy Greedy". At 0:31, the music videos for "Greedy Greedy" and "Barbie Girl" are shown on the left and right sides of the screen, respectively, with both songs mashed up with the advertised track. At 0:33, the first Ray William Johnson clip used in "Rock My Forum" by Xarlable is mashed up with the advertised track, with the associated visuals briefly shown in the background. At 0:34, "The Joker vs FRED - Discord Rap Battles! (ft. Snakebite126 & GamingPlush64)" by DISCORD RAP BATTLES is mashed up with the advertised track, with the music video shown as well. At 0:44, the visuals briefly switch to "Fred [YTP]". At 0:47, the visuals briefly switch to gameplay footage of Fred Figglehorn's Haunted Pizzeria Survival Horror. At 0:56, "Buss it Down" by Big Shaq is mashed up with the advertised track, with the music video shown as well. At 1:07, "Shake" by IShowSpeed is mashed up with the advertised track, with the music video shown as well. At 1:08, the music video for "Buss It Down" is shown again in the background, with its vocals also mashed up with the advertised track. At 1:18, an Advice Dog meme with Skrillex and the caption "YO SKRILL / DROP IT HARD" is shown on the right in sync with the line from "Kyoto". At 1:19, "You're Mine" by DAGames is mashed up with the advertised track, with the music video shown as well. Starting at 1:30, I'm a Gummy Bear (The Gummy Bear Song)" by Gummibär is mashed up with the advertised track, with the video occasionally shown as well. At 1:41, "Son Diss" by Enes Batur is mashed up with the advertised track, with the music video shown as well. At 1:50, "Astronaut in the Ocean" is mashed up with the advertised track out of sync, with the music video shown as well. At 1:52, the visuals switch to an edit of "pinkie just had sex!!!!!!!!!!" by theburninice1, with Masked Wolf as Pinkie Pie, Ray William Johnson as Twilight Sparkle, and Chikn Nuggit as Gummy (referencing "dinnern't" by Robomi), as the same Ray William Johnson clip briefly plays.

The mix name and length of the rip were most likely chosen to deceive viewers into thinking it would be an arrangement of "Dancing Mad".

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Purple_Grape_Announcement;;;The video begins with a parody of Sans' genocide route speech from Undertale, before the final attack, but with Silentó instead. A mashup of "The Choice" from Undertale and "Watch Me (Part 2)" by Silentó plays in the background. The text is displayed through notepad from Mac OS. At 1:49, the window is moved off-screen and a hand appears from below the "MERCY" box, accompanied with a punching sound effect, meaning the option's selection, which is then moved to the text box, onto "Spare 2", and "confirming" the selection. Silentó then continues his speech, before being cut-off by a clip of Chuck Norris shooting, from the movie Lone Wolf McQuade. The video then changes to the album cover, with made-up credits rolling, and a line "geeettttttt nae nae'd!!!", as a reference to sparing Sans, and several "Name Description" lines, accompanied with "geeettttttt nae nae'd!!!", a track exclusive to the album. Near the end, a few lines are advertising SiIvaGunner's Bandcamp page. At 2:13, a picture of Linkara-AtopTheFourthWall appears from the bottom of the video and is then flipped horizontally to the music.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Peaches_-_The_Super_Mario_Bros._Movie;;;This is an original cover of the advertised track, except with modified lyrics mostly referencing "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)". At 0:10, a piano faintly plays the melody to "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)"'s instrumental. At 0:31, various elements from "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)" are mashed up with the advertised track's instrumental.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Lifelight_-_Super_Smash_Bros._UItimate;;;This plays "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)" with the lyrics mostly changed to an AI voice of Silentó singing the lyrics of the advertised track. The chords of "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)" are also changed to match the ones from the advertised track. Instead of the thumbnail, it uses a version of the thumbnail with the Super Smash Bros. Ultimate logo changed to a gif of Silentó dancing and the background changed to have a purple tint, referencing this gif. At 2:58, the gif enlarges before disappearing.       A frame from the rip.   
    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/We_Are_Number_One_-_Undertale_3;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This uses the track "Whip Are Naember One", a mashup of "We Are Number One" and "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)", with a couple of additions.  At 0:05, the meow from "guy holds cat up to doorbell camera cat proceeds to say mggaow" by weehoohaha plays. At 0:29, "Give It To Me x Skibidi Bop Yes Yes Yes" by Fiki & Timbaland is added. Various visuals jokes are also used throughout:  At 0:05, an image of Robbie Rotten appears over the thumbnail with the caption "HI/LAZY TOW". At 0:06 and throughout, it cuts to the music video for "We Are Number One" with Silentó dancing edited over it at various points. At 0:09, it cuts to a clip from the LazyTown episode "Dancing Duel". At 0:11, an image of Silentó's mugshot after being arrested for assault with a deadly weapon appears during the lyric "Kill it". At 0:13, a demotivational image of Sportacus begins to fade in right as he appears with the caption "Explota culos/nunca supe como se escribe". At 0:16, it cuts to a low quality gif of Robbie Rotten dancing from the Adobe Flash game LazyTown: Get Up and Move over a set of gif backgrounds from the Silentó World website. At 0:18, it cuts to an unknown video of MindofJson dancing with Silentó edited in the middle. At 0:21, faint text reading "first i slide", referencing a lyric from "Watch Me (Part 2)" briefly appears. At 0:25, an image of The Grinch edited to be red is added in the bottom middle. At 0:28, the cannonball collides into a still of Steve Harvey with a cake pop of himself on STEVE. At 0:29, a low quality image of a toilet is added over the hole, as the same picture of someone's teacher from "Main Theme - Undertale 2", edited to have a long neck, comes out and "sings" with an MSPaint ellipse mouth in the manner of "Green Day - Boulevard of Broken Dreams - Smiley Face..." by kentdoddsproductions, referencing the "Skibidi Toilet" meme. At 0:32, it cuts to "Silento Watch me part 2 Dance" by BMIKE ROB with the text "#WATCHMEPART2CHALLENGE" on the top, with Robbie Rotten from the "Don't Let Your Kids Watch It!" meme switching it to "WAVE GANG PURPLE FLOWERS" by frank white. At 0:35, the opening text from "Purple Grape Soda" by roachmg777 begins to fade in, before it cuts to "skibidi toilet" with dancing gifs of Silentó and Robbie Rotten added on either side. At 0:39, the video then cuts to "Lil Nuggit (Original Chikn Nuggit Song)" by Chi-Chi, referencing how the Liked videos playlist has two instances of "Lil Nuggit" placed in between dozens of the original "skibidi toilet" video. At 0:42, it briefly cuts to the Chikin Nuggit meme image used on one of the banners after the upload of the rip "Hidden Headquarters - Toree 2". At 0:44, it cuts to a high contrast image of Linkara.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Eye-catching_-_Derpixon_x_FNF;;;The rip plays gameplay footage of a modded version of the level (specifically its "SFW" difficulty) with the following changes:  The naked person from the mod, as well as with June and Charlotte during the third section are replaced with Silentó dancing. The advertised track is mashed up with "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)". In addition, June and Charlotte's vocal melody are changed to "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)". The opponent logo at the bottom is replaced with Silentó's mugshot after being arrested for assault with a deadly weapon. When it reaches the far left side of the screen, the logo is replaced with a viral nude photo mistakenly thought to be Silentó. The mid-song transitions now read "HE CAN DO IT", "NOW WATCH HIM", and "CAN YOU DO IT".  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Theme_(Original_Version)_-_Five_Nights_at_Freddy's_2;;;Like all other "Main Theme" rips from the Five Nights at Freddy's series, this rip uses "It's Been So Long", a song by The Living Tombstone about the advertised game. This rip is a mashup of the instrumental to "It's Been So Long" and "Touchin' on My" by 3OH!3. Additionally, during the second loop of "Touchin' on My"'s chorus, the beep from the aforementioned song is arranged into the melody of "It's Been So Long", while various words in "Touchin' on My" are respectively replaced with audio clips: the "fuck" from "Yankin" at 1:12 and 1:22, the "dick" from "Who's been drawing dicks?" at 1:15 and 1:25, a note from "the new rick rolld" at 1:16 and 1:27, the "op" from "Gangnam Style" at 1:18 and 1:28 and the "fuck" from "Fuck Bees" at 1:19 and 1:29. The rip ends with a Vine boom sound effect.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Tobias_Gregson_-_The_Great_Detective's_Great_Foe_-_The_Great_Ace_Attorney:_Adventures;;;The advertised track is mashed up with "INDUSTRY BABY" by Lil Nas X and Jack Harlow. From 1:01 to 2:13, several visuals with relevant text are also overlaid over the thumbnail in succession, most of which describe Herlock Sholmes' antics in the advertised game, referencing the ""Fans Explaining" Montages / X Slander" meme, which uses "INDUSTRY BABY" as one of its background songs. The slander is meant to be from the perspective of Tobias Gregson, who is frequently the subject of both Sholmes’ antics as well as humiliation.     Time  Text  Visual  Explanation   1:04  herlock sholmes coming into a delicate crime scene  The "Wide Putin Walking / IT'S HIM" meme.  Sholmes often casually enters crime scenes without permission from Scotland Yard.   1:06  sholmes preforming his investigation (he is being as careful as possible)  The "That's It? That's the Lost Episode?" meme.  Sholmes will often appear to get too close to delicate areas and evidence during his unwelcome investigations.   1:09  sholmes pulling out the most goofy invention imaginable to "solve" the case  The "Link finds X" meme.  Sholmes is an inventor, and his inventions were often crucial to Ryunosuke in both investigations and trials despite most people in London not comprehending them.   1:12  sholmes coming up with the most batshit insane answer to the mystery of the crime  The "Brain Blast Jimmy Neutron" meme.  Sholmes will often come to ludicrous conclusions during his deductions, which Ryunosuke will have to correct.   1:14  sholmes explaining the logic that lead him to his conclusion  The "Ibai Llanos Explaining Things" meme.   1:14  the innocent person sholmes just got arrested  The "Sad SpongeBob / Spunchbop" meme.  At least twice in the games and allegedly several times in universe, Sholmes’ deductions lead to the wrong person being suspected of a crime.   1:19  sholmes leaving to go work on another asinine case  The "Hob4s Man Flying Away" meme.  Sholmes will often leave the scene as quickly and unexpectedly as he arrived.   1:22  sholmes chilling in the most logical place at the crime scene  The "Majima Everywhere" meme.  Sholmes often first appears during an investigation either in disguise or hiding in an extremely ridiculous place, for no apparent reason.   1:25  the great deduction  The "Mario dancing Michael Jackson" meme.  Refers to Sholmes’ “Logic and Reasoning Spectacular”, involving various poses and dancing motions while stating his deductions, called a “dance of deduction”   1:27  the foreign law student listening to all of this  The "Kanye's Blank Stare" meme.  Refers to Ryunosuke, the protagonist     1:30  ryunosuke listing all of the reasons sholmes is wrong  The "Spongebob Squarepants To Do List" meme.  Refers to the point just before Course Correction occurs, where Ryunosuke and Susato point out the logical flaws in Sholmes’ deductions   1:33  sholmes after hearing all of the reasons he's wrong  The "Nikocado Punching Car Seat" meme.   1:36  course correction  The "Yakuza Disco Minigame / Friday Night" meme.  During Course Correction, Ryunosuke joins Sholmes in posing and dance moves for fun   1:38  deduction complete  The "SpongeBob Multitasking" meme.  Refers to how Ryunosuke does most of the work in correcting Sholmes’ deductions, but Sholmes brushes it off as what he meant to say all along, avoiding expressing proper gratitude to Ryunosuke   1:41  all of sholmes claims about a person somehow being right  The "The Square Hole" meme.  During the deductions actually seen in game, Sholmes does actually point out suspicious people, points of interest, and motives, but for all the wrong reasons   1:42  most logical herlock sholmes deduction  The "Spike Glitch" from VVVVVV.  Repeating the joke that Sholmes’ deductions are ridiculous   1:46  sholmes when he meets two random foreigners  The "Welcome Door" meme.  Sholmes immediately takes a liking to Ryunosuke and Susato and invites them to stay and hold their law office in his flat, in spite of most other people being bigoted or suspicious toward the two due to racism against Japanese people.   1:48  me getting ready to read the adventures of herlock sholmes  The "Luigi Falls Asleep" meme.  Gregson often insists that Iris’ short stories based on Sholmes’ cases are rubbish and paint him and Scotland Yard very poorly, though Iris gives him royalties for use of his likeness, which he welcomes.   1:51  sholmes trying to remeber people he should know  The "Winnie the Pooh Think" meme.  Sholmes will often insist he’s completely forgotten a person he already met, sometimes after a day or so.   1:54  sholmes checking how much money he has  The "Money Empty" meme.  Sholmes is frequently broke due to his spending habits, so Iris’ short story sales are the biggest contribution to things such as rent and heating costs   1:57  sholmes when he trys fish and chips (he is cringe and therefore doesn't like it)  The "Jet Bean Killer Bean" meme.  Gregson loves fish and chips to the point of obsession, which is a frequent stereotype of Londoners. Sholmes never references fish and chips, but Gregson hates Sholmes anyway, so the joke suggests he would assume that Sholmes hates his favorite food.   2:02  herlock sholmes  The "Nerd Pac-Man" meme.  One more insult directed at Sholmes from Gregson’s perspective.   2:05  iris wilson  The "Gigachad" meme.  As referenced above, Iris gives royalties from short story sales to Gregson, so he will often fall over himself to praise and placate her despite his hatred of her roommate and story protagonist Sholmes.

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/The_Fall_Of_Jake_Paul_-_Logan_Paul_Adventure;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This is a mashup of "The Fall of Jake Paul" by Logan Paul ft. Why Don't We with "Barbie Girl" by Aqua, referencing "Barbie Jake Paul" by Ashley, a RaveDJ mashup of the aforementioned songs. The mashup is accompanied by faux-RaveDJ visuals featuring the music videos for both songs, the site's watermark, and the following titles (which include the incorrect credit for "The Fall of Jake Paul" from "Barbie Jake Paul"):   The Barbie Of Girl Paul Aqua & Full Song Ft. Why Do Not We 2023 Rave Inc.   In addition, the mashup is accompanied by onscreen lyrics in the same style as those from "The Fall of Jake Paul"'s music video. Various other jokes are interspersed throughout:  At 0:41, the rip recreates a moment from "Barbie Jake Paul" where the automatic editing makes it sound as though Logan Paul is saying "Little bong". At 0:44, footage from "SML Movie: Heartbroken!" is displayed. In addition, "brother" and "his" are replaced with sentence-mixed "Barbie" and "her". At 0:51, a clip from "Test animation: Uh... Momiji Inubashiri plays a flute or something" by Daniel Renard plays instead of the dog bark from "The Fall of Jake Paul". At 0:55, footage from "DWARF MAMBA'S FIRST TIME DRIVING! (100+ mph)" is displayed. From 1:03 to 1:17, footage from "I CHANGED?!", three unknown Logan Paul videos and the music video for "2020" by Logan Paul is displayed. This sequence is repeated from 2:33 to 2:48. At 1:23, 1:31, 2:54, and 3:01, the footage from "The Fall of Jake Paul" has a pink and flat filter applied to it. At 1:41, the word "team" is replaced with a sentence-mixed "dick", a joke previously used in "Koopa Cape (JP Version) - Mario Kart Wii". From 1:51 to 2:03, "The Fall of Jake Paul" is repeatedly edited to repeat the phrase "That's fucked up". At 1:52, footage from "So Sorry.", Logan Paul's apology video for his infamous Aokigahara vlog, is displayed over the line "When the contract dies, so does their career, it ends". At 1:56, footage from "HEAD IN TABLE SCARE PRANK (FREAKOUTS)" plays. At 1:58, footage from "If Skibidi Toilet Was A Barbie Girl #shorts" by Carlie HD is displayed. At 2:00, footage from the music video for "Unha de Gel" by Os Barões da Pisadinha is displayed over the line "So you had to replace them with some Spanish twins?". At 2:03, footage from the music video for "It's Everyday Bro" is displayed over the line "It's every day bro, do you give up at night?". From 2:10 to 2:14, footage from two unknown Logan Paul videos is displayed. At 2:14, footage from "I Wanna Thank Me - A SiIvaGunner Christmas Comeback Crisis Side Story" of Snoop Dogg pointing his gun at Nick Crompton is displayed. At 2:26, pictures from Gary “King Pokémon” Haase's Instagram of Haase and Logan Paul holding Barbie dolls are displayed. At 3:03, a clip from the music video for "The Rise of The Pauls" by Logan Paul ft. Jake Paul plays.

    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/The_Real_World_-_Tate's_Journey;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This is a mashup of "Bumble Bee" by Bambee, a song frequently used in TikTok videos about Andrew Tate, and "Go West" by Pet Shop Boys. At 0:05, unknown audio from Andrew Tate plays. The thumbnail at the start is shown in grayscale. At 0:05, it fades into an image of Valdimir Lenin speaking to a crowd in Red Square, which zooms out to reveal Lenin's face replaced with the "Andrew Tate Shocked Face" picture. At 0:10, it cuts to footage of the 1975 October Revolution parade, with flashing text reading "THEREALWORLD.COMINTERN" appearing on the bottom. At 0:19, the footage changes with a slide transition to the USSR flag with Andrew Tate as Bottom G from "Bottom G on Top lately😈 #BrianMichaelHinds #BOTTOMG #shorts a normal day in Barcelona" dancing over it. At 0:29, the flag changes with a slide transition to a frame from Hong Kong 97. At 0:38, it cuts to this video of Bottom G by Brian Michael Hinds, with various effects played over it including changing colors. At 0:43, it changes to sped up footage of Slavoj Žižek talking from his debate with Jordan Peterson quickly followed by a clip of Andrew Tate with a shine effect applied on. At 0:46 and 0:57, it cuts to "Man and Woman in their natural gender roles #BOTTOMG #indila #BrianMichaelHinds #tournerdanslevide" and "Bottom G in London🇺🇸 #BOTTOMG #BrianMichaelHinds #shorts #bigben #london", both by Brian Michael Hinds, with a shine and red tint applied over them. At 1:03, it cuts an unknown video with a quote from Bernie Sanders that quickly gets cut off by a slide transition to a Joe Biden quote reading "You're my bumblebee". At 1:05, it cuts back to the footage of the 1975 October Revolution parade, with the dancing Bottom G video from 0:19 appearing over and with a red tint applied. At 1:16, it cuts to black before changing to the normal thumbnail. Finally at 2:14, it briefly cuts to a image of this tweet by Andrew Tate, with the background of the image changed to a Soviet Gulag, and a circle transition effect applied over the image right before the rip ends.       A frame from the rip.        Another frame from the rip

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Scarlet_Forest_(Beta_Mix)_-_Deltarune;;;This is a recreation of the Undertime Slopper video "Free Hotdogs" using Deltarune sprites. Albert's Forest is represented by the Forest, Nigel is represented by Susie, Brian Smith is represented by Ralsei, and Frog is represented by Lancer. Dialogue is displayed through Dark World-styled text boxes, complete with each character's respective sound bite. The advertised track plays throughout. Susie reads a sign in the Forest that says "FREE HOTDOGS", and exclaims "Free hotdogs!" The view then zooms out to reveal Ralsei in a hole next to the sign, with an anvil dangling by a rope above him, with Lancer to his right. Lancer says "I got you dinner!" Susie replies "What?" Lancer laughs and says, "Watch me add my secret ingredient!" Ralsei does a take and says, "Oh, Susie! Good! I seem to have fallen in this hole. Can you help me out?" Susie responds, "Yeah, you're in a hole. A lot of trouble!" The standard "Undertime Slopper" outro then plays as the advertised track fades out.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Raft_Ride_(Irish_Mix)_-_The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Link's_Awakening;;;This is an arrangement of "Predestined Fate" in the instruments and style of the advertised track. In addition, the mix name references Terry Cavanagh, the creator of VVVVVV, being from Ireland.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Raft_Ride_(Alternate_Xbox_Version)_-_The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Link's_Awakening;;;This is an arrangement of "Mr. Patch" from Banjo-Tooie in the instruments and style of the advertised track. This rip was uploaded immediately after "Raft Ride (Xbox Version) - The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening", which features a song from Banjo-Kazooie, the game Banjo-Tooie is a sequel to; the mix name references this.  Like the previous rip, the rip's mix name and console platform refer to a nonexistent and implausible version of "Raft Ride", as The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening has never officially released or has plans to release on any of Microsoft's Xbox series of consoles, as they are a hardware and software competitor to Nintendo.      
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Raft_Ride_(Xbox_Version)_-_The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Link's_Awakening;;;The melody has been changed to "Freezeezy Peak" from Banjo-Kazooie.  The rip's mix name and console platform refer to a nonexistent and implausible version of "Raft Ride", as The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening has never officially released or has plans to release on any of Microsoft's Xbox series of consoles, as they are a hardware and software competitor to Nintendo. The usage of "Xbox Version" most likely refers to the current state of the Banjo-Kazooie franchise, as the franchise is currently owned by Microsoft.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Pequena_Doce_Abelhinha_-_Toca_Pisadinha;;;"Pequena Doce Abelhinha" is neither a track in the advertised game nor a song by Os Barões da Pisadinha, the inspiration behind the advertised game. Instead, this is an electronic forró-style arrangement of "Bumble Bee" by Bambee using samples used by Os Barões da Pisadinha.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Spaceship_Rumble_-_Tate's_Journey;;;This is an arrangement of "Bumble Bee" by Bambee in the style of "Grandpa Pickles Remastered" by dzmyo. At 0:06, the voice clip in "Grandpa Pickles Remastered" is replaced with audio of Andrew Tate speaking. The rip ends with another audio clip of Tate at 1:20. The credited composer in the description, "bottom gzmyo", is a combination of Bottom G and dzmyo.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Big_Robo_Bug_(Beta_Mix)_-_Mario_Paint;;;At 0:02, the melody and chords change to "We Are Number One". At 0:37, the melody then changes to "Bad Apple!! feat.nomico". And finally, as the rip fades out, the melody changes once again to "Gadget Room".  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Jingle_2_-_Greendog:_The_Beached_Surfer_Dude;;;The melody has been changed to "Giant Steps".  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Volcano_Theme_-_New_Super_Mario_Bros._U;;;The advertised track is mashed up with "Spitfire" by The Prodigy.  
    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/I_Love_Beijing_Tiananmen_Fusion_Collab;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.Missing: Missing source at 7:06   This rip starts with a parody of the intro of Hong Kong 97. The audio is a bitcrushed version of "I Love Beijing Tiananmen", pitch-shifted to match "Meet the Flintstones". There's also several changes to the opening cutscenes. The fusion collab itself lasts from 0:49 to 17:19. The tune is the part of "I Love Beijing Tiananmen" that is looped in Hong Kong 97. The visuals most often show an edit of the Hong Kong 97 title screen, with two figures related to the joke replacing the figures of Chin and Tong Shau Ping on the original. The text above is modified to add the words "Fusion Collab". Bear     16:58  "Redditor Too"  RainingKetchup, "OMORIBOY the SEXY!!! 🔥🔥🔥"  Omoriboy and three Soyjaks     17:03  "One-Winged Angel"  Final Fantasy VII  Cloud and Sephiroth     17:09  "Beach"  Plok  Plok and the Flea Queen     17:14  "A Cruel Angel's Thesis"  Neon Genesis Evangelion  Shinji and Gendo    At 17:20, a parody of Hong Kong 97 gameplay is shown, with the following changes.  The background is packaging art for Totino's Pepperoni pizza rolls, referencing the usage of a Chinese Coca-Cola advertisement in Hong Kong 97. Smol Nozomi and Haruka Amami replace the enemies. President Haltmann is the boss fight instead of Tong Shau Ping's head. The game over screen shows "Felix the Cat Unmasked" by Kris Balerite, also used in the Genesis bootleg port of Felix the Cat. This references the game over screen of the original game, in which a shock image of a victim of the Bosnian civil war is shown. 
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Title_Theme_%26_Ending_(Mario_7)_-_Mario_7-in-1;;;The rip begins as an arrangement of "One-Winged Angel" using the advertised track's instruments. At 1:08, the arrangement transitions into the style and instruments of "Meet the Flintstones" (TV Version), which the advertised track is based on. The vocals of "Meet the Flintstones" are sentence-mixed to recreate those of "One-Winged Angel", though with the lyrics changed to say "The Flintstones" in place of "Sephiroth".     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Ending_-_Super_Mario_World_64;;;This is an arrangement of "Thrilling! is this Love?" from Rhythm Heaven and Rhythm Heaven Megamix in the style of the advertised track. It also includes the cues (specifically the English versions) used in its stage, "Fan Club", from the games. The rip's composer refers to both Koji Kondo, the composer of Super Mario World which Super Mario World 64 is based on, and the B Button Emoji that is sometimes used on other "Boji Bondo" rips.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Intro_Theme_(OST_Mix)_-_Mundial_Ronaldinho_Soccer_64;;;"Se Piscar Já Era" is mashed up with the advertised track, while the rip displays the game's intro, with "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo"'s visuals initially superimposed into the black background. On the title screen, Ronaldo Luís Nazário de Lima's head on the left is replaced with Sorrizo Ronaldo's, while the title is edited into "Mundial Sorrizinho Ronaldo 64". The game's voiceover is additionally replaced with vocals from "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo".       A frame from the rip.   
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Doppler_Stage_-_Rockman_X3_(Genesis);;;This is an arrangement of the advertised track using the instruments from "Doppler Stage 1" from Mega Man X3.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Intro_Theme_(OST_Mix)_-_Mundial_Ronaldinho_Soccer_64;;;"Se Piscar Já Era" is mashed up with the advertised track, while the rip displays the game's intro, with "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo"'s visuals initially superimposed into the black background. On the title screen, Ronaldo Luís Nazário de Lima's head on the left is replaced with Sorrizo Ronaldo's, while the title is edited into "Mundial Sorrizinho Ronaldo 64". The game's voiceover is additionally replaced with vocals from "Mega - Se Piscar já era do Sorrizo Ronaldo".       A frame from the rip.   
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Overworld_-_Sonic_Jam_6;;;At 0:02, the rip becomes an arrangement of "Good Riddance (Time of Your Life)" by Green Day using the instruments of the advertised track.     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Title_Theme_-_Harry_Potter_OBAMA_10;;;Harry Potter OBAMA 10 is not an actual game; the rip references a notorious bootleg backpack with a recolored Sonic the Hedgehog and the text "Harry Potter"/"OBAMA"/"10". Playing off the Harry Potter/Obama/Sonic the Hedgehog combination, this is an arrangement of "Hedwig's Theme", the main theme of the Harry Potter film series, in the style and instruments of "Title Screen" from Sonic the Hedgehog, with the Obama line "They say your father was a great man, you must be what's left" from the Epic Rap Battles of History video "Barack Obama vs Mitt Romney" pitch-shifted to the melody. The composer credit is a reference to John Williams, the composer of "Hedwig's Theme," and Joe Biden, Obama's campaign running mate and Vice-President under Barack Obama's presidency.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Title_Theme_%26_Ending_-_Harry_Potter_und_der_Stein_der_Weisen;;;This is based on the unusually loud nature of the opening of the advertised track. This rip is a YTPMV-styled medley of various songs, using "音割れポッターBB", a Niconico video of a center-symmetrically mirrored image of Harry Potter on a blue background, accompanied with the earrape version of "Hedwig's Theme" by John Williams, the main theme of the Harry Potter film series. At the end of some sections, the aforementioned song plays for a brief period of time, before changing to the next one.  The visuals depend on the section and tone of the pitch-shifting. Each can have one of two versions of the Harry Potter image: first one, coming from "音割れポッターBB", for high notes and second one, coming from "音割れハリーBB.ussr", for low notes. Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.Missing:  Empty sections "Details" bit is a temporary fix, information should be integrated into each section. something like "Further details include: (bullet) (bullet)"    Time  Style  Description   0:00  Intro  The video opens with the Wii's health and safety warning. The Wii home screen is then displayed, which, in addition to the Wii's default channels, contains the following channels, all which reference previous fusion collabs: Mega Man 2 for Wood Man Fusion Collab MOTHER for Snowman Fusion Collab Cave Story for Balcony Fusion Collab Paper Mario for Paper Jams Main Theme Fusion Collab Kirby Super Star for High-Quality Gourmet Race Fusion Collab YouTube for YouTube Premiere Countdown Fusion Collab The Wii Shop Channel is selected. A banner reading "Channel Time Remaining: 13:51" is displayed above the bottom border, referencing the amount of time left in the video. The "Start" button is selected.    0:08  Wii Shop Channel  After a brief loading period, a Mii of Beedle appears, and a bit-crushed Beedle line is heard, referencing the Wii Remote's bit-crushed speaker. A list of "items" from The Wind Waker is displayed, each using a modified game thumbnail: Bait Bag (Cave Story) Arrows (10) (Pinball) Hyoi Pear (World of Goo) The Hyoi Pear is selected, prompting dialogue from Beedle:   You can't buy this anywhere else! Only here! I'm serious! Now's your chance! Buy buy buy! Buy!   The "purchase" button is selected. During the loading screen, 37 memory slots are shown to be available after purchase, the same amount of items bought in the remainder of the video. After the purchase is successful, the player's Wii points drops from 20,000 Wii Points to 18,800. Another bit-crushed Beedle line plays as the segment ends.    0:35  The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker  Referencing the previous segment, this part takes place in Beedle's Shop Ship, which has been retextured to resemble a Poké Mart from Pokémon. Beedle's model has been changed to that of a Poké Mart employee from Gen VI, and the HUD is changed to be Pokémon-themed. A Safari Ball replaces the A button and a regular Pokéball replaces the B button due to their matching color schemes. The A, B, R, X, Y and Z markers denoting the buttons are also replaced with the letters' respective Unown forms, and the Link's health is replaced by heart icons from Pokémon Puzzle League.  Link speaks with the vendor, who's voice line is replaced with a "Yeah!", sourced from Tott, a character from The Wind Waker, and he says:  "OHHHHH! A customer! Welcome to Poké Mart Ship! I deal in pretty much anything and everything Pokémon! / Do you have anything you don't need? If you do, show it to me! I'll pay top rupees for your junk! / Oh, just use (Control stick icon and Pokéball icon) to browse."  The player hovers over a Great Ball, which is priced at 30 Rupees and described as follows:  "This holds Pokémon. It's quite useful. You can't capture Pokémon if you don't have a ball like this!"  Then they hover over a Revive (3 servings), which is priced at 10 rupees and reads:  "If your Pokémon friends faint in battle, you'll need these to help them get up again. Never go into battle without them!"  Then, they scroll back to the Great Ball and purchase it, deducting 30 rupees from their total of 18,800, leaving them with 18,770    0:58  Pokémon Diamond & Pearl     1:20  Persona 2: Innocent Sin     1:40  Night in the Woods  Porkrind's Emporium is rendered in the style of the Snack Falcon of Possum Springs. The Roundabout, Smoke Bomb, Heart, and Chaser weapons/abilities are seen behind Porkrind. A slot machine resembling Ribby and Croaks' final form in their boss fight in Cuphead is to the left of the counter. Mae and Porkrind have the following exchange:  Porkrind:  Welcome!   Mae:  This place looks straight out of the 30s...   Mae:  And I thought I was getting old.   Porkrind:  Ok kid, are ya gonna buy something or not?   Mae:  I don't think I wanna shoplift here anymore, this was before my time.   Porkrind:  Shoplift? You were planning to steal from my store?   Mae:  oknicetalkingtoyoubye   Porkrind:  Goodbye.    Mae runs off-camera during her last line of dialogue. Porkrind's first and last lines are identical to his voice lines when entering and exiting his shop in Cuphead.     2:02  Cuphead  Rendered in fluid, old-style 2D animation like the source game, a vendor with blond hair and a pink gown announces "Hello!" and sits behind the counter of a burger restaurant, bobbing forward and back. A Mr. Saturn from the Mother series sits to her right, and purchasable food is located to her left. The player hovers over a hamburger, which costs 7 coins and heals 48 HP, a cup of coffee which costs 4 coins, heals 12 HP and causes the consumer to "enter a dream like trance", a bag of fries that costs 6 coins and heals 24 HP, and a can of fruit juice that costs 5 coins and "heals 6 HP". The player ultimately buys the cup of coffee, deducting 4 coins from their funds and leaving them with 15,771 coins. The vendor then thanks them. The player then enters their inventory, which displays their card, decorated with an old-style illustration of Ness. They navigate to the Travel Charm, displaying their charms. They have Travel Charm, which protects the player from paralysis, Rabbit's Foot, which does the same and adds +40 speed, and Coffee, which is described above.    2:24  EarthBound  Marnie's store from Stardew Valley is rendered in the EarthBound style. She has several pins in stock, each based on an ability card from Unconnected Marketeers: Bursting Frog for ¥4,900, based on Bursting Red Frog Snowy Snow Storm for ¥800, based on Ice Fairy Fujiwara - Blaze for ¥1,900, based on Phoenix's Tail A life pin for ¥500,000 A pin for ¥10,000 based on Physical Enhancement Jizo A pin for ¥1,600, presumably based on Vampire Fang A pin resembling Sutra of Dharmatic Power, only available through trade Each pin the player scrolls over is paired with a demonstration of the pin's abilities in the bottom right corner. The player purchases one Snowy Snow Storm, and Chimata responds with "ありがとう! ふっふっふ……" ("Thank you! Fufufufu……"), likely a pun on her last name, "Tenkyuu".    13:12  Touhou 18: Unconnected Marketeers  The video shifts to a Wii-themed version of the final boss battle from Unconnected Marketeers. with Drake in place of Chimata. Drake appears on-screen with the animation usually used when a boss starts a spell card. The inventory displays three items in Passive Games, that being icons for Bubble Bobble, YouTube, and Frogger. No games are under the Active Game and Equipment Game slots. The heart icons used for Lives are replaced by Mii Brawler's stock icons from Super Smash Bros., and the icons next to Power and Funds have been replaced by the + and - buttons on a Wii remote, respectively. Reimu defeats Drake, capturing the final spell card, "Asylum of Danmaku". After being defeated, Drake says "Damn girl, you know how to move! You're free to browse my wares!". Reimu responds with "黙れ悪魔! アンタを倒して幻想郷を元に戻す!" ("Shut up, devil! I'll defeat you, and restore Gensokyo!"), which Drake responds with "Uh... yeah girl, you too."  The market opens, and Reimu buys Mart Racer with the remaining 850 funds. Also visible is a card displaying a cell phone, likely referencing Hotline Bling.    13:52  Outro  A splash card featuring all of the many shopkeepers is displayed before the music stops. "The period of use for this channel has ended." and "Press the A Button." flash on the screen, referencing the Wii Shop's closure.   Details[] In TONY'S SHOP, Tony's selling a Sonic CD. This is a reference to Sonic CD. There's also an Omochao graffiti on the wall. In Shop, the paper that covers the screen for the transition has Eggman's speech from SnapCube's fandub of Sonic Adventure 2 written on it. In Buy Mode, the loading bar says "Consuming the Soy", a reference to "OMORIBOY the SEXY!!! 🔥🔥🔥" by RainingKetchup. In Shop Menu (FNF Lullaby), pictures of Gold and Shinto are on the walls. In Lantern, the player's inventory can be seen, mirroring every item bought before then. In Sex Sells, the L and R buttons showcase the previous character, Harmony (or Paruko), and the upcoming character, Prince Fleaswallow. There's also a bookshelf behind the text, with each book featuring SiIvaGunner-related jokes[2]: "THE NUTSHACK EXPLAINED", with a picture of Tito Dick on the back cover "ART OF YANKIN, ACT 1", with a picture of Lady on the back cover "HOBaRT - OPERATION MANUAL", with a picture of HOBaRT on the back cover "TOP 50 REASONS YOUR RIP GOT REJECTED", with a picture of SiIvaGunner on the back cover "The SilvaGunner Christmas Comeback Crisis: Episode 11" "EXTREMELY LOUD SEX GUIDE", with a picture of Loud Nigra on the back cover "7" "SEX 2" "UNLISTED AMONG US RIPS", with a picture of the "Among Drip" render on the back cover In Prince Fleaswallow's Rap, the various item descriptions are lyrics from his level in PaRappa the Rapper. The items he sells are also items featured in his stage, save the Daisy Cake, which is an item bought by PaRappa during the original game's plot. In Goronu, Morshu calls the currency rubies while Parappa calls them rupees. This is a nod to the CD-i Zelda titles mistakenly calling rupees "rubies". In Crazy Dave (Intro Theme), Boyfriend and Whitty from Friday Night Funkin' can be seen for a few frames. In The Trapper, several knick-knacks can be seen relating to previous shopkeepers, like a Rupee, a Seam plushie, a Jerma logo box (likely Grotto Beasts), and a Zacharie mask. In Disco Descent (1-1 with Shopkeeper), the shopkeep doesn't actually appear but is instead Leshy role playing as him like he does in Inscryption. This makes Leshy the only shopkeeper to sell items to the player more than once. In Where is That Bustling Marketplace Now ~ Immemorial Marketeers, several pieces of Touhou-related memorabilia can be seen in the background. In the display case behind Chimata, there are four orbs resembling Aya Shameimaru, Satori Komeiji, Fujiwara no Mokou, and Kogasa Tatara. On the shelf on the right side of the screen, from left to right are displayed the Ibuki Gourd, a small and pixelated Suika Ibuki figurine, a small Youmu Konpaku figurine, a Nazrin fumo, a Patchouli Knowledge figurine, and a Ran Yakumo figurine. On the bulletin board underneath the shelf, several more pins are displayed: Three of Cirno's icicles Yukari Yakumo's gap portal, with ribbons tying off the ends Reimu Hakurei's Yin-Yang Orb Suwako Moriya's hat A yellow star, likely representing Marisa Kirisame A magnifying glass A red crescent, a green shooting star, and a blue 8-pointed star Keychains of the Power and Point items One of Sakuya Izayoi's throwing knives Reimu's ofuda Sanae Kochiya's frog hair pin The four playable characters of Unconnected Marketeers (Reimu, Marisa, Sakuya, and Sanae) can also be seen on the bottom of the screen. In Wii Shop Bling, the lives are Mii Brawler's stock icon in Smash Bros. Drake's text at the very end, "Uh, yeah girl, you too." Is a reference to the Drake song Girls Want Girls, the lyric "Say that you a lesbian, girl me too." The artwork shown at the end includes Spamton from Deltarune, the Weapons Merchant from Resident Evil 4, and HH from hhgregg, despite them not appearing in the collab. The currency is consistent throughout the entire video. Exactly 20,000 in different currencies is spent.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Nowhere_to_Run_(Remastered)_-_Freddy_Fazbear's_Pizzeria_Simulator;;;This serves as a remaster and extended version of the rip "Nowhere to Run - Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator". This is a spoof of the Completion Ending cutscene of Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator with several changes made related to The Stanley Parable much like the original rip, though this time playing the entire ending as well as containing parodies of the visuals. At the start, Scrap Baby is replaced with the Narrator's dialogue from the Mariella ending of The Stanley Parable. At 0:38, the advertised track begins playing, but instead of the Cassette Man's dialogue, the Narrator's dialogue from the Countdown ending plays, as the visuals fade into Stanley's computer monitor with the flashing ">■" is shown on the top left. Starting at 1:17, various images from The Stanley Parable appear at various points to go with the Narrator's dialogue, most of which are from various endings of the game:  At 1:17, the office with various characters added around, mainly ones of the Stanley model from The Stanley Parable. At 1:26, a frame from the opening cutscene of The Stanley Parable, as a countdown timer meant to replicate the one from the Countdown ending appears on the bottom right. At 1:35, the messed up meeting room from the Not Stanley ending as a red alarm appears on the monitor screen, meant to replicate the flames that begin to appear at the same time in the Completion Ending. At 1:39, the Boss's office fades over the computer monitor. At 1:45, the entrance to the "Mind Control Facility" also fades over. At 2:06, the visuals reverse to go with the Narrator adding more time to the countdown timer. At 2:31, one of the control panels in the "Mind Control Facility" is shown as the countdown timer fades in again. At 2:41, one of the fake exit doors, also from the "Mind Control Facility", as the red alarm fades in again. At 2:49, the abandoned office from the Games ending. At 2:54, the museum from the Museum ending. At 3:09, third person view of Stanley frozen in place from the Not Stanley ending. At 3:41, the outside world from the Freedom ending. Finally, at 3:58, the screen starts to distort as the Narrator's dialogue from the Countdown ending ends and cuts to a black screen.

This begins similarly to the remix "Biggest Fan (As Performed on American Idol)" with original lines portraying a contestant and a loved one of theirs before performing for the judges over "Main Theme" from American Idol (GBA).  At 0:30, the remix from "Biggest Fan (As Performed on American Idol)" begins playing, though this time the vocals are pitch-shifted in a manner to match the poor performance version of songs from American Idol (GBA). At 1:09, a drum beat is added to the remix and some backing vocals play at several points. At 1:43, the remix ends, and much like in "Biggest Fan (As Performed on American Idol)", the judges give negative reactions to the performance, though this time the second judge's line at 1:51 is cut off by voice clips pitch-shifted to "Meet the Flintstones", a play on the use of the word "granddad".   Judge 1: I'll be honest, that was one of the most embarrassing performances I've ever seen. (Ohhhh!) Judge 2: My granddad could sings "Meet the Flintstones". Judge 3: This doesn't even deserve a full send back.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Slider_(Zesty_Mix)_-_Super_Mario_64;;;At the start, the opening of "Bumble Bee" by Bambee plays. The composer line is changed to reference "Top G", a term used to refer to Andrew Tate, referencing "Bumble Bee" being frequently used in TikTok videos about Andrew Tate. The word "zesty" (a slang word used to refer to flamboyantly gay men) in the mix name additionally references the "Bottom G / Gay Andrew Tate" trend.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Challenge_Failed_-_BitLife;;;There is no actual track in BitLife titled "Challenge Failed". Instead, this is a tongue-in-cheek video "complaining" about the current state of the channel, singling out the heavy amount of "Raft Ride" rips, rips featuring "Bumble Bee", and the fakeout of The Nutshack event on May 31 instead being the Saidai Seichi Challenge. "Diary" from Metal Wolf Chaos XD plays throughout. After this, the person receives a message from Patty Martin about playing 8Ball, before Patty barges into the room and shoots the person.  Various images, most of which are stock images, appear throughout, which go along with what the person in the rip is speaking of:  At 0:10, a fake Super Smash Bros. Ultimate character thumbnail for Patty Martin appears. At 0:16, the 6 PM PDT banner art for the event Dick's Retribution is shown. At 0:21, a scroll down of various rips that featured "Saidai Seichi Carnival" is shown. At 0:38, a stock image of a phone is shown with the following crudely drawn over it: A time of "5:40 PM". A drawing of The Voice Inside Your Head. Three fake notifications: Message app from "Patty" reading "Let's play 8ball!" BeReal app with the text "It is time to Be Real" A YouTube notification reading "Someone liked ur comment! "harlem shakeover is better" At 0:44, the "porn.png" image from the album GilvaSunner's Highest Quality Video Game Rips Volume 5 (Beta Mix) appears with the annotation text changed to "Cant post rips you perverted dip shit" and a hand holding a gun placed over Patty's hand. After this, it fades to an edit of the "Take the Dirty Bubble Challenge" flyer from the SpongeBob SquarePants episode "Have You Seen This Snail?", with the following changes: The top changed to read "Take the Saidai Seichi Challenge!". The image of the dirty bubble was replaced by the cover art for "Saidai Seichi Carnival". The "Hit the Paddle Ball" text was replaced with "May 31 is National Flip-Flop Day!" The bottom text is replaced with "endure this song for the next remaining 6 hours of your life", with the "6" being crossed out with "7", with it crossed out with "8". A signature on the bottom is added reading "From your friends, Patricia "Patty" Martin & Tito "Dickman" Dick. The caption "And that's on gang..." appears over the edit, referencing the video "RIP Steve Harvey" by RIP Steve Harvey, as the losing horn from The Price is Right plays, edited to have the melody of "Saidai Seichi Carnival".  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Upside_Down_-_Curious_George:_The_Video_Game;;;"Upside Down" is not a track in Curious George: The Video Game; the track comes from the 2006 movie that the game is based on. This is a cover of the advertised track with spoof lyrics. The lyrics largely reference the Lucky Star character Patty Martin and, in particular, her character song "Saidai Seichi Carnival", with many direct quotations from the song in both English and Japanese. The lyrics also reference the channel in general, the Saidai Seichi Challenge taking place on National Flip Flop Day, and the main catchphrase used during the event. In addition, the advertised track's instrumental is mashed up with "Saidai Seichi Carnival"'s instrumental. The rip comes with closed captions, which are in a font and color referencing the Curious George logo. The lyrics are also transcribed in the rip's Bandcamp track page.  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/A_Feeling_Of_Power_(Blue_Lagoon)_(Alternate_Mix)_-_Heavy_Rain;;;Like all rips of this track, this rip references "im here to see doom". In this case, an inverse of said video is presented: audio from the relevant Heavy Rain scene is spliced in, while the main background music is "Rapp Snitch Knishes" by MF DOOM ft. Mr. Fantastik. Also featured is "EARLWOLF EUROPE SUMMER TOUR 2013", a compilation of footage of Earl Sweatshirt and Tyler the Creator on their 2013 Europe Summer tour as EarlWolf, including their meeting MF DOOM. The rip begins with a clip from "EARLWOLF EUROPE SUMMER TOUR 2013" of Jasper Dolphin shaking hands with MF DOOM set to the advertised track, both of which are edited to imitate the beginning of "im here to see doom". Footage from "EARLWOLF EUROPE SUMMER TOUR 2013" then plays set to "Rapp Snitch Knishes", the song featured in "im here to see doom". Clips from the video are spliced together to say "I'm tryna see--", followed by a clip of the Heavy Rain character Norman Jayden saying his name repeatedly playing in the same manner as the "MF DOOM"s in "im here to see doom", accompanied by various clips from "EARLWOLF EUROPE SUMMER TOUR 2013". The clip with music from the beginning of the rip is then edited to imitate the ending of "im here to see doom". After a brief cut to black, a clip from "EARLWOLF EUROPE SUMMER TOUR 2013" plays of Jasper Dolphin saying "--chillin', man, bout to go, uh, see this nigga DOOM here tonight", with "DOOM" replaced with a clip of Norman Jayden saying "Paco" from the Heavy Rain cutscene used in "im here to see doom".

Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog, "Boogey-Mania"  After the track ends, a clip from the pilot for Yo Gabba Gabba! plays, referencing the popular use of the "Biz's Beat of the Day" segment from the pilot as a YTPMV source. However, "My name is--" is cut off by "--Mama Luigi to you, Mario!" from the Super Mario World episode "Mama Luigi". Luigi's wheeze from "Mama Luigi" is then pitch-shifted to "ryukenden (Shuric Scan 1.99crk)" by SofT MANiAC, a song notorious for being used in low quality .veg replace YTPMVs. At 1:02, Morshu saying "Bombs" from Link: The Faces of Evil is also pitch-shifted to "Shuric Scan 1.99crk" right before the rip abruptly ends.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/16_Melodies_(Beginning)_-_MOTHER_3;;;This is an arrangement of "Let It Grow" from The Lorax using the instruments of the advertised track with different instruments used for the various different people featured in "Let It Grow".  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Johnny_C._Bad_(Extended)_-_Final_Fantasy_VI;;;At the start, several sound effects from the Final Fantasy VI play, while in sync, the thumbnail flashes white, turns fainter, shakes while turning red, and fades to white. At 0:09, Kefka's laugh plays, followed by the "Wipeout!" line from the opening of "Wipeout" by The Surfaris, playing off the laugh at the beginning of "Wipeout". At 0:14, the rip becomes a medley rip of various songs in the instruments and style of the advertised track, with a theme of 50s/60s rock songs and tracks inspired by 50s/60s rock. The thumbnail also reappears, but with each joke, the text in the logo changes to the name of the source of the respective joke (a reverse of what is sometimes done for fusion collabs). At 7:27, the logo briefly changes to read "FAMILY GUY"/"FUNNY MOMENTS" at the point corresponding to the "Woo!" in "Tutti Frutti".  https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Credits_-_Densha_de_GO!!;;;No elements of the advertised track appear in this rip. Instead, it's a mashup of the theme song of Densha de GO!! and "Snow halation". The rip has the standard format for character-dedicated "Snow halation" rips: μ's' stage panning down with animated snow as the featured character, in this case Futaba, the mascot of Densha de GO!!, appears on the right. At the beginning of the rip, the announcement "まもなく、4番線に上野池袋方面行きが参ります。危ないですから、黄色い線までお下がりください。" (Shortly, the train bound for Ueno and Ikebukuro will arrive on platform 4. For your safety, please stand behind the yellow line.) As well as that, there is also a map of the Yamanote Line at the center of the screen, which goes through all of the stations of the map counter-clockwise starting from Tokyo Station (JY01) and ending at Yurakucho. Right as the chorus is about to start, the text "ミッションクリア！" (Mission Clear!) appears, which spin and transition to the stage's lights turn yellow with a flash to white. Afterwards, Futaba and the map are replaced with a chibi version of Futaba and promotional art of an E235 series train, both from Densha de GO!! Hashirō Yamanote-sen. At the rip's end, the stage pans up, followed by a fade to black, as the on-board announcement "ドアが閉まります。ご注意ください。" (The doors are closing. Please be careful.) plays, followed by the warning chimes of the doors closing.  A frame from the rip, showing Futaba and the Yamanote Line.Another frame from the rip, with "Mission Clear!" overlaid onto the visuals.Yet another frame from the rip, with the yellow stage, chibi version of Futaba, and the E235 series train promotional art.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/When_I_Get_Mad_I_Dance_Like_This_(Extended_Version)_-_Deltarune;;;This initially starts out as an arrangement of "Dancing Mad (Movement 1)" from Final Fantasy VI in the style and instruments of the advertised track, as a pun on the advertised track's name "When I Get Mad I Dance Like This". However starting at 0:38, the arrangement begins to loop the 0:29 to 0:38 section of the arrangement, with it increasing in pitch until it fades out. After this is a lengthy silence, timed such that the video length gives a false impression of a full "Dancing Mad" arrangement. Finally, at 17:16, the rip becomes a mashup of Deltarune's "When I Get Happy I Dance Like This" with The Nutshack theme.

Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   The advertised track's click plays repeatedly as "From the Window" by C418 fades in, with the clicks synced to its tempo. The clicks fade out and sounds of basketball dribbling start fading in at 0:30, also synced to the tempo, which then escalate into full audio of a basketball game at 1:04 and an announcer says "And we are underway from Oakland, Barkley." The rip then becomes a mashup of various sources, most prominently "Space Jam", with C418's "From the Window", "Along the Busiest of Roads", and "Welcome Back to the Machine". The songs are played back-to-back, with "Along the Busiest of Roads" starting at 6:58 and "Welcome Back to the Machine" starting at 12:13. Other audio clips of basketball game announcers relating to Charles Barkley are interspersed throughout the rip. From 6:03 to 7:03 and 10:30 to 10:59, "Space Jam"'s vocals are arranged and pitch-shifted to the melody. Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This is a YTPMV mostly centered around the advertised track and sketches from The Eric Andre Show, mainly the original "Bird Up!" sketch. Various other jokes are interspersed throughout:  At the start, the rip plays the "I have a secret" scene from season 2, episode 6 of The Eric Andre Show. When the eyes appear, Mario's mustache and Cappy from Super Mario Odyssey slide down onto Eric Andre as the text "maric andrio???" appears in the bottom right corner. At 0:16, "Super Mario Smoking Weed The Movie" by من قبل عن طريق appears inside the greenscreen outfit. At 0:24, the bird on Eric Andre's shoulder bobs to the music in the bottom left corner and is edited to have accordion-playing hands (edited from the popular YTPMV source "Rude Ass Ray") and floating musical notes, accompanying the "Bird Up!" bird sound being pitch-shifted to the accordion in the advertised track. As well as that, gameplay of "Ricco Harbor" and a "Secret Course" level appears inside the greenscreen outfit. At 0:42, the visuals transition to incorporating elements from The Eric Andre Show (mainly Henry Rollins' appearance in season 2 episode 9 of The Eric Andre Show) into Delfino Plaza with the Super Mario Sunshine HUD. Mario's head on the lives counter is replaced with Eric Andre, Gerald is recolored and edited to appear as three Piantas, Questlove is seated behind three watermelon blocks, the Bowser television is on Andre's desk and briefly shows a clip of Henry Rollins stand-up show in 2001, and then this video of a chicken walking upright at 0:50, and the segment's "lyrics" are transcribed with captions based on text in the advertised game. At 1:10, the visuals transition into this video (original video with sound not found), while another clip from Henry Rollins' stand-up show plays. At 1:11, the rip transitions to the "Snail Down!" sketch from season 3, episode 10 of The Eric Andre Show, which is quickly interrupted by the "FUCK YOU" from "HOTEL MARIO YOUTUBE POOP" by BigBowsaALT and unknown images of a recursive Circle Game character and a frustrated person. An unknown video briefly appears in the background, and the "Snail Down" footage oscillates wildly as explosions appear and crashing sounds play. At 1:15, the "basketball twerk" video zooms in as "Monster Mash Dance Potion" from ROBLOX plays.

At 1:43 and 2:15, Chaze's cough is heavily reverbed. At 5:57, his cough is heavily distorted. At 6:16 and 6:22, sections from the "Weird Al" Yankovic interview with Madonna play, with "Weird Al" Yankovic saying "What are you looking at, there's nothing up there!" and "Ok, ok, shut up" in response to Chaze's actions. The ending video concludes at 6:26 and the rest of the "Circus" rip plays.  
    https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/The_key_we've_lost_(Beta_Mix)_(with_lyrics)_-_Xenoblade_Chronicles_X_OST;;;The Joke-Explainer™ 7000 needs your help!  This joke list is incomplete! Please listen to the rip and help fill out these pesky missing spaces.   This is a parody of the rip "The key we've lost (with lyrics) - Xenoblade Chronicles X OST". The rip begins with audio from "Purple Grape Soda" by roachmg777, as an iMovie caption reading "Purple Grape Soda" in the style used by "Purple Grape Soda" (which the original rip also uses) appears. The rip then becomes a mashup of "Purple Grape Soda" (as well as "Court Date" by DJ Hotday, the song used for its instrumental) with the advertised track, as footage from "Purple Grape Soda" is displayed onscreen. The footage is accompanied by iMovie captions transcribing the lyrics, which progressively have the letters more spread out with each slide, as well as another set of captions heckling other elements of the rip. At 0:22, "Meet the Flintstones" is added to the advertised track's melody, referencing the original rip. At 1:12, over the lead-up to the drop, the video "haha chocolate milk" plays, crudely edited to be partially purple. The rip then becomes a grape soda-themed spoof cover of the advertised track's chorus, with its own set of iMovie captions, accompanied by various videos and images related to the lyrics:    Time  Visual   1:14  "Firing a 2 inch Gun at 12,500fps" by The Slow Mo Guys   1:17  a gif of purple bubbles   1:19  "Foam Adventure" by CanineHybrid   1:22  a gif of a grape Fanta levitating in a box   1:24  The Boyboy West Coast's Instagram release of "U Was At The Club (Bottoms Up)"   1:28  a gif of a fizzy glass of Coke   1:31  ???   1:33  a still of "GRAPES" from "(Alternate) Dynasty TV Intro" by Fatal Farm   1:38  a still of NUMP from The Nutshack   1:44  footage from "Purple Grape Soda"   1:49  a stock photo of a vineyard  At 1:53, a clip of the "Obamna/SODA!" video plays, transitioning into a frame from "Purple Grape Soda" with Impact text reading "GET TROLLED" as the stock scream used in "dog dancing we no speak americano" by LegoMaster121000 is pitch-shifted to the advertised track's vocal melody. The rip then transitions to camera footage of the ripper holding a can of soda and viewing the results on SiIvaGunner's "channel content" page for videos with "beta mix" in the title, referencing the mix name's use during the April Fools' Day 2023 event. The person says "Sounds like me watching this fucking channel.", drinks some soda, and burps. At 2:04, the "Purple Grape Soda" mashup and footage resume, as the melody of The Nutshack theme is added to the advertised track.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Ruby_Illusions_-_Final_Boss_(In-Game_Version)_(Beta_Mix)_-_Sonic_Mania;;;The rip begins as a mashup of "Ruby Illusions - Final Boss (In-Game Version) - Sonic Mania" and "Ruby Illusions - Final Boss - Sonic Mania Plus". At the beginning, the screaming hamster visual from the former rip appears over the Sonic Mania Plus thumbnail seen in the latter rip. At 0:05, the visual fades to black, leading into an edited version of the "CHOMIK MANIA" visual seen in "Ruby Illusions - Final Boss (In-Game Version)" with the following changes:  "MANIA" is crudely replaced with "(BETA MIX)", referencing the use of said mix name during the April Fools' Day 2023 event. The rows of hamsters are replaced with references to various rips uploaded during the April Fools' Day 2023 event: the album cover for Osamu Sato's Equal ("Equalize (Beta Mix) - Equal"), James Grime from the thumbnail for the Numberphile video "e (Euler's Number)" ("Main Theme (Beta Mix) - e"), an image from the Markiplier video "Markiplier in the Hospital" ("O (Beta Mix)"), and footage from "...of 2017 (Beta Mix)". The background is replaced with the Sonic Mania Plus thumbnail, which has a rainbow filter and continuously scrolls vertically in the background. In addition to all this, the "Meet the Flintstones" title sequence to The Flintstones and the rip "SFX: Waddle Dee! - Kirby's Avalanche" are pitch-shifted to the track and superimposed over the other visuals. At 0:20, the Flintstones and "SFX: Waddle Dee!" clips end with a flash of white. "SiIva Direct Mini Quarantine 2020 (Beta Mix)" then fades in and is edited and mashed up with the track in the same manner as the "vxcv" clip in "Ruby Illusions - Final Boss (In-Game Version)". From 0:27 to 0:41, "A Video Based On Your Defeat" and "...of 2017 (Beta Mix)" are pitch-shifted to the track and superimposed over the other visuals. At 0:41, elements from "Rave Thing" by Excision (referencing "Rave Thing (Beta Mix) - Excision's Heckin' Epic Safari") are arranged to "Ruby Illusions - Final Boss - Sonic Mania", as the Excision's Heckin' Epic Safari thumbnail zooms in and out over footage from "Ruby Illusions - Final Boss - Sonic Mania", which itself zooms in and out in sync with the music. In addition, the visualizer and copyright disclaimer from the official Pokémon "A Few Musical Notes from Game Developer Toby Fox" video are displayed onscreen in reference to "A Few Musical Notes from Game Developer Toby Fox (Beta Mix) | #PokemonSwordShield", with the visualizer matching the rip's music. At 1:01, "Ruby Illusions - Final Boss (In-Game Version) - Sonic Mania" is both mashed up with and superimposed over "Ruby Illusions - Final Boss - Sonic Mania", accompanied by the scrolling Sonic Mania Plus thumbnail. In addition, the "(BETA MIX)" text is displayed sideways on the left-hand side of the video and flips vertically in sync with a voice saying "BETA MIX" being pitch-shifted to the track, and "VID_20191028_202432 (Beta Mix)" and "Welcome to SiIvaGunner! (Beta Mix)" play while being superimposed over the other visuals. At 1:07, an Opila Bird jumpscare from Garten of Banban plays in sync with a "Rave Thing" sample, in reference to the long series of Garten of Banban rips during the April Fools' Day 2023 event, with the visuals heavily saturated, shaking, and zooming in. In addition, the thumbnail uses the Plus version of the thumbnail despite being titled under the base game, referencing a mistake on the initial upload of the rip "Hi-Spec Robo Go! - Hard-Boiled Heavy Boss - Sonic Mania Plus" where the thumbnail was set to the original thumbnail before being fixed.

 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Strawberry_Shortcake_(Beta_Mix)_(Beta_Mix)_-_Kirby:_Squeak_Squad;;;At 0:02, the melody changes to "Sunshine Girls" from Strawberry Shortcake's Berry Bitty Adventures. At 1:04, the rip transitions to a fake King for Another Day Tournament trailer. The trailer uses a clip from the official WildBrain video "Strawberry Shortcake 🍓 SPECIAL 1 HOUR COMPILATION 🍓 Berry Bitty Adventures". At 1:46, SiIvaGunner "SG" logos replace the strawberries on the stamps. As the theme song for Strawberry Shortcake's Berry Bitty Adventures fades in, Clement Cricket's name is crudely replaced with a clip from Berry Bitty Adventures of Strawberry Shortcake's name, and the video rapidly zooms in on Strawberry's face. The "trailer" then "reveals" Strawberry as a contender, complete with a King for Another Day-style render of Strawberry running while holding a cake.       The render of Strawberry featured in the rip.   This rip references both "Strawberry Shortcake - Kirby: Squeak Squad" and the fan ripper Prabowo Muhammad, who gained minor notoriety among the SiIvaGunner fan community for repeatedly suggesting Strawberry Shortcake's Berry Bitty Adventures characters as King for Another Day contestants on the SiIvaGunner Wiki.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Hopes_and_Dreams_(Beta_Mix)_(Beta_Mix)_-_Undertale;;;This is a parody of the rip "Hopes and Dreams - Undertale". At 0:11, a violin instrument plays "Meet the Flintstones", mimicking the violin playing "Snow halation" in the original rip. At 0:22, the advertised track is mashed up with the lyrics of the rip "Snow halation - Love Live!" instead of the original "Snow halation", and a chiptune instrument plays the melody of that rip, which is "Meet the Flintstones" in the chorus, but the same as "Snow halation" in the verses.     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Last_Goodbye_(Alternate_Mix)_(Beta_Mix)_-_Undertale;;;This starts exactly like the rip "Last Goodbye (Alternate Mix) - Undertale", but at 0:05, the advertised track is mashed up with rip "Title Theme & Ending - The Flintstones: The Rescue of Dino & Hoppy".     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/HYPER_ULTRA_-CLIMAX-_TRIAL_(Beta_Mix)_-_SilvaGunner:_King_for_Another_Day;;;Starting at 0:09 the advertised track is mashed up with "Deez Nuts! [Trap Remix]" by Dennibro, with elements of the advertised track changed to accompany the song. At 1:25, the melody changes to "Once Upon a Time" from Undertale. At 2:15, elements from "S.L.A.B. Freestyle" and "Yankin" are added to the instrumental. At 2:31, the instruments from "Among Us Trap Remix" are added to the track. Finally, at 3:37, the melody changes to "Meet the Flintstones". Additionally, most characters' voicelines used in the advertised track are replaced by memes. "Gentleman" is sampled at 1:00 and 2:59,  "S.L.A.B. Freestyle" is sampled at 1:03, 2:15, and 3:02, "Yankin" is sampled at 1:07 and 3:05, Vinesauce Joel's reaction to 7 GRAND DAD is sampled at 1:10 and 3:09, "STOP POSTING ABOUT AMONG US" by biggayrapper is sampled at 2:35 and 3:11, and LowTierGod's "You should kill yourself now" speech is sampled at 2:39 and 3:15.     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Smile_Song_(Beta_Mix)_(Beta_Mix)_-_My_Little_Pony:_Friendship_Is_Magic;;;Much like "Smile Song (Beta Mix) - My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic", this plays the The Cleveland Show theme, with the bass played by the synth from "Pony" by Ginuwine from 0:00 to 0:01. However, the vocals are replaced with those from various PSY songs, which are pitch-shifted to match: "Daddy" at 0:01, "That That" at 0:11, "Gangnam Style" at 0:19, and "Gentleman" at 0:23. From 0:12 to 0:19, the opening saxophone from "New Face" by PSY doubles the bass line of the The Cleveland Show theme.     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Final_Boss_(Beta_Mix)_-_iCarly_(DS);;;This uses the rip "Final Boss - iCarly (DS)", a final boss styled arrangement of "Leave It All to Me" by Michael Corcoran. In this rip, "Bangarang" is mashed up with and pitch-shifted to the aforementioned rip, before switching to "Kill EVERYBODY" by Skrillex at 0:23.     
https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Woodyana_Stones:_Raider_Made_of_Lost_Bark_(Beta_Mix);;;No joke found.
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/My_Last_Message_(Beta_Mix);;;The rip plays the "My Last Message" video in its entirety, but with various TikTok "attention bait" gameplay videos overlaid on top of it. Over time, more videos are added onto the screen, so as to completely obscure the original video. The video begins with gameplay footage of Sandwich Runner playing on the bottom left corner of the screen, and Going Balls playing on the bottom right corner. At 3:55, gameplay footage of the ROBLOX game Tower of Hell is added between the Sandwich Runner and Going Balls footage. At 6:31, footage from Subway Surfers is added to the top of the screen. At 8:17, footage from the Family Guy episode "Patriot Games" is added to the top left corner of the screen. At 11:00, footage from Crossy Road is added to the right of the Subway Surfers footage. Finally, at 11:58, the Jeff the Killer image is added to the top right corner of the screen, completely covering the original video.  
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Gravity_(Alpha_Mix)_(Beta_Mix)_-_Cave_Story;;;This rip starts off the same way as the rip "Gravity (Alpha Mix) - Cave Story", being an arrangement of "YO-KAI Disco (Hell's Entrance World)" using the advertised track's instruments. However, starting from 0:08, the rip instead becomes an arrangement of "Disco Necropolis (Graveyard Stage)" from Skeleton Boomerang. This references the rip "Disco Necropolis (Graveyard Stage) (Alpha Mix) - Skeleton Boomerang", which is an arrangement of the Mamorukun Curse! tracks "YO-KAI Disco (Hell's Entrance World)" and "Karakuri Spirits (Trap Castle World)" in the style of "Disco Necropolis (Graveyard Stage)".     
 https://siivagunner.fandom.com/wiki/Point_of_Entry_(Beta_Mix)_-_Contra_III:_The_Alien_Wars;;;Clips of Sneako from this video are pitch-shifted and mashed up with the advertised track. This is a reference to "Point of Entry - Contra III: The Alien Wars (SNES)", which uses a similar joke in a related fashion. Additionally, the rip's title omits "(SNES)" from the game's title. This quirk originates from the original rip prior from it being renamed.
